title: fs.compound(search) silently ignores regex:true and matches literally, returning false-negative 0 hits
description:
zero.fs.compound('search', {..., regex:true}) silently ignores the regex flag and matches the query literally, returning 0 hits for valid patterns.

Verified at HEAD 355a7b7.

REPRO:
  await zero.fs.compound('search',{query:'PERMIT_POLL|COOLDOWN',
     path:'crates/zerostack-machine-permit/src', regex:true, max_results:5});
  => "search:0 hits (literal-only: query contains regex metacharacter(s) | and was
      matched literally, not as a regex; ...)"

  await zero.fs.compound('search',{query:'PERMIT_POLL.*Duration',
     path:'crates/zerostack-machine-permit/src', regex:true, max_results:5});
  => "search:0 hits (literal-only: ... metacharacter(s) * ... matched literally ...)"

  Control (no metacharacters):
  await zero.fs.compound('search',{query:'PERMIT_POLL', path:'...', max_results:5});
  => "search:14 hits"

Ground truth: both patterns DO match - crates/zerostack-machine-permit/src/lib.rs:19-20
define PERMIT_POLL and PERMIT_POLL_MAX as Duration constants, confirmed via grep.

The response text does warn "literal-only" and suggests fs.searchMany with regex:true,
which is good, BUT: the caller explicitly passed regex:true and it was accepted without
error and then dropped. An accepted-and-ignored parameter is worse than a rejected one -
callers get a confident "0 hits" that looks like proof of absence.

EXPECTATION: either honor regex:true in compound('search'), or hard-error with
"regex not supported here, use fs.searchMany" instead of silently degrading to literal.

Severity P2: not data-corrupting, but it produces false-negative searches, which can
lead an agent to wrongly conclude code does not exist.
notes:
FIXED. Commit pi-stack-main 8b66547fb913a1dad70bb591488ddaf2ca88cc12 "fix(zerostack): forward regex/path/max_results in compound('search')".

=== WHAT CHANGED (packages/pi-zerostack/router/lib/lowering.js) ===
Two sites, not one. The attempt-2 note named only the adapter shim; the live repro
(a single 'return await zero.fs.compound(...)' plan) actually takes the OTHER path.
1) directFsPlan() searchMatch fast path (~L595): regex-lowered plans rebuilt the call
   as fs.search({query}) only. Now, when the plan carries regex:true / path / paths /
   max_results / case, it lowers to fs.searchMany({queries:[{query,regex,paths,limit,case}]}).
   Unconstrained searches keep the cheaper single fs.search.
2) The inlined adapter shim zero.fs.compound 'search'|'grep'|'find' arm (L433-436):
   same forwarding at runtime from the args object.

Arg spelling verified against FSZero, NOT guessed:
  batch_ops.rs SearchRequest::parse:672-714 reads query / paths (string OR array) /
  limit / case / regex. So max_results -> limit, path -> paths:[...]. Confirmed
  fs.search itself cannot carry them: dispatcher.rs:307 declares
  "fs.search" => Some(('S', &["query","arg"], Some("query"))) — query/arg only.
  That is why option (a) (route to the searchMany kernel) is the only correct fix;
  passing path/max_results to fs.search as the drafted patch did would have been a
  second silent drop, one layer lower. Drafted patch amended accordingly.
No FSZero or ZeroStack source changed.

=== TESTS ===
New: packages/pi-zerostack/router/test/search-contract.test.mjs (5 tests), sitting
beside read-contract.test.mjs and citing the vzo/zez precedents as the same bug class.
Covers: regex lowers to searchMany; path+max_results emitted as paths/limit (and
max_results NOT emitted); case forwarded; unconstrained search still uses fs.search;
adapter shim builds the batch item.

MUTATION-VERIFIED: with the test in place, 'git checkout -- lowering.js' (fix reverted)
=> npm test: tests 96, pass 86, fail 4 — all 4 failures in search-contract.test.mjs
(lines 19, 26, 35, 47). Fix restored => tests 96, pass 90, fail 0. The 6 'cancelled'
entries are node --test harness teardown and are identical before and after the change.
Command: cd packages/pi-zerostack && npm test.

=== FOLLOW-UP BEAD WORTH FILING (noted, not built, per instruction) ===
Yes — file a shim arg-forwarding contract test. Three beads now (vzo, zez, 0wnl) are the
same defect: lowering.js rebuilds a call from scratch and silently drops any arg not
explicitly re-listed, and each was caught only by a human noticing a wrong result. The
guard should be generic rather than per-op: for every zero.fs.compound op, assert that
every argument key the caller passed either appears in the lowered plan, or is rejected
with a named error — never accepted-and-ignored. Note the extra hazard this fix
surfaced: forwarding is two-sided, an arg must also be spelled the way the engine ABI
actually accepts it (max_results vs limit), so the contract test should assert against
the FSZero op ABI, not just against non-disappearance. directFsPlan's regex-based
rewriting is the structural root and is worth revisiting in that bead.

Residual risk: directFsPlan matches args with regexes over plan text, so it reads only
quoted-literal path and numeric max_results; a computed expression (path: somevar) still
falls through to the unconstrained fs.search branch. Behavior is unchanged from before
for that shape, not a new regression, but it is not a complete fix for dynamic plans —
the adapter-shim path (site 2) handles those correctly at runtime.
close_reason: Fixed in pi-stack-main 8b66547: compound(search) now forwards regex/path/max_results/case to the fs.searchMany kernel (paths/limit spellings per FSZero batch_ops.rs:672-714). New router/test/search-contract.test.mjs, 5 tests; mutation-verified (revert => 4 fail, restore => npm test 96 tests / 90 pass / 0 fail).

title: conformance: bound McpClient stdout reads so timeout cannot hang
description:
Parent epic: zerostack-elc

Location: conformance/src/lib.rs McpClient::request (~1082-1110).

Problem: timeout is checked only between blocking read_line calls. If the child never writes a newline, the harness hangs past self.timeout.

Why it matters: conformance can hang agents/CI forever and never produce a fail verdict.

Suggested fix direction (not implemented in audit): non-blocking read, read with poll/select, or kill child when Instant budget expires before/while waiting.

Discovered by UBS multi-round residual audit 2026-07-27 (source-verified). Audit-only.
close_reason: McpClient now reads stdout on a dedicated thread and receives complete lines/errors through a channel bounded by one absolute request deadline. Timeout/disconnect/read failures terminate and reap the child. One narrow Spark filter passed 2 tests. [commit 7afd8c1080bd14a9d392d3d85b1a1e312b5381d0]

title: call-issues-0729: GraphZero fixes (durable aggregate refs, blast timeout propagation)
description: Items 2(gz),4 in zerostack-call-issues-2026-07-29.md
close_reason:
Fixed in GraphZero commit 9f2f3b7 (main).

ITEM 2 - durable aggregate refs. gz://node/<symbol> refs (minted by orient/snap/blast when an edge has no inline evidence span) only resolved for <hash>@B<start>-<end> ids and bare blob hashes; a bare symbol id fell through to the blob path and failed, so aggregate refs died with the minting session. crates/graphzero-store/src/store/expand.rs now routes bare non-hash node ids through resolve_symbol_node, which reads the durable locate index rebuilt from the published snapshot (survives process exit, works from any authorized root). ITEM 4 - blast timeout propagation. codemode wall budget defaulted to 1s, so graph.blast depth 3 died with deadline_exceeded. crates/graphzero-query/src/codemode/types.rs: default is now 30s via default_max_wall_ms(), overridable by hosts through GRAPHZERO_CODEMODE_MAX_WALL_MS; bindings.rs limit_constants() reports the effective budget instead of the compiled-in floor.

3. MUTATION VERIFIED both fixes. Removing the resolve_symbol_node dispatch from expand.rs -> both new store tests FAILED (test result: FAILED. 3 passed; 2 failed). Reverting MAX_WALL_MS to 1_000 -> wall_budget_inherits_host_deadline_and_otherwise_defaults_high FAILED. Both mutations reverted and re-confirmed green.
4. END-TO-END repro against release binary on the original /tmp/gzrepro fixture, separate CLI processes per ref (proves cross-call durability): graphzero expand gz://node/composeFooterLines -> rc 0 composeFooterLines; gz://node/outer -> rc 0 outer; gz://node/helper -> rc 0 helper; gz://node/definitelyNotAThing -> {"error":"node_symbol_not_found"} (typed miss, not a generic ref failure).

title: Rename or measure 18x claim artifacts (AR-007 adversarial-review)
description:
## Goal
Stop filenames/schema ids embedding `18x` without a measured ratio field in the claim payload.

## Why
Adversarial-review AR-007: `benchmarks/claims/tokenzero-live-9pb-18x-proof.json` and related `*18x*` artifacts use 18x in the name/schema while payload is boolean/smoke fields (status_bins_ok, wall_ms) with no measured speedup ratio.

## Risk
medium — readers treat filename as published performance claim

- Report: .prosecution/runs/ar-20260727T231345Z-full/ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_REPORT.md AR-007
- Files: benchmarks/claims/tokenzero-live-9pb-18x-proof.json, tokenzero-zerostack-meta-repo-18x-smoke.json

- [ ] Either rename claim files/schema to drop unmeasured 18x, OR add explicit measured ratio fields (baseline_ms, candidate_ms, ratio) with provenance


No full cargo tests. Do not invent fake ratio numbers.

title: Make CodeMode refs expandable across parent and subagent sessions
description: A worker-sol subagent returned Spark verification ref `tz://blob/bed78c60cf793c1f09d6d6be3bd28a69f3dd14596f39b7e7a1b7589d78af0654` from its `zero_execute` call. Expanding that exact ref in the orchestrating parent session failed `ref-not-found; tiers tried: explicit/env cache, current-root store, per-user ref-index` and stated `mint and expand must share --cache-path`. This violates the RACC durability contract and prevents the mandatory parent review-resume loop from inspecting child evidence. Child session: worker-sol run `8c43a83a`; parent session goal `59f77854-c598-442a-bd4f-577b68e0110c`.
design: Use one owner-authorized durable CAS/ref index across parent and all spawned subagent sessions, or transmit/register child refs into the parent registry on completion/tool results. Preserve root/store authorization without requiring callers to know a private cache path. The same `tz://`, `fz://`, or `gz://` ref must expand after child process exit, host restart, and in the parent/reviewer session.
acceptance_criteria: A child mints refs on every surface, exits, and parent plus a separate authorized reviewer expands them byte-exactly without re-execution or cache-path plumbing. Unauthorized roots remain typed failures. Conformance covers concurrent children, host restart, child crash, process exit, range fragments, ref-index rebuild, and store-root isolation. Tool cards never advertise a ref that the orchestrator cannot expand.
notes: Additional 2026-07-31 parent-session reproduction: one `zero_execute` in `/Users/aditya/AI/TokenZero` returned `tz://blob/51e67d5601388773db4ebe1319fb1854c5312f1f6b3895fabe638e2710241ab5`; the immediately following `zero_execute` in the same orchestrator session/root failed expansion with `ref-not-found` and `mint and expand must share --cache-path`, naming recovery cache `/var/folders/.../pi-zerostack-sessions/2670-db1d0d2e38187e3c/6316db134dbfb947e9e6/tokenzero/recovery-cache.json`. Scope is therefore broader than child-to-parent: refs can fail across consecutive calls in one parent session.

title: Enforce output budgets on aggregate CodeMode results
description: P0 model-visible compaction bypass found while attributing `/Users/aditya/Downloads/Screenshot 2026-07-31 at 12.43.23 AM.jpg`. In wave-parent session `/Users/aditya/.pi/agent/sessions/--Users-aditya-AI-ZeroStack--/2026-07-31T04-34-28-719Z_019fb673-c6ef-7d66-8ebe-c099615eaecc.jsonl`, the exact plan `const [contract, env] = await Promise.all([zero.fs.compound('read',{path:'Downloads/zerostack-goal-7-30.md'}), zero.token.shell("env | grep '^PI_' | sort")]); return {contract,env};` produced a 40,034-character tool result beginning `Script completed{"contract":{"ack":"R3"..."payload":[47,103,111,...]`. It serialized file bytes as decimal integers, bypassed the normal compact result card, and had no `actions`, `visible_tokens`, `estimated_raw_visible`, savings receipt, or telemetry. The goal session accumulated 171,587 characters of tool results before its Luna wave; its explicit fork policy then copied that waste to eight children. A separate full-ref expansion also returned an 18,216-character unbudgeted `Script completed[...]` envelope. Result normalization/output budgeting must apply to arbitrary returned JS values and every completion branch, not only recognized connector envelopes.
design: Create one mandatory result-finalization sink at the canonical aggregate runtime boundary; every returned JavaScript value and every success/error/cancel/yield branch passes through it exactly once before any adapter sees bytes. Normalize recursively with cycle/depth/width/byte limits, batch encoding/writes, and no redundant deep clone. Borrow the proven shape of Senpi's bounded streaming output: fixed head/tail/status budgets and one overflow handle, but replace its absolute spill files with durable authorized CAS refs and RACC certificates. Finalization records exact raw/visible/ref bytes and telemetry. Adapters may render the finalized envelope but may not compact again or bypass it. Inject oversized arrays, decimal byte arrays, nested connector envelopes, and unrecognized return shapes at this boundary.
acceptance_criteria: The exact reproduction plan returns a normal slim envelope with <=2,000 visible tokens, complete measured telemetry, and an exact durable ref; no decimal byte array and no unframed `Script completed` text appears. Property/fuzz tests cover large nested strings, byte arrays, arrays of expanded refs, cycles, depth/width limits, mixed connector results, and outputs near/over max_output_bytes. Every returned byte is classified as inline visible, certified omitted behind a ref, or typed failure; visible/raw/savings receipts match the actual model-facing serialization. Standalone zs, aggregate raw-worker v2, pi-zerostack, cancellation, crash, and oversize paths are byte/semantics conformant. A regression proves a broad parent plan cannot inject >configured visible budget into later context while exact expansion remains one explicit call.

The copied child session preserves the result at `/Users/aditya/.pi/agent/sessions/--Users-aditya-AI-ZeroStack--/2026-07-31T04-41-52-416Z_019fb67a-8c20-7a28-9744-c9128d1617fb.jsonl`. First six child tool outputs in the screenshot lane totaled only 2,589 characters, so the 141k jump itself was fork/cache amplification; this bead owns the upstream ZeroStack output-budget escape that enlarged the fork source.

title: CAS size-policy divergence: TokenZero and FSZero publish objects the hub and GraphZero refuse to read
description:
The hub and GraphZero cap objects at 256 MiB and return PolicyDenied above it (ZeroStack/crates/zero-store/src/cas.rs:17 and :156; GraphZero/crates/graphzero-store/src/store/shared_cas.rs:26 and :99). TokenZero and FSZero have no size policy in publish or resolve at all.

So TokenZero or FSZero can publish a >256 MiB object into a shared store root that a hub-based or GraphZero-based reader can never read: same digest, same path, hard PolicyDenied. Interop breaks asymmetrically and only for large payloads, which is exactly the case least likely to be covered by a test.

Fix: one policy constant in zero-store, enforced identically on publish and on read. Boundary vectors at 256 MiB minus 1, exactly 256 MiB, and plus 1 belong in the shared fixture so all three engines are pinned to the same answer.

Note the related asymmetry in hash validation: hub and TokenZero and GraphZero build object paths by slicing hash[..2] without validating the input is hex first (hub cas.rs:128, TZ :219, GZ :76), so a short input panics; only FSZero validates and returns Malformed (src/core/cas.rs:140-143). Fix that in the same pass.

Part of zerostack-sce part A wave 1.
close_reason:
STALE - already fixed by cd59568. Verified against CURRENT code.

CLAIM (two parts): (1) hub and GraphZero cap CAS objects at 256 MiB and return PolicyDenied above it while TokenZero and FSZero have no size policy at all, so a large object published by one engine is permanently unreadable by another; boundary vectors at 256MiB-1 / exactly 256MiB / +1 should be pinned in a shared fixture. (2) hub, TokenZero and GraphZero build object paths via hash[..2] without validating hex first, so a short identity PANICS; only FSZero returned Malformed.

CURRENT STATE, part 1: crates/zero-store/src/cas.rs:18 CAS_MAX_OBJECT_BYTES = 256*1024*1024 is the single policy constant, and it is enforced on BOTH sides as the bead required -- publish via put/put_outcome/put_with_limit (cas.rs:181,197,257) and read via get_verified (cas.rs:464, 'object of {} bytes exceeds the CAS size policy'). Gates: cas.rs:866 size_policy_boundary_is_exact asserts limit-1 accepted, exactly-limit accepted, limit+1 refused with class 'policy_denied' -- all three boundary vectors named in the bead; cas.rs:888 size_policy_constant_is_256_mib pins the constant itself so an engine cannot silently retune it.

CURRENT STATE, part 2: object_path (cas.rs:164) uses sha256.get(..2).unwrap_or(sha256), NOT hash[..2], with a doc comment stating it is deliberately non-panicking so a malformed identity yields a nonexistent path rather than aborting the process. Every entry point validates first via is_full_lower_hex and returns CasError::Malformed('identity must be full lowercase 64-hex SHA-256, got ...') -- get_verified :451, touch :352, put_prehashed :206, sweep :428. So the hub now matches FSZero's Malformed behavior rather than the panicking behavior described. Gate: cas.rs:896 short_and_non_hex_identities_never_panic.

MUTATION-VERIFIED (this session): restoring the exact defect described in the bead -- replacing sha256.get(..2).unwrap_or(sha256) with &sha256[..2] at cas.rs:168 -- makes short_and_non_hex_identities_never_panic FAIL with 'end byte index 2 is out of bounds for string of length 0', panicked at cas.rs:168:26. That is the bead's reported panic reproduced verbatim, proving the guard is load-bearing and the test is not vacuous. Restored; cas.rs is byte-identical to HEAD.

COMMANDS: RCH_COMPRESSION_LEVEL=0 RCH_FORCE_REMOTE=1 rch exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/Users/aditya/rch_target_zs_shared cargo test -p zero-store -> 49 passed; 0 failed. Targeted run of the 5 gate tests: 5 passed.

NOT CLOSED BY THIS: per-engine adoption of zero-store (zerostack-ee2/sce) is still open, so FSZero and TokenZero private CAS copies retain their own policy until they cut over.

title: pi-zerostack extension has no git repo, so extension fixes cannot be committed, reviewed, or shipped
description:
The origin/main backend mechanism exists so that pushing to origin/main rebuilds the live pi-zerostack binaries. The extension that implements it cannot itself be delivered that way, because <home>/Developer/pi-stack is not a git repository:

  cd ~/Developer/pi-stack && git rev-parse --show-toplevel
  fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git

There is no .git anywhere up the tree, and no remote.

Consequences:
1. My fix for zerostack-9jj is applied and fully tested on disk (router/lib/substrates.js plus two new tests in router/test/substrates.test.mjs, 162/162 passing), but it cannot be committed or pushed, so it is one stray file operation away from being lost. There is no history, no diff to review, and no way for another agent to see what changed or to revert it.
2. The same is true of every other change any session makes to pi-zerostack, including the je4 and spz render fixes that were verified through this extension.
3. Reviewing extension changes is impossible. I could not produce a diff for the 9jj fix even to describe it accurately; I had to keep a manual copy at /tmp/az/subs.fixed.js to restore after a RED/GREEN experiment. A tmp copy is the only backup that currently exists for anything here.

The package declares "private": true and version 0.1.2, and Pi loads it by path from ~/.pi/agent/settings.json:
  "../../Developer/pi-stack/packages/pi-zerostack"
so it is a live, load-bearing component with no version control at all.

Wanted, in order:
1. git init the pi-stack repo, or move packages/pi-zerostack under a repo that already exists, and commit the current state as a baseline BEFORE anyone else edits it.
2. Add a remote so extension fixes can be reviewed and rolled back like engine fixes.
3. Decide whether the live extension should be loaded from a checkout that refreshes, the same way the engine binaries do, so that the verify-live workflow covers the extension too and not only the three engines.

Until then, treat any pi-zerostack edit as unbacked: take a copy first. Note the irony that this is the same class of trap as zerostack-9jj itself, where the mechanism meant to keep the live surface current was silently not doing so.

Blocks delivery of the zerostack-9jj fix.
close_reason: All three asks resolved. (1) git init: pi-stack IS now a git repository at /Users/aditya/Developer/pi-stack with 7 commits; the premise that it had no repo is stale. My zerostack-j0j extension fix is committed there as f81ba36 rather than living only on disk. (2) Remote: added, per an explicit user decision to use a local bare remote rather than publishing a load-bearing local extension. ~/git/pi-stack.git created, 'git push -u origin HEAD' done, main tracks origin/main. Verified recoverable, not just configured: cloned the bare repo to a scratch dir and confirmed all 7 commits and the PROTECTED_PREFIXES change in packages/pi-zerostack/shared/paths.js are present. Extension changes now have history, diffs, review, and rollback. (3) Refreshing-checkout decision: NO, deliberately. Pi loads the extension by path from ~/.pi/agent/settings.json ('../../Developer/pi-stack/packages/pi-zerostack'), and that should stay. The origin/main rebuild mechanism exists because the engines are compiled Rust binaries whose build must be reproduced; the extension is plain JS with no build step, so a refreshing checkout would add a staleness and divergence failure mode while buying nothing. Editing the loaded tree directly is also what makes the verify-live workflow honest: a change is exercised by the running session immediately. The actual risk in this bead was loss of uncommitted work, and version control plus a remote is the correct fix for that, not indirection. Follow-up if ever wanted: a real off-machine remote, which is a hosting decision for the user.

title: Add native one-call URL fetch to aggregate CodeMode
description: Basic URL reading currently requires capability discovery and an external adapter. Exact 2026-07-31 reproduction: the active Pi tool set could not read `https://github.com/code-yeongyu/senpi`; `search_tools` first promoted Z.AI Zread MCP, which failed three calls with `repo not found`; a second discovery promoted `fetch_content`, which finally worked. Local `read` cannot accept URLs and CodeMode shell is intentionally forbidden from reaching remote hosts. Reading a user-supplied public link must be one native aggregate call, not MCP/plugin archaeology.
design: Add a policy-owned `zero.web.fetch(url, options?)` connector to the canonical aggregate `zero-codemode` host and `zsx`, available identically to pi-zerostack and every client adapter. It is not a new planner, MCP server, or shell escape. Implement bounded HTTP(S) retrieval in the shared Rust runtime: HTTPS by default, bounded redirects/time/DNS/TLS/body/decompression, content-type validation, ETag/Last-Modified cache, exact raw bytes in authorized CAS, and optional certified text/Markdown extraction. Block file/Unix/data schemes, credentials in URLs, loopback/private/link-local/metadata addresses, DNS rebinding, cross-policy redirects, and implicit secret/cookie forwarding. Route every result through the canonical output budget/ref/receipt finalizer. Expose one complete signature and intent-search entry so a pasted URL can be fetched in the same `zero_execute` plan as local analysis. Later adapters may alias existing `fetch_content` UX to this connector, but the runtime must not depend on any external MCP or Pi package.
acceptance_criteria: From a fresh session, one `zero_execute` call containing `zero.web.fetch('https://github.com/code-yeongyu/senpi')` returns bounded readable content plus an exact durable ref, without `search_tools`, MCP, provider web search, shell, Python, or plugin installation. The same plan can fetch pinned raw GitHub files and feed them to FS/graph/token analysis without a second model-visible call. Standalone `zsx`, pi-zerostack, Claude, Codex, ZCode, Kimi, Grok, and optional edge are byte/error/receipt conformant. Tests cover redirects, TLS failure, timeout/cancel, compression bombs, MIME/charset, binary content, ETag/304, offline mode, proxy policy, SSRF IPv4/IPv6/DNS rebinding, credential stripping, oversize output, and CAS expansion. Remote network time is reported separately; warmed cache-hit runtime overhead meets p50 <=1ms/p95 <=2ms and q6am resource/lifecycle gates. Disabled network policy fails once with typed remediation.
notes: Reproduction tool sequence: search_tools -> z_ai_zread promotion -> three `repo not found` failures -> search_tools -> fetch_content promotion -> success. This is exactly the model-visible round-trip waste ZeroStack exists to remove. Security-sensitive connector must remain aggregate-host-owned and approval/policy gated; raw workers stay planner-free and networkless.

title: br create has no --description-file or stdin input; long evidence must go through argv
description:
Found while filing beads on 2026-07-25. Minor but it will bite scripted/agent use.

br create ADVERTISES FLAGS ITS USAGE LINE REJECTS
  br create "title" -t bug -p 1 --description-file /tmp/d.txt
fails with exit 2 and
  Usage: br create --type <TYPE> --priority <PRIORITY> --description <DESCRIPTION> <TITLE>
So --description-file is not accepted, and the usage line implies --description is REQUIRED and positional-title-last. The workaround is
  br create "title" -t bug -p 1 -d "$(cat /tmp/d.txt)"
which works, but shoving a multi-KB description through argv is exactly what a --description-file flag exists to avoid, and it is fragile: the body must survive shell quoting, and long descriptions risk ARG_MAX.

Two things worth fixing:
1. Support reading the description from a file or from stdin (-d - is the conventional spelling). Bead descriptions here are routinely long-form evidence with embedded quotes, backslashes, and JSON, which is the worst case for argv passing.
2. If --description-file is genuinely unsupported, the error should say "unknown flag --description-file" rather than printing a usage line, since the current message reads as though the ARGUMENTS were wrong rather than the FLAG being unrecognized. I initially reread my quoting before realizing the flag simply does not exist.

Low priority, but agents writing detailed beads hit this immediately, and the failure mode teaches the wrong lesson about what went wrong.
close_reason: Upstream, not fixable in these repos: br is a prebuilt binary from github.com/Dicklesworthstone/beads_rust with no local source. Re-tested against 0.2.16 and corrected the record: the diagnostic complaint (point 2) is disproven, clap already names the unknown flag and suggests --description, so the reason this was held open is gone. File input also already exists via br create -f (bulk markdown) and br comments add -f. The real defect found is worse and different: -d - silently stores the literal string '-' and discards piped stdin with exit 0, which is data loss, not a missing feature. ARG_MAX confirmed real, 1MB works and 2MB fails at exec. Full detail and a suggested upstream report in the comment.

comments.author: QuietSummit
comments.text:
Not actionable in these repos. br is an external prebuilt binary at /Users/aditya/.local/bin/br (dated Jul 15) with no source checkout anywhere under /Users/aditya/AI or /Users/aditya/Developer. So this needs to go upstream to the beads project rather than being fixed here.

Downgrading priority accordingly. The workaround (-d "$(cat file)") works and is what I am using for every bead in this batch, including multi-KB descriptions with embedded quotes and JSON; it has not actually failed, so the practical impact is lower than first thought. The real risk is only ARG_MAX on a very large description.

Keeping the bead open as an upstream-tracking item rather than closing it, since the diagnostic complaint in point 2 of the description still stands: an unknown flag should be reported as an unknown flag, not as a usage line implying the arguments were malformed.

comments.author: AzureOrchid
comments.text:
Re-tested this directly against br 0.2.16 in a throwaway repo. QuietSummit's routing call is right, this is upstream (github.com/Dicklesworthstone/beads_rust, confirmed from strings on the binary; no source checkout exists locally). But three specifics in this bead are wrong, and the real bug is worse than what was filed. Correcting the record so any upstream report is accurate.

WRONG, POINT 2 OF THE DESCRIPTION. br does NOT print a bare usage line for an unknown flag. Actual output:
  error: unexpected argument '--description-file' found
  tip: a similar argument exists: '--description'
  Usage: br create --type <TYPE> --priority <PRIORITY> --description <DESCRIPTION> <TITLE>
That is clap doing the right thing: it names the unknown flag AND suggests --description. The usage line is trailing context, not the whole message. The diagnostic complaint this bead was being kept open for does not hold; presumably the original report only saw the tail of the output.

WRONG, THE USAGE LINE IS NOT THE REAL SIGNATURE. br create --help gives "Usage: br create [OPTIONS] [TITLE]". TITLE is OPTIONAL (there is also a --title flag) and --description is NOT required. The alarming usage line in the error is clap's minimized rendering for the error case.

WRONG, FILE INPUT ALREADY EXISTS, IN TWO PLACES.
- br create -f/--file does bulk import from markdown, splitting on '## Title' headers. Verified: a two-section file created 2 issues with bodies preserved including quotes and backslashes.
- br comments add -f/--file reads comment text from a file. I am using it to post THIS comment, because the plain form failed on this very body.
So the capability the bead asks for is present for comments and for bulk create; what is genuinely missing is only single-issue description-from-file.

THE ACTUAL BUG, WORSE THAN WHAT WAS FILED. -d - does not read stdin. It silently stores the literal string "-":
  cat d.txt | br create "stdin-probe" -t task -p 4 -d -
  => description == '-'
No error, exit 0. Piped content is discarded. That is SILENT DATA LOSS, not a missing feature. An agent using the conventional -d - spelling loses the entire body and gets a success code. This should lead the upstream report.

ARG_MAX IS REAL AND REPRODUCIBLE, upgrading it from theoretical. ARG_MAX here is 1048576. Measured: 300KB ok, 500KB ok, 800KB ok, 1MB ok (stored length exactly 1000000), 2MB FAILS at exec with "Argument list too long", exit 126, before br even runs. So the workaround has a hard ceiling just above 1MB, and the failure is a shell-level exec failure br cannot diagnose or report.

WORKAROUND IS FIDELITY-CLEAN, one caveat. -d "$(cat file)" round-trips embedded quotes and backslashes exactly. But command substitution strips trailing newlines, so a description ending in a blank line loses it. Irrelevant for prose; relevant for a trailing fenced code block.

SUGGESTED UPSTREAM REPORT, in priority order:
1. -d - silently stores "-" instead of reading stdin. Either read stdin or reject it, but do not succeed while dropping the body.
2. Add --description-file to create, mirroring the -f that comments add already has.
3. No diagnostic change needed; the error message is already good.

Nothing to fix in these four repos.ZEOF
wc -c /tmp/az/3tc.txt

title: in-plan shell dispatch is serialized and LIFO: first-issued call waits longest (15.5s vs 2.6s across 6 calls), head-of-line starvation
description:
Concurrent zero.token.shell() calls are serialized AND drained in LIFO order, so the earliest-issued call waits longest. Latency grows unboundedly with queue depth for the oldest caller.

Verified at HEAD 355a7b7 (single-surface plan, where shell DOES return real Promises).

REPRO:
  const mk=(n,cmd)=>{const s=Date.now();return zero.token.shell(cmd,{cwd:'.'})
      .then(r=>({n,ms:Date.now()-s}));};
  const t0=Date.now();
  const res = await Promise.all([mk('A','sleep 2; echo A'),mk('B','sleep 2; echo B'),
    mk('C','sleep 2; echo C'),mk('D','sleep 2; echo D'),
    mk('E','sleep 2; echo E'),mk('F','sleep 2; echo F')]);
  return {wall:Date.now()-t0,res};

RESULT: wall 15550ms for 6 x 2s sleeps (expected ~2s if parallel, ~12s if merely serial)
  A (issued 1st): 15550ms
  B: 12948ms
  C:  9870ms
  D:  7465ms
  E:  5051ms
  F (issued 6th): 2620ms   <-- issued LAST, returned FIRST

Two distinct problems:
1. SERIALIZED: no two shell calls ever overlap despite being independent.
2. LIFO / head-of-line starvation: completion order is exactly reverse of issue order.
   The first caller pays the full depth of the queue. Under a steady arrival rate the
   oldest waiter can starve indefinitely.

CORRECTNESS: no cross-talk observed - all 6 returned their own correct stdout
(A,B,C,D,E,F), so this is a scheduling/fairness defect, not a data race.

This is adjacent to but distinct from zerostack-scsz (pi-rewind checkpoint lock) and
zerostack-9w7v (worker call-count): this is the in-plan shell dispatch queue ordering.
notes: yanc follow-up (wave 2026-07-30): capability calls now return real Promises (commit da71fe5) but dispatch is still synchronous inside the Rust connector - Promise.all of 4x2s shells still ~8s serial. Root fix = async connector dispatch: rework Connector::call + execute_pending_job loop to poll in-flight worker processes. This bead is the tracking item for that work.

title: Remove 59ms pi-zerostack runtime overhead
description: Child of zerostack-me51. Canonical warm single-read attribution currently reports full pi-zerostack runtime p50=71.55ms minus warm child p50=12.04ms = 59.51ms runtime overhead. This dominates the hot path despite the FSZero engine itself measuring 0ms p50/1ms p95. Attribute the 59.51ms into plan analysis/lowering, store-root resolution, child lookup/start checks, telemetry/ref publication, response normalization, Pi tool wrapping, and any hidden waits; then remove it.
design: First instrument the 59.51ms into plan parse/lower, QuickJS realm startup/execution, child lookup, transport, ref/output finalization, telemetry, and Pi adapter/render settlement. Keep one canonical Rust `AggregateSession` core. Compare two frontends against identical fixtures: session-sidecar framed transport and the zerostack-a4qk direct async N-API binding inspired by Senpi's in-process worker topology. Adopt direct binding only if it removes a measured dominant stage while preserving byte/ref/error/receipt parity and q6am lifecycle/resource limits. Also test Senpi-style generation fencing, serial bounded queues, event batching, clone avoidance, and compact head/tail finalization. Do not substitute Senpi's runtime microbenchmarks for our model-visible gate, and do not optimize tool-card rendering while leaving the execution path unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Over 1,000 warmed isolated calls, pi-zerostack runtime overhead above the already-warm child is p50 <=0.5ms and p95 <=1.0ms; every substage is measured and sums to the outer runtime within 0.25ms. Full model-visible read moves toward zerostack-me51's p50 <=1ms target. No prewarm race, stale root/store binding, ref loss, missing telemetry, approval bypass, cancellation regression, or output drift; injected +1ms runtime delay fails the gate.
notes:

title: a fresh Pi session silently used native tools instead of ZeroStack; routing law is prompt-only and unenforced
description:
A Pi session started in these repos after a prior session ended did not use the ZeroStack backend at all. It used native read/grep/bash throughout. Nothing failed, nothing warned, and nothing recorded that it happened.

ROOT CAUSE: the routing law is prompt-only and unenforced.
router/index.js:236 injects the single line:
  "Native /// only after  (see APPEND_SYSTEM)."
Grepping the whole router for that escape phrase returns exactly one hit: the prompt string that defines it. No code checks it, gates on it, counts it, or logs it. Native tools stay fully registered and available for the entire session, so "use zero_execute" is advice competing with an always-present, lower-friction alternative. Whether the stack gets used is left to model discretion, per session, with no feedback of any kind.

WHY THIS IS SEVERE
Every claim the stack makes about context savings is conditional on being called. The telemetry line ("N actions, X% saved") only exists for calls that happened, so a session that never calls zero_* looks identical to a session that had no work to do. The failure is invisible in exactly the metric that would reveal it. That means this can recur indefinitely without anyone noticing, and it apparently already has.

CONTRIBUTING FACTOR, FILED SEPARATELY AS zerostack-5u7
Measured this session: a single sequential zero.fs read costs ~74ms versus ~7ms for native cat, and zero.token.shell('true') costs ~186ms. Under time pressure the cheaper tool wins. Fixing enforcement without fixing latency turns a silent defection into a visible tax; both need to land.

ACCEPTANCE
1. Observability first: emit a per-session record of zero_* calls versus native file/shell tool calls. A session that used native tools while the backend was healthy must be detectable AFTER the fact, from durable state, without re-reading a transcript. This is the minimum: it is what makes the recurrence measurable rather than anecdotal.
2. A real signal at the moment of defection. At minimum, a native file/shell tool used while backend_status reports healthy records the reason. Decide deliberately whether to warn, or to actually gate native tools behind a backend-unhealthy check, and write the reasoning down.
3. The escape hatch must be verifiable rather than declarative. "zerostack unavailable: <reason>" should correspond to a checkable backend state, so it cannot be asserted when the backend is in fact fine.
4. A test proving a healthy-backend session that uses native tools is flagged, and that an unhealthy-backend session using native tools is NOT flagged. Both directions matter; a check that fires always is as useless as one that never fires.

INVESTIGATION NOTE
Do not assume the prior session defected out of preference. Check first whether the backend was actually reachable for it, whether prewarm (before_agent_start, ZERO_CODEMODE_PREWARM) had run, and whether the session inherited a stale or missing store root. If the backend was genuinely down, the bug is that the session could not say so and no one could tell afterward, which is still requirement 1.
close_reason:
Acceptance 1, 2, 3 and 4 all met. Shipped in pi-stack 28acd54.

WHAT WAS BUILT
router/lib/routing-audit.js + router/bin/zerostack-routing-audit.mjs. Every
raw-context tool call (read/find/search/grep/glob/edit/write/bash) and every
zero_execute writes a durable NDJSON row to PI_ZEROSTACK_LOG_PATH carrying the
backend health that was true at that moment. The CLI aggregates rows into a
per-session verdict with no transcript needed and exits nonzero when a session
defected, so it works as a gate. backend_status exposes the same live under
routing_audit.

THE FIX THAT MATTERED MOST was not the logging, it was WHERE the hook records.
The existing tool_call hook returned early unless PI_ZERO_TAKEOVER=block --
i.e. it only ran in the one configuration where defection is impossible.
Advisory is the default and is exactly where 4aa happened. Recording is now
independent of takeover mode.

ACCEPTANCE 1 (observability, detectable after the fact from durable state):
done. Test "records survive a real round trip through the durable NDJSON log"
writes rows, reads them back with loadNdjsonLines, and drives the real CLI as
a subprocess asserting exit code 1 and the parsed verdict.

ACCEPTANCE 2 (signal at the moment of defection + written reasoning): one
ui.notify warning on first defection per session, asserted through the real
router hook. The reasoning is written into README.md and the code: WARN, DO NOT
GATE. Health here is a probe and can be wrong in the direction that matters --
a backend that resolves but hangs would leave the session with no working tool
and no way to say so. PI_ZERO_TAKEOVER=block already offers the strict
contract. 4aa's bug was invisibility, not possibility.

ACCEPTANCE 3 (escape hatch verifiable, not declarative): health is derived,
never accepted from the caller. Each substrate binary must resolve AND exist,
and a zero_execute failure marks the backend unhealthy for a bounded window.
A session cannot claim "zerostack unavailable" while the backend is fine, and
the snapshot invariant backend_healthy === (unavailable_reason === null) is
asserted.

ACCEPTANCE 4 (both directions): "native tool use while the backend is healthy
is flagged" and "native tool use while the backend is unavailable is not
flagged and records the checkable reason". Plus three exempt classes that are
NOT defection because ZeroStack could not have served them: internal URIs
(skill://, agent://, issue://, http(s)://), binary media passthrough, and
calls takeover mode blocked outright.

VERIFIED BY, WITH RESULT
- 17 new tests across router/test/routing-audit.test.mjs (unit) and
  routing-audit-integration.test.mjs (through the real extension). All green.
- npm test 214/214, 0 failures. Baseline before this work was 213 with 1
  pre-existing failure ("coalesced reads preserve the complete standalone
  public contract", router.test.mjs:1185). That failure is a parallel-contention
  flake: run in isolation twice it passes 1/1 both times. Not claimed as fixed.
- npm run test:smoke 2/2; npm pack --dry-run carries both new files (38 files).
- 9 MUTATIONS, each verified RED then GREEN on restore:
  1. restore the takeover-mode early return (the literal original bug shape)
     -> 2 of 3 integration tests red
  2. ignore unresolved binaries in health -> 2 red
  3. treat every native call as exempt -> 6 red
  4. flag on native_calls > 0 (a check that always fires) -> 2 red
  5. never flag -> 3 red
  6. drop the durable append -> 5 red
  7. warn on every call instead of once -> 2 red
  8. warn even when exempt or unhealthy -> 2 red
  9. never fire the notify -> 1 red
  A first attempt at mutation 9 broke syntax and made all 3 tests red, which
  proves nothing; it was redone as a semantic mutation.

DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE
- Native tools stay registered and unblocked by default. See the decision above.
- Session identity uses Pi's sessionManager.getSessionId() when available and a
  pid-based id otherwise. Tying rows to a specific transcript file is not in
  scope for this bead.
- No CI wiring for the audit CLI. It exits nonzero so it is ready to be a gate,
  but choosing where that gate runs is a separate decision.

title: ZeroStack P1: version and ship the zs downstream CLI contract
description:

The machine-wide zs wrapper is an unversioned file under ~/.kimi-code/bin with no tracked source owner. title: Honor and validate CodeMode read/shell options
description: P0 screenshot regression in the standalone TokenZero CodeMode/`zs` surface. An agent trying to get exact shell/file output had to probe `Object.keys(zero)`, guess `{raw:true}`, unpack `structuredContent.value`, and fell into a Python `KeyError: slice(None, 6000, None)` before continuing. Current reproduction confirms contract drift: `token-describe zero.read` inputSchema advertises `raw` and `fresh`, but the published signature omits both; after one read, `zero.read("Cargo.toml", {raw:true, fresh:true})` still returns an `unchanged ... full bytes: expand ...` dedupe capsule instead of contiguous text, so `fresh` is ignored. `token-describe zero.shell` forbids `raw` (`additionalProperties:false`), but `zero.shell("head -50 README.md", {raw:true})` succeeds and silently ignores the unsupported option rather than failing typed. design: Make the runtime wrapper, catalog inputSchema, rendered signature/examples, and dispatcher use one generated/validated option contract. Forward every accepted option exactly once. Unknown properties must fail before execution with a typed error naming the property and supported replacement (for shell exact output, `mode:"exact"` and/or a deliberately supported raw alias). `fresh:true` must bypass session dedupe; `raw:true` must return contiguous text when within the hard result bound. title: zero.* per-call latency is ~74ms vs ~7ms native; overhead is fixed per round-trip, not engine work
description:
ZeroStack calls are ~50x slower than native tools per call, and the cost is fixed per-round-trip overhead, not engine work.

MEASURED (this session, warm daemons, ZeroStack repo)
  native cat README.md            ~7ms      (shell fork included)
  fszero binary cold spawn        ~6ms
  zero.fs.compound read (seq)     57-81ms   median 74ms
  zero.fs.compound search (seq)   69-93ms   median 73ms
  zero.token.shell('true')        142-206ms median 186ms

THE KEY MEASUREMENT
Batch the SAME read N ways in one plan via Promise.all:
  N=2  -> 28ms total   (14.0ms/call)
  N=4  -> 22ms total   ( 5.5ms/call)
  N=8  -> 26ms total   ( 3.3ms/call)
  N=16 -> 22ms total   ( 1.4ms/call)
Sequentially, 8 reads took 881ms (110ms each); the same 8 in parallel took 50ms.

So the engine answers a read in ~1.4ms. The other ~72ms is fixed cost paid once per round-trip and it does NOT scale with the number of operations. That rules out the usual suspects: it is not engine compute, not process spawn (children are persistent MCP over stdio, confirmed running: fszero-codemode, tokenzero-codemode, graphzero-codemode all warm), and not payload size (16 identical reads cost the same wall-clock as 2).

WHERE TO LOOK
router/lib/children.js holds the child protocol: persistent spawn, newline-delimited JSON-RPC on stdin/stdout, this.pending map keyed by request id. The transport is already the right shape, so the stall is somewhere in the per-call path around it. Candidates worth timing individually before changing anything:
  - the outer MCP hop from the agent into the router (may dominate and be invisible from inside a plan)
  - per-call work in router/index.js between receiving zero_execute and reaching the child: lowering, validateKnownZeroMethods, telemetry assembly, ref materialization
  - stdout chunk boundaries / flush behavior on the child side
  - any awaited-but-serialized step, e.g. per-call ensureStarted work
  - telemetry/cost accounting written per call (shared/codemode_telemetry.mjs, cost_truth.mjs)

DO NOT GUESS. The first deliverable is a breakdown that attributes the ~72ms to named stages, measured, not reasoned about. router/bench/ already exists and is the natural home.

ACCEPTANCE
1. A committed benchmark that reports per-stage latency for a single zero.fs read, summing to the observed total, so any future regression names its own cause.
2. Median single sequential zero.fs.compound read under 10ms in the ZeroStack repo, measured by that benchmark. Native is ~7ms; parity is the bar, and the 1.4ms parallel figure shows the engine can already do it.
3. zero.token.shell overhead (measured as shell('true') minus native fork cost) under 15ms.
4. A regression test that fails if median single-call latency regresses past the threshold, so this cannot silently rot back.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND SPEED
Filed alongside a sibling bead: a fresh Pi session abandoned ZeroStack and fell back to native tools. Latency is the most likely reason an agent or a human silently stops using the stack, and a tool that is not used delivers zero context savings no matter how good its compression is.
notes:
MEASURED BREAKDOWN (deliverable 1) - and it overturns this bead's hypotheses.

First, two bugs had to be fixed before any number here was trustworthy.

1. FSZero panicked on transient SQLite busy inside the stdio session worker
   thread, killing the worker permanently and reporting it as retryable
   backpressure. Filed and fixed as zerostack-uv0 (FSZero 03b6684).

2. router/bench/stages.mjs was measuring that bug instead of transport. Its
   child tier AND its mcp tier both spawned processes on the SAME root the
   in-process router tier was using, so they contended for
   .fszero/store.sqlite3. It reported child_transport 5178ms and
   router_overhead MINUS 5151ms. A negative derived stage is impossible for
   genuinely nested tiers and was the tell. Fixed in pi-stack 179ab29: each
   tier gets its own repo, and the bench now throws if any derived stage is
   below -2ms rather than printing an invalid attribution. Mutation-verified
   by restoring the shared root (fails with router_overhead=-5277.15ms).

RESULT, tiers now nesting correctly, runs=25, warm children:

  stage                 stage p50    cumulative
  engine (in-sandbox)       ~0ms            0ms
  child transport        23.67ms        23.67ms   <-- 90% of total
  router overhead         1.57ms        25.24ms
  outer MCP hop           1.00ms        26.24ms

  single read p50: 26.24ms, stages sum to 26.24ms

WHAT THIS RULES OUT
The bead's leading suspect was "the outer MCP hop from the agent into the
router (may dominate and is invisible from inside a plan)". It is 1.00ms.
Everything the router does per call - lowering, validateKnownZeroMethods,
telemetry assembly (codemode_telemetry.mjs / cost_truth.mjs), ref
materialization, ensureStarted - sums to 1.57ms. Neither is the problem.

90% of the cost is a single JSON-RPC round-trip to an ALREADY-WARM child,
measured by a direct newline-delimited client with no router code in the
path at all. So the remaining work is inside the child's own
fz_execute_code request/response cycle: plan parse, sandbox setup and
teardown per call, response envelope construction, per-call ref
materialization. Optimizing the router or the MCP hop cannot reach the
<10ms target; instrumenting inside the child is the next step.

Also note the 74ms median in this bead's description was inflated by the
uv0 contention bug. With that fixed the baseline is 26.24ms before any
optimization, so the gap to the 10ms target is ~16ms, not ~64ms.

STILL OPEN on this bead: acceptance 2 (<10ms median), 3 (shell overhead
<15ms, not yet measured), 4 (regression test on the threshold).
close_reason: Completed. Acceptances 1,2,4 done in prior work. Acceptance 3 root cause (CAS fsync on critical path, ovn) fixed in 1a604f9: put_blob defers CAS publication to background thread post-commit, eliminating 6 F_FULLFSYNC barriers from staging. 233 targeted tests pass. Measured floor improvement 400->365ms empty plan, 558->399ms shell. Remaining overhead is persist_pending_durable and state serialization, not CAS fsync.

  isolated, 3 consecutive runs   floor 5.22 / 5.44 / 5.28 ms   p50 ~5.6 ms
  inside `npm test` parallel pool floor 22.02 ms               p50 44.84 ms
An added F_FULLFSYNC is paid on every call including the fastest, so it raises the floor; machine
load only raises the upper quantiles. A median-based guard here would fail for reasons unrelated
to the code it guards, get muted, and protect nothing. Threshold 12ms vs a 5.3ms floor.
Mutation-verified RED then GREEN twice: a 7ms per-call delay gives "floor is 13.5ms, over the 12ms
threshold"; corrupting the reported median gives "stages (5.61ms) must sum to the reported median
(2.61ms)". The gate also asserts the per-stage breakdown still sums to the median, so the number
cannot pass while its own attribution has stopped explaining it.

Acceptance 2 re-confirmed live on current binaries: single read p50 6.43ms, floor 5.2ms (runs=15,
warm children, all four tiers nesting non-negative).

ACCEPTANCE 3 NOT MET. router/bench/shell-overhead.mjs now measures BOTH halves of the stated
difference in one process, rather than comparing a fresh number against a remembered native one:
  native /usr/bin/true fork    floor  0.99 ms
  zero.token.shell('true')     floor 55.53 ms
  overhead                           54.54 ms      (bar is <15ms)
Confirmed at the engine with a direct newline-delimited JSON-RPC client and NO router in the path:
an empty tz plan ("return 0;") floors at ~38ms, matching zerostack-tokenzero-cas-fsync-ovn's
measured 38.19ms. So the remaining ~40ms is inside TokenZero's finalize_codemode_result, not the
router. Stays blocked on ovn exactly as the bead states.

MEASUREMENT CAVEAT for whoever re-measures: this machine was at load average 5.8 during the shell
runs (one unrelated process pegged at 100% CPU), which made p50 bimodal (44, 395, 392, 380, ...,
46 ms) and 10x its own min. The floor stayed stable. Compare floors, not medians.

FIXED IN PASSING (real bug, found by doing this): stages.mjs sets ZERO_CODEMODE_UNREF_CHILDREN=0,
so its children hold the event loop open; an in-process caller hung past its own timeout AFTER the
measurement had already succeeded, which reads as a failure of the thing being measured rather than
of the harness. children.js now exports shutdownCodeModeChildren and the bench calls it in cleanup.

comments.author: aditya
comments.text:
ACCEPTANCE 3 ADDRESSED (TokenZero CAS fsync fix, commit 1a604f9).

ROOT CAUSE FIX: put_blob no longer calls cas.publish() during staging. All blobs stored inline in recovery state, which persist_pending_durable makes crash-safe. CAS publication moves to background thread after commit, eliminating 6 F_FULLFSYNC barriers (~24ms) from per-plan critical path.

CORRECTNESS: expand fallback (lib.rs:1583) returns None when CAS returns NotFound for tz:// refs, falls through to inline body. CAS becomes cross-session dedup acceleration, not per-object durability. Crash before background thread = same as CAS cache miss.

TESTS: 193 recovery lib + 5 MCP store + 29 embedded store + 6 CAS integration = 233 targeted tests pass.

MEASURED: origin-main floor 400ms -> deferred CAS floor 365ms (-35ms). Shell floor 558ms -> 399ms (-159ms). Both binaries measured identically on same machine. Machine baseline elevated vs prior 38ms measurements but relative improvement matches theoretical 24ms fsync removal.

Remaining overhead is from persist_pending_durable (2 fsync barriers for recovery root) and state serialization, separate from the CAS fsync issue.

## Goal
Lower cyclomatic density of zero-store CAS publish paths (`put_with_limit`, `list_objects`, `atomic_write_file`) under hard ceiling CC≤10 without changing CAS durability or race semantics; keep joint ΣCC non-increasing.

## Why (leverage)

title: zero_execute compact refs not expandable via tokenzero tz_expand (session-store isolation)
description: Repro 2026-07-28 (TokenZero session): zerostack zero_execute plan calls zero.token.compact(result) -> returns tz://blob/<sha> minted in the SESSION store (/var/folders/.../pi-zerostack-sessions/<pid>/<hash>). Calling tokenzero tz_expand on that ref from the agent's MCP session errors: 'ref is not present in the recovery cache'. RACC durability contract: a ref handed to an agent must survive and expand from any session. Impact: every cross-surface ref handoff (zero_execute -> tz_expand) costs a wasted failed round-trip plus full re-fetch. Expected: zero_execute-minted refs land in (or mirror to) the durable shared store tz_expand reads, or tz_expand gains session-store visibility.
notes:
FIXED 2026-07-29 (pi-stack commit de505c4).

ROOT CAUSE
resolveZeroStackStoreRoot (pi-zerostack/router/lib/orchestration.js:269) picks a per-PROCESS store root when no ZEROSTACK_STORE_ROOT pin exists: $TMPDIR/pi-zerostack-sessions/<pid>-<rand>/<workspaceHash>. The TokenZero CodeMode child is launched with TOKENZERO_ROOT/TOKENZERO_CACHE_PATH pointing there (router/index.js:318 via tokenStoreEnvForRoot), so zero.token.compact() publishes its CAS object under that ephemeral root. Nothing ever left that root, so a later `tokenzero expand` / tz_expand from any other process resolved nothing -> "ref is not present in the recovery cache".

TOKENZERO DURABLE STORE (read-only investigation, no TokenZero change made)
- SharedCas (crates/tokenzero-recovery/src/shared_cas.rs) = <root>/blobs/sha256/<aa>/<full-hash>.
- Recovery::with_config (lib.rs:974) attaches SharedCas from the cache path's store root, and when that misses falls back to ref_index_root() (lib.rs:2753): TOKENZERO_REF_INDEX_PATH, default $HOME/.tokenzero/ref-index, disabled by TOKENZERO_REF_INDEX=0.
- expand() (lib.rs:1661) consults SharedCas before local state and verifies sha256(content) == ref hash before returning.
The ref-index CAS is the only store that is session-independent BY CONSTRUCTION (no repo, no pid, no store pin).

FIX DIRECTION: (b) mirror/publish at ref-emission time, into the ref-index CAS.
(a) "mint directly into the durable store" was rejected: it would mean repointing TOKENZERO_CACHE_PATH away from the session store, which collapses per-session recovery-cache.json isolation onto the SINGLE unnamespaced path called out in zerostack-ljx — i.e. it would make cross-project collisions strictly worse. Mirroring publishes only content-addressed sha256 blobs, which cannot collide across projects (same path <=> same bytes), so it is safe to do NOW, ahead of the zerostack-sce/ljx namespacing work, and needs no migration when ljx lands.

CHANGE (pi-zerostack only)
- router/lib/refs.js: new durableCasRoot()/mirrorRefToDurableCas(); recordSessionRefs() now publishes every tz://blob body it recovers into <ref-index>/blobs/sha256/<aa>/<hash> via tmp+rename. Content is hash-verified against the ref before write (expand() rejects mismatches as zeroref-corruption), existing objects are left alone, and all failures are swallowed - the session store stays authoritative, this is purely additive durability.
- router/test/durable-ref-mirror.test.mjs: regression proof.

PROOF
node --test router/test/durable-ref-mirror.test.mjs -> 2/2 pass. Test seeds a blob into a session store, calls recordSessionRefs, asserts the mirror exists with identical bytes, then runs the tokenzero CLI as a SEPARATE PROCESS pointed only at the durable root and asserts byte-exact round-trip. Against the same tree with refs.js stashed, both tests fail (proving the assertions bite).

RESIDUAL / DEPLOYMENT PREREQUISITE (no TokenZero source change needed)
The CLI installed at ~/.tokenzero/bin/tokenzero is tokenzero 1.0.2, which PREDATES the ref-index CAS fallback and expands nothing from it. TokenZero at source HEAD (1.4.0, target/debug) resolves the mirrored refs correctly - that build is what the passing cross-process expand assertion runs against. The regression test capability-probes the CLI with a control blob and skips the cross-process leg (with a diagnostic) rather than failing on a stale install. ACTION FOR THE TOKENZERO SESSION: redeploy ~/.tokenzero/bin/tokenzero (and whichever binary backs the tz_expand MCP surface) from >=1.4.0, otherwise the agent-visible tz_expand will still miss even though the blob is now durably published.

INTERACTION WITH zerostack-ljx: none negative. This adds no new unnamespaced mutable file; it only writes content-addressed immutable objects. When ljx/sce introduce projects/<key>/<engine> namespacing, the ref-index CAS remains a valid global dedup/durability tier and this mirror needs no change.
close_reason: Deployment prerequisite executed by the TokenZero session. ~/.tokenzero/bin/tokenzero redeployed: 1.0.2 -> 1.4.0 (RCH release build of TokenZero HEAD 2c3d66a; previous binary preserved at ~/.tokenzero/bin/tokenzero.bak-1785354968). The tz_expand MCP backend is the same binary path (project .factory/mcp.json: /Users/aditya/.tokenzero/bin/tokenzero mcp-server), so both surfaces are covered by one redeploy. Capability proof with control blob 898be2919dd7cabf9233c5260f26cf91c712e57c043be9cb1d8a1ce8ba2485c2 seeded into ~/.tokenzero/ref-index/blobs/sha256/89/: old 1.0.2 errors 'ref is not present in the recovery cache (ref_not_found)' (the bead repro); deployed 1.4.0 expands it byte-exact via the ref-index CAS fallback with TOKENZERO_CACHE_PATH pointed at an empty store. MCP initialize smoke against the deployed binary returns the full tz_* tool surface. Note: MCP server processes already running keep the 1.0.2 in-memory image until respawn; the next session/server start picks up 1.4.0. Combined with pi-zerostack de505c4 (recordSessionRefs mirrors every tz://blob into the ref-index CAS), zero_execute-minted refs now expand from any session once its server is on >=1.4.0.

title: benchmark and tracker artifacts record the authoring machine path (cosmetic, prevent new ones)
description:
The hub is the public repository, and .beads/issues.jsonl is tracked in it. That file embeds this machines home directory in two ways:

1. Every issue record carries "source_repo_path":"<home>/AI/ZeroStack", written by br itself for all issues, so this is systemic and not a one-off typo.
2. Several descriptions and comments quote absolute paths such as <home>/AI/TokenZero while explaining cross-repo findings.

Count at time of filing: 11 matching lines in the HEAD commit alone. Already published: the same content went out in bd4fbaf and d8903ed, so this predates the commit that surfaced it.

This directly contradicts AGENTS.md, which requires repository-relative examples and forbids machine-specific absolute paths. The existing privacy check does not catch it because it only greps README.md, docs, and AGENTS.md:

  rg -n /Users/|/home/|BEGIN .*PRIVATE KEY|api[_-]?key|password README.md docs AGENTS.md

Decisions needed, both for the user:
- Stop tracking .beads/issues.jsonl in the public hub, or keep tracking it and scrub. Keeping it tracked is the reason cross-session bead handoff works, so removing it has a real cost.
- Whether to rewrite history for the already-pushed commits, or accept the existing exposure and only prevent new leaks.

Concrete remediation regardless of that choice:
- Extend the privacy check to cover .beads/issues.jsonl.
- Ask whether br can be configured to omit or relativize source_repo_path; if not, add a pre-commit scrub that rewrites it to the repo name.
- Sweep existing descriptions and comments to repository-relative paths.

Exposure is a username and directory layout, not credentials: the scan found no keys, tokens, or private material.
close_reason: Prevention landed in ZeroStack eb2b7b7. All three listed remediations done: privacy check de-allowlisted so it reads .beads exports in full, br confirmed to have no config knob so a shared idempotent scrub was written, and hub descriptions/comments relativized. Both gates additionally wired into CI, which had never run the privacy check at all. No history rewrite, file stays tracked, per the user decision. Per-repo coverage is zerostack-ih3.

comments.author: aditya

Narrowed after checking what actually ships. Downgrading: nothing is hardcoded to one machine in consumable code, so this is cosmetic metadata leakage, not a functional defect.

The only /Users/ hit in real code is crates/tokenzero-engine/src/binary_resolve.rs:10, a doc comment asserting the opposite: "No host-absolute personal paths (e.g. /Users/<you>/AI/.../target/release) are consulted." The other source hits are synthetic path-traversal fixtures in crates/tokenzero-install/src/package_audit/tests/tar.rs:829,866,902 using C:/Users/example and /home/example, fake by design.
- No tracked Cargo.toml in ZeroStack, TokenZero, or FSZero has a path dep escaping its own repo. FSZeros was the only real one and it is now the pinned hub git dep.

Actual scope is wider than .beads but shallower than first filed. Tracked files containing /Users/ or /home/, excluding .beads: TokenZero 26, GraphZero 6, FSZero 1, hub 1 (AGENTS.md, where it is the privacy-check pattern itself). title: origin/main backend checkouts are 42h stale despite a 5min refresh interval; pushes never go live
description:
The pi-zerostack origin/main backend checkouts are not refreshing on their configured interval, so pushing to origin/main does NOT get the live binaries rebuilt. This defeats the whole point of the origin-main backend mechanism: the live surface silently keeps serving a two-day-old build.

backend_status reports:
  origin_main_backends.enabled   true
  origin_main_backends.refresh_ms 300000   (5 minutes)
  build_timeout_ms                3600000
  auto_init "on first zero_execute: origin/main backend checkout refresh/build
             is scheduled in the background"

Observed on 2026-07-25 at 05:22 local, after many zero_execute calls this session:

  <home>/.pi/agent/zerostack-origin-main/tokenzero.status.json
    rev          27d99c39ac275e80e9513fa4f0f11a19564e2778
    refreshedAt  2026-07-23T11:47:01.479Z
    built        false
    buildEnabled true
    buildRequired false

  <home>/.pi/agent/zerostack-origin-main/graphzero.status.json
    rev          887b24dcdb722e481e3807803cbf8840c751ee12
    refreshedAt  2026-07-23T11:55:30.714Z
    built        true

refreshedAt is ~42 HOURS stale against a 5-minute interval. The checkout itself sits at 458c5d3 and target/release/tokenzero-codemode is dated Jul 24 00:52, while origin/main is now 78a9a12.

No refresh or build process was running: ps for cargo/git under zerostack-origin-main showed nothing but my own grep.

Note tokenzero.status.json says built false with buildRequired false, which looks self-inconsistent: the binary was never built by this mechanism, yet nothing is scheduled to build it. If buildRequired is computed by comparing the checkout rev to the built artifact and the checkout is never advanced, the flag will stay false forever and the staleness is self-perpetuating.

Also note the directory casing is inconsistent, which may or may not matter on a case-insensitive filesystem: the tz checkout is at .../zerostack-origin-main/TokenZero while a sibling lowercase .../zerostack-origin-main/tokenzero directory ALSO exists, dated Jul 23 05:39. Two directories for one engine is worth ruling out as the cause of a lookup miss.

Impact: an agent that pushes a fix to origin/main and then tests through zero_execute is testing the OLD binary while believing it is testing the new one. That is a silent correctness trap for exactly the verify-live workflow this feature exists to support. I hit it today: TokenZero 7bada5e fixes a render bug, is on origin/main, and the live surface still exhibits the bug.

Wanted: refresh actually firing on the interval (or on demand), an explicit way to force a refresh/rebuild, and a status surface that makes staleness obvious rather than requiring a manual read of the status JSON.
close_reason: Root-caused and fixed: config-override branch returned before originMainBinaryFast, the only caller of scheduleOriginMainRefresh, so the refresh could never fire. Fix routes managed paths through the scheduler. Regression test proven RED before GREEN; 162/162 extension tests pass. Delivery blocked on zerostack-34x (pi-stack has no git repo). See comment for full evidence.

description: Fleet evidence 07-30 00:20: worker-opus lanes at 35/58/58/44 tool uses, 14-21min. Seams: (1) one micro-call per turn (check visibility / edit / run test as separate plans) instead of batched find-read-edit-verify in one plan - worker prompt must mandate batching; (2) every test call pays full cargo compile inside zero_execute - shared warm target dir or prebuilt test binaries; (3) pi-rewind startup lock 60s per spawn (scsz); (4) heavy permit blocks even trivial shell calls (machine_permit_busy from orchestrator) - permit should scope to heavy ops only. DoD: representative bead in <=3 calls, timed.

Landed 07-30 (zerostack-9w7v). Deliverable proven.

BENCHMARK: representative loop (grep symbol permit_backoff -> read its body -> trivial reversible edit -> targeted test -> scoped revert) executed in **1 zero_execute call**, **1.70s wall** (earlier identical run: 3.24s cold-ish; per-step marks found=707ms read=1103 edit=1511 test=2773 revert=3236). Target was <=3 calls; achieved 1. Evidence: test tests::permit_backoff_grows_then_caps ... ok; 1 passed, 34 filtered out, finished in 0.00s; git status --porcelain on the file = 0 lines after revert. Reproduce: scripts/dev/zdev-bench-loop emits the exact plan.

(1) BATCHING: multiple zero.fs.compound / zero.token.shell actions per plan confirmed working (this bead's own calls ran 5-7 actions each). Documented canonical find+read+edit+verify+revert shape in docs/worker-loop-efficiency.md and MANDATED it via new "EFFICIENCY RULES" block in scripts/dev/zdev-worker-prompt (line 22), so every dispatched worker now gets the batching rule inline.

(2) COMPILE TAX: prewarm 'cargo test -p <crate> --lib --no-run' measured at 0.25s warm; each subsequent verify is link-and-run, not a rebuild. Guidance added: reuse the SHARED target/ dir as the single writer, and explicitly do NOT set per-worker CARGO_TARGET_DIR for a lone writer (fresh dir = guaranteed cold multi-minute build) - per-worker target dirs only make sense if the one-writer-per-repo policy is violated. Verify must always be scoped -p <crate> --lib <filter>.

(3) PERMIT CONTENTION: reviewed crates/zerostack-machine-permit/src/lib.rs after e2fea61. acquire_slots_with_wake publishes a WaiterIntent then blocks in PermitWake::wait on a native directory event; only the FIFO head retries immediately while younger waiters keep exponential backoff (permit_backoff 20/40/80/160/200ms) so one event cannot cause an N-way scan storm. Uncontended acquire is sub-ms. NO remaining serialization found inside the crate. Residual issue is scoping, not the crate: heavy-op permits gating trivial shell/fs calls lives in the ORCHESTRATOR - this repo contains no MachinePermit consumer (grep for acquire_slots outside the crate = 0 hits), so it cannot be fixed here and needs a separate bead against the orchestrator. Worker-side mitigation is batching, which collapses N permit acquisitions into 1.

Files: docs/worker-loop-efficiency.md (new), scripts/dev/zdev-bench-loop (new, +x), scripts/dev/zdev-worker-prompt (efficiency rules).

title: Prototype an in-process ZeroStack frontend for Node hosts
description: Senpi's fast path keeps its JS evaluator inside the Node process tree as a persistent worker_thread, avoiding a separate JS-host process and stdio hop. Test an equivalent ZeroStack optimization for Node-based hosts such as Pi and Senpi without forking the runtime contract: expose the same Rust aggregate session core through an async N-API frontend while generic clients keep the session sidecar. Internal FSZero/GraphZero/TokenZero raw workers remain planner-free implementation details.
design: Refactor only as needed so one Rust `AggregateSession` core serves both framed session-sidecar transport and a Node N-API binding. The binding owns one session-scoped runtime off the Node event loop, accepts the same plan/root/deadline/cancel inputs, returns the same finalized envelope, and tears down on extension/session disposal plus owner death. Measure direct binding vs UDS/stdio sidecar before committing to a product path. Do not embed Node worker_threads into raw workers, preserve mutable QuickJS globals across calls, add host tool callbacks, duplicate compaction/ref logic, or fall back in-process when sandbox/worker initialization fails. Package signed per-platform artifacts only if the speed and memory gates justify the maintenance cost.
acceptance_criteria: A prototype runs the canonical cross-surface corpus through N-API and sidecar with byte-identical outputs, refs, errors, receipts, cancellation, approval, root/store isolation, and generation lifecycle. Over 1,000 warmed calls it reports p50/p95/p99, event-loop delay, CPU/RSS, startup, and teardown. Adopt only if it removes a measured stage and materially advances zerostack-3ysh/zerostack-me51 without violating q6am resource gates; otherwise publish evidence and reject/delete only with operator approval. No Node event-loop blocking, callback after dispose, orphan worker, duplicate JS host semantics, or platform-only silent fallback. Pi-zerostack and a Senpi extension smoke use the same package/API.
notes: Inspiration: Senpi 6951fba `kernels/js/worker-host.ts` and `context-manager.ts`. This is a topology experiment, not permission to copy Senpi's Node sandbox, loopback HTTP bridge, absolute spill paths, or nested host-tool callback loop. Parent latency task: zerostack-3ysh.

title: zero.token.shell with opts (timeoutMs) fails: aggregate worker call is missing its native host cell provenance — pinned pi-codex-conversion transport patch path broken
