title: Corrupt store.sqlite3 permanently bricks every session on a root; salvage is created, verified good, then never used
description:
FOUND LIVE while using zero_execute. Every plan against two different roots
returned:
  {"kind":"substrate","message":"stdio MCP session worker is gone (terminal)"}

Running the child directly showed the real cause, which the router hides:

  thread '<unnamed>' panicked at src/core/session.rs:196:25:
  fszero: durable store required (durable integrity gate rejected the source:
  integrity_check row failed: database disk image is malformed; source was not
  repaired or replaced; forensic=...; salvage=...; report=...; salvage may
  contain data loss, was not auto-promoted, and must be reviewed before use)

This is NOT the transient-busy case fixed in zerostack-uv0/03b6684. The gate
correctly refuses to retry a malformed image. The bug is what happens next.

SCOPE - not a one-off
  ~/AI/FSZero/.zerostack/fszero/store.sqlite3            malformed
  ~/AI/TokenZero/.zerostack/fszero/store.sqlite3         malformed
  ~/AI/TokenZero/.zerostack/tokenzero/.fszero/store.sqlite3  malformed
  ~/AI/TokenZero/.zerostack/fszero.corrupt-1784351118/   an EARLIER occurrence
Independent roots corrupting the same way, plus a pre-existing .corrupt-
directory, means this recurs. Two engines are unusable until a human notices.

THE SHARP EDGE
The salvage copy the gate itself produced passes cleanly:
  sqlite3 store.sqlite3.salvage-<ts>/store.sqlite3 "PRAGMA integrity_check;" -> ok
  sqlite3 store.sqlite3 "PRAGMA integrity_check;" -> malformed (11)
So recovery data exists and is verified good, but is deliberately not promoted,
and nothing offers it to the operator. The session panics instead. The engine
does the hard part (detect, quarantine, salvage, verify) and then strands the
result. Meanwhile the panic kills the session worker for the life of the
process, so every later request fails terminally.

Refusing to auto-promote is defensible - salvage can lose data. Bricking the
root with no path forward is not.

WORKAROUND USED: manually moved store.sqlite3 aside; the engine rebuilt and
service returned immediately. That is exactly what should not require a human.

ACCEPTANCE
1. A malformed store does not permanently brick the root. Either rebuild
   empty (the store is a cache) or start ephemeral, with a loud warning.
2. The verified-good salvage is surfaced to the operator with the exact
   promote command, not just a path buried in a panic string.
3. The router surfaces the underlying cause; "session worker is gone" with the
   real reason discarded is undebuggable without running the child by hand.
4. Investigate the WRITE PATH. Three independent stores malformed on one
   machine points at how pages are written/flushed, not at hardware.
5. Regression test: corrupt a store, assert the session still serves and the
   salvage is reported.
close_reason:
Fixed in FSZero cf387c6 (committed, NOT pushed).

WHAT CHANGED
An unusable durable store now degrades the session to in-memory recovery with a
loud message instead of panicking. durable_degraded was already plumbed through
capabilities and doctor, so the degradation is visible rather than silent.

Deliberately narrow. Only corruption and a rejecting integrity gate degrade:
  integrity gate rejected the source / disk image is malformed /
  file is not a database / database corruption
Permissions failures, a missing parent directory, or a full disk still panic,
because those may mean the caller is pointed somewhere wrong and silently
dropping durability would hide a real misconfiguration.

Nothing repairs, replaces or deletes the corrupt source. The gate's
forensic/salvage contract is untouched, and the test asserts the store bytes are
byte-identical after degrading.

VERIFIED
- End to end against a real fszero-codemode child on a deliberately corrupted
  40000-byte store: the session serves
  "read:6 bytes ref=fz://blob/5891b5b522d5df086d0ff0b110fbd9d21bb4fc7163af34d08286a2e846f6be03"
  and the corrupt file is still 40000 bytes afterwards.
- MUTATION-VERIFIED: removing the degrade arm reproduces
  "panicked at src/core/session.rs:222:25" and fails the test. With the arm,
  both tests pass.
- New tests/corrupt_store_degrades.rs: 2 passed. Also asserts the negative case
  (a healthy root must NOT report degraded), so the fix cannot pass by making
  every session ephemeral.
- Baseline, same tree, like with like: batch_ops, cas, cas_migration,
  child_root, fidelity, fz_ref_expand, index_producer and mcp_adapter fail
  identically with and without the change (1,1,2,5,3,4,1,1). No regressions.

ACCEPTANCE STATUS
1. A malformed store does not permanently brick the root - DONE. It starts
   ephemeral with a warning, which is the option the bead allowed.
2. Salvage surfaced with the exact promote command - NOT DONE. The message
   points at `fszero doctor` for the forensic and salvage paths, but there is
   still no one-line promote command.
3. Router surfaces the underlying cause - NOT DONE. The router still reports
   only "stdio MCP session worker is gone"; I had to run the child by hand to
   see the real error. This matters less now that the common case no longer
   kills the worker, but a genuinely fatal open is still opaque from the
   router.
4. Investigate the WRITE PATH - NOT DONE, and this is the important one. Three
   independent stores malformed on one machine points at how pages are written
   or flushed, not at hardware. This fix makes corruption survivable; it does
   NOT explain or prevent it.
5. Regression test - DONE.

Items 2, 3 and 4 remain. Refiled as zerostack-e3g so the root cause of the
corruption itself is not lost behind this mitigation.

title: Stop saturated TokenZero ref-index shards recompacting per append
description: Controlled 8-Luna read-only review wave on 2026-07-31 reproduced 98-100% TokenZero CodeMode CPU. Bounded evidence: `/tmp/zerostack-hj87-recurrence-20260731-064410/`. PIDs 27645 and 30818 were hot for 22-34s with no children. `sample` stacks spent 735-756/759-781 samples in `tokenzero_recovery::compact_ref_index_if_needed` via `RecoveryStore::persist`, serializing/writing ref-index entries. The live per-user index has 272 shards totaling 433,865,054 bytes; all 256 canonical two-hex shards exceed the 1MiB compaction threshold, so every append re-enters an O(shard) compaction that cannot shrink below threshold. There are also 374 retained interrupted temp files totaling 238,535,221 bytes; do not delete them without operator permission.
design: Move new writes to a finer-grained shard generation so hot shards remain below the compaction threshold. Preserve read compatibility with immutable legacy two-character shards, deduplicate across generations, and keep writes/compaction lock-bounded per new shard. Never perform an O(legacy-shard) rewrite on the request path. Add a saturated-index regression that proves append cost is bounded and legacy refs remain expandable. Existing temp evidence is retained.
acceptance_criteria: A bounded reproduction with legacy shards already above 1MiB performs new persists without scanning, serializing, or rewriting those saturated shards. Ref lookup and sticky expansion metadata remain correct across legacy and current shard generations. Concurrent append/lock tests pass. The controlled 8-Luna wave no longer drives TokenZero workers to sustained 40-139% CPU in ref-index compaction. RCH-targeted recovery and packaged CodeMode tests pass; hot-stack evidence no longer points at compact_ref_index_if_needed.
notes: Delivered root-cause fix across TokenZero commits e31302fe136e56b33242209ef210361ff456c9e1 and b8d81e30348c3133c77d1f5fe5ed755ff917d10b, both pushed to origin/main. New writes use 3-hex shards; immutable 2-hex legacy shards remain readable; lookup deduplicates both generations; sticky expansion metadata migrates once and remains cumulative on the exact valid source store, including a newer-stale-store regression. RCH `cargo test -p tokenzero-recovery ref_index -- --test-threads=1`: 10/10 passed. RCH packaged raw-worker conformance: 11/11 passed. Independent Luna and Sol review-resume loops ended ACCEPT. Non-vacuous controlled eight-Luna wave evidence `/tmp/tokenzero-hj87-e313-wave-v4-summary.json`: 180 samples/185.48s, 146 worker rows, 7 unique TokenZero PIDs, max CPU 27.1%, zero rows >=40%, zero consecutive hot samples. The previous `compact_ref_index_if_needed` 98-100% stacks did not recur. Active origin-main artifact refresh now verifies b8d81e3, SHA-256 d272706135549f66d47db53e3823a2f79bbb7224bb4d2d16637e68f7b82e870b.
close_reason: Fixed by TokenZero commits e31302f and b8d81e3. RCH ref index tests passed 10 of 10, packaged conformance passed 11 of 11, independent reviews accepted, and the eight Luna CPU wave passed with 146 rows and no hot samples.

title: declare canonical zero-ref line-clamp policy per dimension (two engine p1s wait on this)
description:
crates/zero-ref already implements the mechanism: LineEndPolicy::Strict and LineEndPolicy::ClampEnd, with select_fragment defaulting to Strict (crates/zero-ref/src/lib.rs, select_fragment at ~line 345, policy match at ~line 410).

What is missing is the contract decision about which policy is canonical for which dimension, and whether the capability descriptor must advertise it. Without that, engines diverge by default:
- TokenZero clamps (tokenzero-52gv, p1)
- shared strict selection errors with RangeOutOfBounds
- FSZero calls select_fragment_with_policy explicitly at src/core/zeroref.rs:40 (fszero-00vq, p1)

So the same ref over a short file can succeed in one engine and error in another, which is exactly the drift the shared crate exists to prevent.

Today the only hub-side mention is inside zerostack-b3l, a p2 wave-4 bead covering the per-dimension clamp policy vocabulary ({byte, line_start, line_end}, cf. FSZero b369c99). That is a priority inversion: two p1 engine beads are blocked on a p2 hub decision. This bead pulls the decision out of b3l so it can land independently of the capability-negotiation work.

Deliverables:
1. Decide and document canonical policy per dimension in the hub contract.
2. Encode it in zero-ref as the default, so engines cannot silently pick differently.
3. Extend the golden-vector fixture with clamp and strict cases at the boundary.
4. State whether the capability descriptor must advertise the policy, and if so add it to the conformance schema.

Unblocks: tokenzero-52gv, fszero-00vq.
notes: Implemented canonical v1 bounds policy: byte strict, line_start strict, line_end clamp. zero-ref defaults now encode ClampEnd; explicit strict APIs remain for validation. Fixture v2 includes canonical clamp and strict override boundary vectors. docs/zeroref.md states policy is fixed by ZeroRef v1 and not separately capability-negotiated. Verified on spark-1672 via rch: zero-ref 4/4 tests passed; clippy -D warnings passed; rustfmt and git diff --check passed. Independent review's versioning wording concern was fixed by clarifying this establishes the previously unspecified v1 default.
close_reason: Canonical ZeroRef bounds policy implemented and documented. Golden fixture v2 covers clamp and strict boundaries. Remote Spark tests and clippy pass.

title: aggregate codemode host rejects multi-action v2 plans: missing native host cell provenance
description: Repro 2026-07-29 (Fable session): any zero_execute plan with multiple awaited zero.token.shell calls (or one call with opts like timeout_ms) through the aggregate host errors: aggregate worker call is missing its native host cell provenance; apply the pinned pi-codex-conversion transport patch. Single-action v1 plans work. Likely introduced by 133ba38 (native aggregate codemode host). Impact: orchestrators forced into one-action-per-plan, defeating batching — directly against the ≤3-call force-multiplier target. Fix: aggregate host must propagate host cell provenance for every worker call in a plan, and shell opts must not strip it.
notes: CONFIRMED stale-build theory: the orchestrator session itself reproduced the exact error string 'apply the pinned pi-codex-conversion transport patch' (2026-07-30, zero_execute root=FSZero), which does not exist anywhere in pi-zerostack or ZeroStack source at HEAD (in-repo remediation says 'rebuild the ZeroStack CodeMode host and reload Pi'). Worker harness vs real binary: 8/8 cases missingProvenance:0, 27/27 tests, live v2 multi-action OK. Root cause: the long-running Pi orchestrator process has a stale/forked pi-zerostack transport module loaded. Remedy is external: reload the Pi session / rebuild host. No source defect at HEAD. Test gap filed separately: no positive-path test asserts multi-action plans deliver cellId to every delegate (only negative guard at raw-runtime.test.mjs:346).

(1) The reported error string 'apply the pinned pi-codex-conversion transport patch' does not exist in either repo; the only guard raising 'aggregate worker call is missing its native host cell provenance' is packages/pi-zerostack/raw-runtime.js:677 (added by deeaf16f496b05e6af5c6c53e056a1e6f999ec7e), whose remediation text reads 'rebuild the ZeroStack CodeMode host and reload Pi'. The reported suffix therefore came from a stale/forked transport build, not current source. (2) Provenance is bound per-cell, not per-call: code-mode-client.js:159 stores context {...context, cellId} once per cell; handleDelegate (code-mode-client.js:127-131) resolves cell by frame.cell_id and passes cell.context to every tool.invoke. The Rust host stamps cell_id on every delegate_request (zerostack-codemode-host.rs:274) from PendingDelegate.cell_id. There is no code path where action count, opts, or payload size can strip cellId. (3) Deterministic harness driving the real host binary target/release/zerostack-codemode-host with 8 cases (single-min, multi-2, opts timeout_ms, opts mode:raw, && chain, 200KB payload, mixed 5-action, parallel-3) reported missingProvenance=0 and FAILURES=0 for all. (4) Live v2 orchestrator plan with 4 awaited zero.token.shell calls including a && chain, {timeout_ms}, and a 5KB command succeeded. (5) Targeted tests green: node --test raw-runtime.test.mjs code-mode-client.test.mjs => 27/27 pass, including the existing cell_provenance_missing coverage at raw-runtime.test.mjs:346. Conclusion: no code fix applied (nothing to fix in-repo); the guard is correct and fires only when a caller invokes supervisor.invoke with aggregateExecutionId but no cellId, which the current transport never does. Most likely root cause of the live failure: the running Pi process had a stale CodeMode host binary / stale loaded pi-zerostack module - i.e. exactly what the in-repo remediation text says (rebuild host + reload Pi). Recommend the reporter capture the failing build's binary path + module path before closing. No repro harness committed (deleted after use); no source changes.

title: EPIC: Staged engine-MCP compatibility migration and removal gates
description:
DECISION
CodeMode is the only default and aggregate hot path. TokenZero engine MCP becomes explicit opt-in compatibility, maintenance-only. FSZero/GraphZero engine MCP remains unmarketed compatibility-only. An aggregate generic MCP transport may expose only zero_execute/zero_wait.

STAGES
Release N makes CodeMode default while preserving existing upgrades. N+1, no earlier than 90 days, moves engine adapters to explicit compatibility packages. Removal is no earlier than 180 days and two stable releases after that split, and remains a later owner-approved major-version decision.

NON-GOALS
No silent breakage and no feature parity promise.

## Acceptance Criteria
Policy is dated/versioned; defaults select CodeMode; compat warnings stay off protocol stdout; security/correctness fixes remain supported; removal requires complete supported-client migration matrix, 60 days without P0/P1 migration defects, corroborated low compat usage/support demand where opt-in data is sufficiently representative, a tested rollback package, major-release notice, and explicit owner approval. Telemetry alone cannot authorize removal.

Natural host for the four dependency-law migration gates (remove machine-permit / zero-cert / zero-gate from fs-zero, graphzero-query, tokenzero-codemode, tokenzero-mcp-compat normal graphs). Council plan names the removals but no bead carries them today.

Reuse jgm.5 as the migration carrier unless its active owner rejects scope after handoff. Remove zero-cert, zero-gate, and machine-permit from fs-zero normal dependencies; remove machine-permit from graphzero-query, tokenzero-codemode, and tokenzero-mcp-compat. tokenzero-engine may retain zero-gate/zero-ledger only as dev/test dependencies absent from release artifacts. Forbidden proof/gate/permit crates can leak into release artifacts through normal, transitive, feature-unified, build, example, or bench edges.

Remove zero-cert, zero-gate, and machine-permit from fs-zero normal dependencies; remove machine-permit from graphzero-query, tokenzero-codemode, and tokenzero-mcp-compat. tokenzero-engine may retain zero-gate/zero-ledger only as dev/test dependencies absent from release artifacts.

## Staged design

## Failure semantics
- Each rejected forbidden transitive dependency mutant is loud, typed, non-zero/non-promotable, and leaves no partial trusted result

- Each rejected boundary field loss mutant is loud, typed, non-zero/non-promotable, and leaves no partial trusted result
- Crash, timeout, unavailable native host, or verifier disagreement is NOT_RUN/FAILED, never inferred success
- Expandable evidence is retained for every failure; indeterminate state is reported without clamping or guesswork

## Residual risks
- Migration can change authorization semantics
- Cargo feature unification can reintroduce forbidden crates
- Prerequisite receipt or native-target skew can invalidate closure; the bead must remain open rather than weaken evidence

## Closure rule
Close only after every acceptance item passes and immutable receipts include every receipt_must_bind field; RCH is compilation evidence, never native evidence.

- No compatibility break beyond the frozen migration law.
- No global daemon, nested planner, or per-engine JS host.

title: store.sqlite3 corruption root cause: three independent stores malformed on one machine; salvage + router error reporting still missing
description:
Carries acceptance items 2, 3 and 4 of zerostack-byn, which was closed with a
mitigation only. cf387c6 makes a corrupt store survivable (the session degrades
to in-memory recovery instead of panicking); it does NOT explain why stores are
corrupting in the first place.

ITEM 4 IS THE IMPORTANT ONE - WHY ARE STORES CORRUPTING?

Observed on one machine in a single session:
  ~/AI/FSZero/.zerostack/fszero/store.sqlite3               malformed
  ~/AI/TokenZero/.zerostack/fszero/store.sqlite3            malformed
  ~/AI/TokenZero/.zerostack/tokenzero/.fszero/store.sqlite3 malformed
  ~/AI/TokenZero/.zerostack/fszero.corrupt-1784351118/      an EARLIER occurrence
all reporting `PRAGMA integrity_check` -> "database disk image is malformed (11)".

Three independent stores under different roots, plus a pre-existing .corrupt-
directory from a previous incident, is not plausibly hardware. It points at how
pages are written or flushed. Worth examining:
  - journal/WAL mode and synchronous pragma actually in effect
  - whether more than one process ever writes one store concurrently (note
    zerostack-uv0: multi-engine contention on a single root was real and is why
    the busy-retry exists)
  - crash/kill behavior: children are routinely SIGKILLed when a session ends
    or a router restarts, so an interrupted write must be recoverable
  - whether .zerostack stores ever live on a filesystem where locking is
    unreliable

A useful signal: the salvage copy the gate produced passes integrity_check
cleanly while the source does not, so the damage looks localized rather than
total, which is consistent with a torn or partially flushed write.

REMAINING SMALLER ITEMS

Item 2 - the verified-good salvage is still not offered to the operator with a
concrete promote command. The degrade message points at `fszero doctor`, but a
human still has to work out what to do with the salvage directory. Refusing to
auto-promote is correct (salvage can lose data); leaving the operator to figure
it out is not.

Item 3 - the router still reports only "stdio MCP session worker is gone" when
a store open fails fatally. Diagnosing the original incident required running
fszero-codemode by hand to see the real error. Less urgent now that the common
case degrades instead of killing the worker, but a genuinely fatal open is
still opaque from the router.

ACCEPTANCE
1. A documented explanation of how a store reaches "disk image is malformed",
   with a reproduction or a specific ruled-in cause.
2. Whatever the write path is doing unsafely is fixed, or the unsafe condition
   is prevented.
3. The verified-good salvage is surfaced with an exact promote command.
4. The router propagates the underlying store-open error instead of only
   "session worker is gone".
notes: Phase 1 (worker-opus forensics): NOT torn writes — pragmas already WAL+FULL. Root causes: fsqlite 0.1.18 leaks pages (page_count grows without freelist linkage -> 'Page N: never used' -> SQLite flags malformed) + unbounded per-PID forensic snapshots amplified one benign leak into 32GB. Phase 2 fix landed in FSZero 32397ed: (a) benign leaked pages self-heal via VACUUM under re-acquired lock + attestation, destructive findings still quarantine; (b) forensic dedupe by store fingerprint + MAX_SNAPSHOT_DESTINATIONS=3 cap + hardlinked packs; (c) typed GateError{Benign,Destructive,Busy,OpenFailed}, busy detection by rusqlite ErrorCode not string match, real reason reaches caller. Targeted tests green via RCH remote (14+2+2). Residuals filed separately: fsqlite writer bug itself NOT fixed (upstream fsqlite issue), 32GB operator cleanup pending. Reports: /tmp/racc_run/opus-e3g-fix.md
close_reason: Fixed in FSZero 32397ed (self-heal + snapshot cap + typed errors); fsqlite root-cause bug filed in FSZero repo (fsqlite-page-leak); 32GB cleanup tracked there too.

title: Recover stale CodeMode machine permits with actionable ownership
description: A bounded `zero_execute` session can leave the repository-wide heavy-operation permit held for minutes by a still-live worker while every later CodeMode call fails `machine_permit_busy`. The error identifies ownership only as `cm://exec/unknown`, exposes no cell/run/session identifier, and offers no safe status/interrupt/recovery path. This makes the sole execution surface globally unavailable and forced a native diagnostic fallback. 2026-07-31 evidence: `/tmp/zerostack-codemode-heavy-8a6d3b8d1b260a41.permit/slot-0` recorded PID 6313, repository `/Users/aditya/AI/ZeroStack`, command `tokenzero-codemode-heavy`; PID 6313 remained alive more than five minutes. The typed busy error said `held by live process(es) a cm://exec/unknown`. Multiple concurrent `zero_execute` callers could not identify or control the owner. Related CPU recurrence is tracked separately in `zerostack-hj87`.
design: Make machine permits lease/heartbeat-based and bind every owner to a durable CodeMode cell/run/session ref. On owner death or expired heartbeat, reclaim atomically without racing a live owner. Busy errors must report owner PID, repository, operation class, start/heartbeat time, and a usable status/control ref. Provide bounded status and owner-authorized interrupt/recovery through `zero_execute` or the aggregate host; never require deleting permit files or killing unknown processes. Ensure completed, failed, cancelled, and disconnected calls release permits exactly once.
acceptance_criteria: Reproduce a holder crash/disconnect and a live long-running holder. Dead/stale ownership is reclaimed within a bounded documented interval; live ownership is never stolen. Busy errors carry actionable PID/repository/age/session/cell metadata and a working status or authorized terminate route, never `cm://exec/unknown`. Unit/conformance tests cover normal release, crash, cancellation, owner death, PID reuse, stale heartbeat, concurrent reclaim, and host restart. A fresh `zero_execute` succeeds after each recovery without native tools or manual permit-file edits.

title: Kill ephemeral node resolution: ship a stable node/runtime resolution contract (no fnm multishell paths)
description: Hermes pinned node at /Users/aditya/.local/state/fnm_multishells/1347_1785364489620/bin/node (~/.hermes/config.yaml:138). That directory is a per-shell fnm multishell symlink keyed by pid+timestamp and disappears on reboot/new shell, so the integration silently dies. Earlier MCP attempt used a different node path (config.yaml.before-remove-zerostack-mcp-20260729-134709 mcp_servers.zerostack.command = .../fnm/node-versions/v24.14.1/...). ZeroStack must either (a) require no node at all for the aggregate path, or (b) resolve/bundle its own runtime and report it via `zerostack locate`, refusing ephemeral paths with a clear diagnostic. title: GraphZero declares mutation "store-only", a value the contract does not define
description:
Found by the first live conformance run after the harness was repaired (ZeroStack 2241b75). G7 limits and G8 mutation both FAIL against GraphZero for the same reason.

CONTRACT.md section 2 defines exactly three mutation values and pins gz:
  | GraphZero | gz | readonly |
  readonly: same rejection behavior as denied, and the substrate additionally
  declares that no mutating substrate operations exist in CodeMode. Read-only
  metadata/ref writes needed to store execution records are not domain mutation.

GraphZero declares a fourth value instead:
  crates/graphzero-query/src/codemode/discovery.rs:33   "mutation": "store-only"
  crates/graphzero-query/src/codemode/discovery.rs:129  "mutation_surface": "store-only"
  crates/graphzero-query/tests/codemode_e2e.rs:661      asserts "store-only"
with the inline rationale "remember/reserve/index mutate GraphZero's own store".

Both sides have a real argument:
- The contract's readonly clause already carves out "read-only metadata/ref writes needed to store execution records", but remember/reserve/index are more than execution bookkeeping; they are caller-initiated writes to GraphZero's store. Calling that readonly is arguably a lie.
- Equally, the contract is normative and enumerates three values. An engine unilaterally inventing a fourth is exactly the drift the conformance suite exists to catch, and any consumer switching on mutation will hit an unknown variant.

Note the vocabulary ALSO drifts inside GraphZero: the CodeMode surface says "store-only" (hyphen) while the operation ABI says "store_only" (underscore) at operation_abi/digest.rs:64 and operation_abi/vectors.rs:76. Whatever is decided, one spelling.

This needs a contract owner, not a guess. Two coherent resolutions:
A. Add store-only to CONTRACT.md section 2 as a fourth value with defined semantics (which operations may write, what a consumer must assume), repin gz to it, and update the conformance schema + harness validator. Pick one spelling.
B. Declare readonly is correct because GraphZero's writes are store-internal and not domain mutation, and change GraphZero to declare readonly.

Blocks a passing gz attestation, so it blocks zerostack-conformance-refresh-ci-30a deliverable 4 (reconcile the GraphZero closed-but-unproven state). Related: zerostack-hix.

title: GraphZero has a second canonical-JSON implementation off zero-abi
description:
Undetected drift, no bead in any repo before this one.

GraphZero/crates/graphzero-pack/src/manifest.rs:85 defines its own unsigned_canonical_json. GraphZero already re-exports zero_abi canonical JSON elsewhere (crates/graphzero-query/src/operation_abi/schema.rs re-exports zero_abi canonical_json, canonical_schema_json, normalize_schema, schema_diff, and digest.rs:53,58 call zero_abi contract_digest*), so this one function is a parallel implementation of the single most drift-forbidden primitive in the stack.

Canonical JSON feeds the contract digest. If the pack manifest hashes bytes that zero-abi would encode differently, pack manifests and contract digests disagree about identity, and the disagreement is silent because both sides produce valid-looking hashes.

Deliverables:
1. Confirm whether unsigned_canonical_json is byte-identical to zero_abi canonical_json today. Differential test over the zero-abi fixture corpus plus pack manifest fixtures.
2. If identical, delete it and call zero-abi.
3. If not identical, that is a live digest bug: record which manifests were hashed with the divergent encoder before replacing it.
4. Add a hub-side guard so a second canonical-JSON implementation cannot reappear unnoticed.

Related: tokenzero-hks0 (canonical-JSON digest hardening against zero-abi), tokenzero-ghv7 (contract digest depends on registry declaration order).
close_reason:
STALE - all four deliverables already landed. Verified by executing them against CURRENT code, not by reading commit messages.

D1 (confirm whether unsigned_canonical_json is byte-identical to zero_abi canonical_json, via differential test): DONE and the answer is NO, they diverge. GraphZero 41170ab 'test(pack): prove the canonical-JSON divergence against zero-abi' adds crates/graphzero-pack/tests/canonical_json_drift.rs with 4 tests: manifest_encoder_emits_declaration_order_not_sorted_order, the_two_encoders_disagree_on_bytes (asserts different bytes but semantically equal after reparse), the_two_encoders_produce_different_digests, manifest_encoding_is_deterministic_and_blanks_the_signature.

D2 (if identical, delete it): NOT APPLICABLE - D1 proved non-identity.

D3 (if not identical, that is a live digest bug; record which manifests were hashed with the divergent encoder before replacing it): correctly SPLIT OUT rather than done here, because replacing the encoder is digest- AND signature-invalidating: unsigned_canonical_json is both the digest input (digest_sha256) and the exact ed25519-signed payload (graphzero-pack/src/sign.rs:9 sign, :16 verify). That migration is zerostack-t76, which is open and carries the manifest-recording item plus the schema-version bump and the v1 verification policy. Closing 881 does not lose D3; t76 owns it.

D4 (hub-side guard so a second canonical-JSON implementation cannot reappear unnoticed): DONE. conformance/scripts/check_canonical_json_impls.py walks all four checkouts for functions matching a canonical/json name regex, allows only zero-abi paths plus test/bench-local normalizers, and carries an explicit KNOWN_EXCEPTIONS map with the ONE tracked divergence keyed to its bead (graphzero-pack/src/manifest.rs unsigned_canonical_json -> zerostack-t76). Wired into .github/workflows/ci.yml job 'drift-guards', which no-ops with ::warning when engine checkouts are absent rather than falsely passing.

MUTATION-VERIFIED (this session): planted /tmp/fakeengine/crates/foo/src/lib.rs containing 'fn my_canonical_json'. The guard FAILED with exit 1 and named the file and function. Baseline run over the real checkouts: exit 0, '1132 files, 1 tracked divergence(s), 0 new'. So the gate detects a new implementation and is not vacuously passing.

Note the bead's own ordering constraint is satisfied: t76 says 'do NOT start until deliverable 4 of the parent lands' - D4 has landed, so t76 is now unblocked.

No code changed by me; verified-and-closed. Tree clean apart from pre-existing .beads/issues.jsonl export churn.

comments.author: QuietSummit
comments.text:
Deliverable 1 DONE, and the answer is NO: the two encoders are not byte-identical.

Evidence: GraphZero 41170ab adds crates/graphzero-pack/tests/canonical_json_drift.rs, 4 tests, all passing on spark via rch.

Root cause is narrower than the bead assumed. unsigned_canonical_json (graphzero-pack/src/manifest.rs:85) is plain serde_json::to_string over #[derive(Serialize)] on UnsignedPackManifestRef, so it emits DECLARATION order. zero_abi::canonical_json (ZeroStack crates/zero-abi/src/schema.rs:33) emits SORTED keys recursively. Both produce valid JSON that parses to an equal Value; only a hashing consumer can see the difference. So this is deliverable 3 (a live digest divergence), NOT deliverable 2 (identical, safe to delete).

Blast radius, why I did NOT migrate in that commit: unsigned_canonical_json feeds digest_sha256 and is the exact payload ed25519-signed at sign.rs:9 and verified at sign.rs:16. Switching encoders changes every pack manifest digest AND invalidates every existing signature. That needs a recorded migration with a schema_version bump, not a drive-by.

Also note graphzero-pack did not depend on zero-abi at all (only graphzero-query did), which is how this went undetected. Added zero-abi as a dev-dependency so the gate exists without coupling the shipped crate.

Remaining: deliverable 3 (record which manifests were hashed with the divergent encoder) and deliverable 4 (hub-side guard against a third canonical-JSON impl). Filing those separately as migration work.

title: Add generation-fenced aggregate session lifecycle
description: Transfer Senpi's strongest architecture pattern into the canonical ZeroStack runtime without copying its Node/HTTP trust boundary. Senpi `SessionManagerProxy` uses a monotonically increasing generation, aborts and settles tracked executions before CAS replacement, disposes stale managers, and handles session start/shutdown/switch/fork. Its JavaScript kernel combines lazy persistent process reuse, a serial run queue, generation-fenced callbacks, and restart-after-interrupt. ZeroStack needs the equivalent in Rust across the full aggregate surface and pi-zerostack session hooks.
design: Add a generation-fenced `AggregateSession` in `zero-codemode`, shared by session sidecar and direct frontends. Beginning replacement atomically stops admission, increments generation, cancels every tracked plan, waits for all settlements under a deadline, disposes the old host/workers, and installs the next only if its generation still matches. Every callback/result carries generation + request id; stale events are discarded with typed audit evidence. Keep host/worker processes warm but create/reset the QuickJS realm per plan so mutable globals do not leak across calls. Serialize operations that mutate shared engine/session state; allow only explicitly bounded independent work; cap queue length and return typed backpressure. Integrate start/shutdown/before-switch/before-fork hooks, while OS owner-death remains authoritative. Never fail open to inline execution if worker spawn/sandbox initialization fails.
acceptance_criteria: Race/property tests cover overlapping replacements, start vs shutdown, switch/fork during plan, cancel vs result, timeout vs crash, worker revision change, stale callback, and owner death. Exactly-once settlement holds and no old generation can mutate, publish a ref, emit output, or revive after replacement. Admission and queue bounds are enforced with typed retry guidance; threads/FDs/processes remain stable across 10,000 replacements/calls. Process reuse improves warm latency without preserving QuickJS user globals between model-visible plans. Session close meets zerostack-q6am teardown gates. Differential fixtures prove byte/ref/error/receipt parity through session sidecar and pi-zerostack. Injected stale-generation, unbounded-queue, inline-fallback, and orphan mutants fail tests.
notes: Source inspiration pinned at Senpi 6951fba: `packages/senpi-codemode/src/extension/session-manager-proxy.ts`, `src/index.ts`, `kernels/js/context-manager.ts`, and `kernels/js/run-queue.ts`. Reimplement the pattern under MIT attribution as needed; do not import Node worker_threads, loopback HTTP, host tool callbacks, persistent mutable VM state, or inline fallback. Parent: zerostack-q6am.

title: EPIC: harness-agnostic distribution — engine-first, adapters for MCP / CLI / Claude Code / Pi
description:
Everything ships open source and must work outside Pi for users on stock vendor plans/apps. The Rust engines and canonical `zerostack-codemode-host` are the product; Pi, Claude Code, Codex, ZCode/GLM, Kimi Code, Grok Build, MCP, and plain shell are thin adapters. Product requirement: one model-visible aggregate CodeMode call, not N raw filesystem/shell tools, with exact refs, measured compression, typed failure/cancellation, and no harness-private paths. Current local evidence (2026-07-31): Claude Code 2.1.220, Codex 0.145.0, ZCode 3.6.4, Kimi Code 0.29.2, and Grok Build 0.2.117 all expose skills/hooks/plugins or shell execution, but their plugin manifests expose no general native local custom-tool ABI; Codex/ZCode plugin manifests use skills/apps and optional `mcpServers`, while Kimi/Grok/Claude can invoke stable CLI commands. Therefore the program uses a non-MCP core plus universal shell adapter and an optional one-tool MCP edge only where a vendor requires it for a first-class named tool.

Existing adapter distribution train; amend to carry the P1 thin-adapter audit gate. Pi-specific P1 tracking bead lives in the adapter repo per council section 6.

Reuse 59ra as the P1 carrier. Audit the harness-agnostic distribution train and thin pi-zerostack adapter after engine gates. The adapter composes planner-free workers and imports no engine crate. Packaging can pull planners, policy, forbidden dependencies, or daemons into the thin aggregate adapter even when source layout looks correct.
design:
Four tiers share one contract and one session lifecycle. Tier 0: an invisible `zerostack-session` sidecar is owned by exactly one vendor agent/app session, prewarms the canonical aggregate host/workers, exposes the full `zero.fs`/`zero.graph`/`zero.token` CodeMode surface on a private socket, blocks idle, and dies with the owner process; there is no global daemon. Tier 1: tiny Rust `zsx` sends one aggregate JS plan to that session socket, so shell-capable apps need one built-in Bash/terminal call without MCP. Tier 2: optional slim MCP edge advertises exactly one deferred-schema `zero_execute` tool, owns the same session process tree, and forwards bytes unchanged; it has no planner, engine, store, or ref logic. Tier 3: SDK-native wrappers call the same client library where a vendor actually offers custom-tool registration. Generate adapters and lifecycle hooks from one manifest for Claude, Codex, ZCode, Kimi, Grok, Pi, and plain shell. Static recipes reduce quoting while arbitrary `zsx exec` preserves CodeMode. Durable workspace refs outlive the process without any resident service. Never fork vendor binaries, proxy provider APIs, expose three public engine selectors, or duplicate JS hosts.

## Scope in
- Reuse 59ra as the P1 carrier. Audit the harness-agnostic distribution train and thin pi-zerostack adapter after engine gates. The adapter composes planner-free workers and imports no engine crate.
- Implement only the named contract, fixtures, verifiers, and receipts needed by this bead
- Preserve all protected-owner carrier constraints and machine-readable dependencies

## Scope out
- Engine planner rewrites
- Per-engine JS hosts
- Carrier mutation before owner approval

## Anchors
- carrier [unresolved-alias-removed] only after protected-owner handoff
- pi-zerostack manifests/install hooks/package archives
- zero-codemode/raw-worker v2 boundary and ADR comparison

## Staged design
- Record owner handoff and freeze allowed surface
- Build/package targeted artifacts through RCH
- Inspect archive contents, dependency graph, and binary linkage
- Run aggregate typed-failure and owner-death smoke
- Emit bill of materials and thin-adapter receipt

## Compatibility and migration law
- Aggregate zero.fs/graph/token API remains unchanged
- raw-worker v2 skew remains fail-closed
- No daemon or store layout is introduced
acceptance_criteria:
A clean-machine install provides `zerostack integrate {claude,codex,zcode,kimi,grok,pi,all}` plus doctor/uninstall. Each CLI/app session silently owns one bounded aggregate sidecar and completes search/read/impact/edit/verify in one model-visible call through either built-in terminal or optional one-tool edge. There is no user-global resident ZeroStack process. Warm calls meet p50 <=1ms/p95 <=2ms with separately measured client/edge overhead; skills add <=500 prompt tokens and edge schema <=250. Thirty-minute idle, 10,000-call leak, hard CPU/RSS/FD/thread/backpressure, and owner-death tests satisfy zerostack-q6am. Normal close, crash, SIGKILL, terminal loss, and update leave no worker/socket/orphan. Cross-harness fixtures prove byte/ref/error/cancel/approval/accounting parity, stable root/store isolation, app/CLI config discovery, rollback, and zero hardcoded paths. Live current-version smokes record calls, provider tokens/cost, local latency, process-tree resources, and teardown time. MCP remains optional and removable without changing the core.
- Dependencies are machine-readable
- Receipts bind all frozen receipt fields
- Targeted RCH checks pass
- Native claims require native hosts; cross-compilation does not count
- No engine crate appears in normal/release dependency graph
- All three raw-worker boundaries pass parity vectors
- One aggregate CodeMode endpoint remains
- Session process tree meets lifecycle/resource gates inherited from q6am
- Distribution artifacts bind the assembly manifest
- Every required receipt binds exact source heads, assembly, toolchains, commands, fixtures, outputs, mutants, platform profile, result, and residual assumptions
- Negative, crash, skew, or mutant evidence returns the documented typed failure and can never count as a pass
- RCH output is compilation/test evidence only; native, filesystem, crash, performance, and packaging claims require preregistered native execution
notes:
Operator decisions: hybrid one-tool edge (mem_01KYVCEPT6EY8BRZG3ZW6AFTNJ), then corrected lifecycle to invisible session-owned sidecar, never global daemon (mem_01KYVCXGHBEDGB8YY90XN27WKX). Existing private skills prove shell reachability but per-engine `zs`, path pins, and deny/retry hooks are transitional and must be removed.

- rch exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/rch_target_zerostack_p1 cargo test -p zero-testkit packaging -- --test-threads=1

}

## Proof receipt

  "immutability": "Hash canonical receipt bytes and referenced fixtures/artifacts. Corrections create a successor; promoted receipts are never rewritten.",

  ],

  ]
}

## Failure semantics
- Each rejected engine import mutant is loud, typed, non-zero/non-promotable, and leaves no partial trusted result
- Each rejected nested planner mutant is loud, typed, non-zero/non-promotable, and leaves no partial trusted result
- Each rejected second JS host mutant is loud, typed, non-zero/non-promotable, and leaves no partial trusted result

title: conformance harness must test ONE installed surface, not a dual-surface binary
description:
The conformance harness cannot run against ANY current engine. This is worse than the staleness recorded in zerostack-conformance-refresh-ci-30a: the suite is not merely out of date, its core process model contradicts what all three engines now enforce.

HARNESS ASSUMPTION (conformance/src/lib.rs):
  :885  McpClient::spawn(bin, mode, timeout) runs Command::new(bin).arg("--mode={mode}")
  :477  check_exposure spawns ONE binary as --mode=codemode
  :487  ...then spawns the SAME binary as --mode=mcp
  G1 "exposure" is defined as: the codemode surface exposes exactly the codemode tools, AND the mcp surface exposes none of them. That check is only meaningful if one artifact can serve both.

ENGINE REALITY (verified by direct invocation, 2026-07-25, all three release binaries):

  TokenZero target/release/tokenzero-mcp --mode=codemode
    exit 101: "artifact is locked to surface 'mcp'; refused --mode=codemode.
    Install tokenzero-codemode for the CodeMode catalog (mutually exclusive)."

  FSZero target/release/fszero --mode=codemode
    exit 2: "packaging shim has no surface runtime compiled in. Install fszero-mcp
    or fszero-codemode (selection is immutable), or invoke that artifact directly.
    Do not pass --mode= to a dual-capable process - dual surfaces are forbidden."

  GraphZero target/release/graphzero --mode=codemode
    exit 1: "the compatibility shim does not host MCP/CodeMode servers. Install
    graphzero-codemode (selected surface) or rebuild the matching single-surface artifact."

TokenZero enforces this at COMPILE time, not just runtime: building --features "surface-mcp,surface-codemode" hits
  compile_error!("tokenzero surfaces are mutually exclusive (tokenzero-irx9.3): enable exactly one of feature surface-mcp or surface-codemode - never both.")
So a dual-surface tokenzero artifact cannot be produced at all. The harness's G1 is unsatisfiable by construction.

This explains why the reports froze on 2026-07-01: that is approximately when single-surface artifacts landed, and nobody could run the suite afterward. The 23 committed reports attest to a binary shape that no longer exists.

REQUIRED CHANGE:
RunConfig must take a surface pair, not one path. Suggested:
  --codemode-bin <path> --mcp-bin <path>
with --bin kept as a back-compat alias meaning "same artifact for both", which is now only true for test fixtures like the built-in fake substrate.

G1 exposure then becomes a cross-ARTIFACT check: the codemode artifact exposes exactly the codemode tool set, and the mcp artifact exposes none of it. That is the same invariant the check was always trying to express, and it stays meaningful under single-surface packaging. It arguably gets STRONGER, since surface separation is now enforced by the build rather than by a runtime flag.

Also fix while in here (found during the same investigation):
- Reports record substrate_binary as an absolute authoring-machine path, e.g. "/Users/<name>/AI/tokenzero/target/release/tokenzero". That is a local-layout leak in a public repo. Record basenames. Overlaps zerostack-9g4.
- ReportFile has no engine revision field, so no report can be tied to the code it attests to. Contract and checker for this already landed: conformance/reports/ATTESTATION.md and conformance/scripts/check_freshness.py.

BLOCKS: zerostack-conformance-refresh-ci-30a deliverable 1 (re-run the suite against current engine HEADs). 30a deliverables 2 and 3 (CI wiring, freshness contract) are already done and do not depend on this.
close_reason: Fixed and pushed as a25c523. Harness now models one artifact + one Surface (bin/surface), infers surface from filename, refuses to guess on the bare shim, and G1 checks that the artifact serves its own surface AND refuses the opposite. G2-G10 only run against a codemode artifact. Verified against installed graphzero-codemode: G1 now PASSES (previously failed only because the harness demanded a second artifact that must not exist); G4/G5/G10 pass; remaining failures are the real contract divergences tracked as mpi and g25. Workspace fmt+clippy -D warnings+tests green.

comments.author: QuietSummit
comments.text:
Harness now runs against real engines (ZeroStack 2241b75). First live gz run produced ACTIONABLE findings, and they point at the HARNESS being wrong, not the engine.

G2/G6 "invalid CodeMode ref": GraphZero emits
  gz://codemode/execution/cm___exec_1784970306329-20532-0-2afa6c5e5632
The harness ref regex (conformance/src/lib.rs:64) is
  ^{ns}://(blob/[0-9a-f]{64}|codemode/execution/[^/]+/(code|steps|telemetry|result|error))$
which REQUIRES a trailing /code|/steps|/telemetry|/result|/error segment. The bare execution root ref has no suffix and cannot match. GraphZero also emits all four suffixed refs alongside it, so the engine looks correct and the regex looks too strict. Needs a contract decision: is the bare execution root a legal ref? If yes, make the suffix optional.

G5 errors, G10 sandbox: harness reports "case did not return structured error", but the payloads clearly ARE structured, with correct kinds:
  validation -> kind "validation"
  sandbox    -> kind "sandbox"   ("network/fetch denied")
  runtime    -> kind "runtime"
  substrate  -> kind "substrate"
  policy     -> kind "policy"    ("CodeMode is read-only; mutating JS binding 'edit' is unavailable")
Every one carries isError true, structuredContent.error.{kind,message,retryable}, and error_ref. So extract_json_payload is failing to find them. GraphZero wraps them in a content[] entry of type "structuredContent" AND repeats them at top-level structuredContent; the harness likely only looks at content[0].text and tries to parse it as JSON, but content[0].text here is the human-readable ack line, not JSON. Harness bug.

G7 limits: "invalid mutation \"store-only\"". CONTRACT.md section 2 admits only allowed|denied|readonly, and pins gz to readonly. GraphZero declares store-only. This one may be a real engine or contract divergence: either GraphZero should declare readonly, or the contract needs a fourth value defined. Do not guess, needs a decision.

G1 exposure: "server exited while waiting for initialize response" for the mcp side. graphzero (the shim) is not the mcp-surface artifact; there is probably a graphzero-mcp that was not built. Need the right artifact before G1 means anything.

Recommend splitting: harness ref-regex + payload-extraction fixes are one bead, the mutation vocabulary question is another, since the second needs a contract owner.

comments.author: QuietSummit
comments.text:
CORRECTION. My first fix was also wrong, in the same direction as the original bug.

I replaced "one binary, two --mode= spawns" with "--codemode-bin plus --mcp-bin", i.e. two artifacts present at once. That still assumes both surfaces exist side by side. They do not. The product rule is EITHER/OR at INSTALL time:

  crates/tokenzero-install/src/packaging.rs:3
    "Product rule: users install **one** of tokenzero-mcp or tokenzero-codemode
     from the same revision and shared core. The installer writes one client
     registration and replaces any prior surface. Dual catalog / dual mode
     startup fails closed."
  packaging.rs:13
    "The tokenzero name is a compatibility shim / selected symlink only -
     never a dual-surface binary."

So you install ONE surface. Requiring both artifacts describes a machine state that is not allowed to exist, and on a normally-installed host the second path simply is not there. My version would have failed for the wrong reason.

Correct model, now implemented:
  RunConfig { bin, surface }        one artifact, one surface
  --bin <path> --surface codemode|mcp
  surface inferred from the filename (<name>-codemode / <name>-mcp) so the
  common case needs no flag. The bare shim is NOT guessed: it is a selected
  symlink, so an unrecognizable name is a hard error rather than a default,
  because silently running the wrong surface's checks yields misleading
  evidence.

G1 exposure is now a property of the ONE artifact under test, checked two ways:
  1. it serves the tool set its surface implies (codemode artifact exposes
     exactly the codemode tools; mcp artifact exposes none of them), and
  2. it REFUSES the opposite surface. A single-surface artifact that also
     answers as its opposite is precisely the dual catalog the product rule
     forbids, so serving it is the failure and refusing it is the pass.
That second half is the invariant that actually protects the separation, and neither the original harness nor my first fix tested it.

G2-G10 exercise CodeMode execution semantics, so they now only run against a codemode artifact. Against an mcp artifact there is no execute_code to drive; reporting those as failures was a category error.

VERIFIED against the installed gz codemode artifact:
  bin: graphzero-codemode
  G1 exposure PASS      <- was FAIL "server exited while waiting for initialize"
  G4 leak-proof PASS
  G5 errors PASS
  G10 sandbox-denial PASS
  G2/G3/G6/G9 FAIL -> zerostack-mpi (no execution_id, no inline telemetry)
  G7/G8 FAIL       -> zerostack-g25 (mutation "store-only")
G1 was only ever failing because the harness insisted on a second artifact that must not exist. The remaining failures are the real contract divergences, unchanged.

Also verified the shim refuses to be guessed:
  --bin .../graphzero
  -> Error: cannot tell which surface "graphzero" serves; pass --surface codemode or --surface mcp

title: Prevent runaway TokenZero CodeMode and xtask CPU
description: Operator observed `tokenzero-codemode` and likely `tokenzero-xtask` at roughly 100% CPU. Current sample is intermittent, not active: at 20:12 the aggregate host and TokenZero worker were 0.0% CPU, load averages 2.43/2.96/3.09. Existing watchdog PID 841 only matches argv[0] `tokenzero` or `*/tokenzero`; it explicitly ignores `tokenzero-codemode` and `tokenzero-xtask`, so it cannot detect the reported processes. Capture parent/command/stack during recurrence and fix lifecycle or busy-loop root cause rather than merely killing workers.
design: Instrument exact host/worker process lineage, stacks, wakeups, active request/generation, queue depth, and CPU/RSS. Reproduce idle stdio wait, EOF, cancel, timeout, aborted plans, stale callbacks, worker reuse/reaping, and xtask completion. Replace polling/spin with blocking kernel primitives and generation-fenced cancellation/settlement. Bound queues and process trees before adding any watchdog. Extend watchdog coverage only as a final fail-safe after safe exact-name matching and sustained-window behavior are proven; healthy short active work must never be killed. Senpi's generation CAS, serial queue, and exactly-once settlement are reference patterns, not its Node/HTTP topology.
acceptance_criteria: Root cause the observed `fszero-codemode`/`tokenzero-codemode` 40-139% CPU recurrence; do not merely extend a killer watchdog. A bounded reproduction captures parent lineage, command, stacks, wakeups, and current operation while hot. After the fix, each host/worker blocks idle: a 30-minute process-tree soak has average CPU <0.1%, p99 sampled CPU <1%, stable threads/FDs/RSS, and no timer/busy loop. Completed/cancelled/timed-out/crashed/session-closed calls leave no orphan within 1s p95. Active CPU is attributable to bounded requested work; injected spin, runaway child, cancellation loss, and owner death trip hard controls. Coverage includes approved codemode/xtask executable names without killing healthy short work. This gate must pass before zerostack-q6am session-sidecar rollout.
notes:

Existing watchdog source still matches only `tokenzero|*/tokenzero`, excluding both recurring `tokenzero-codemode` and `tokenzero-xtask`.

Second recurrence 2026-07-31 around 03:31 local during bounded tau2 review/revision work. Native diagnostic was required after `zero_execute` became unavailable with `machine_permit_busy`, owner reported only as `cm://exec/unknown`. Process sample showed `tokenzero-codemode` PIDs 15155 and 80301 at about 95.7% and 95.8%, `fszero-codemode` PID 78013 at 99.7%, and another token worker PID 56725 at 80.1%. Permit metadata named owner PID 6313, parent Pi PID 79527, repository `/Users/aditya/AI/ZeroStack`, command `tokenzero-codemode-heavy`; that worker was still alive after more than five minutes while the global CodeMode permit remained unavailable. title: apply the beads-export scrub and privacy gates to TokenZero, FSZero, and GraphZero
description:
Follow-up to zerostack-sg3, which built and proved the shared scrub but deliberately applied it only to the hub.

scripts/scrub_beads_export.py in the hub (ZeroStack eb2b7b7) works cross-repo. Run from the hub against each engine's export it reports:
  TokenZero  248 record(s) carry absolute host paths
  FSZero     310 record(s)
  GraphZero  846 record(s)

All three .beads/issues.jsonl files are tracked, and TokenZero is public, so this is the same exposure as the hub had: username and directory layout on every issue record via br's source_repo_path stamp, plus absolute paths quoted in descriptions and comments.

WHY THIS WAS NOT DONE IN THE SAME PASS
Scrubbing rewrites 248/310/846 records, which is a very large diff in each repo. At the time of filing, other sessions had substantial uncommitted work in those trees (I lost my own uncommitted TokenZero edits to a concurrent operation earlier in this session, see the note on zerostack-wth). Landing a whole-file rewrite of a tracked, actively-synced file underneath another agent is a good way to cause a conflict or destroy work. It should be done when those trees are quiet.

DELIVERABLES
1. Run the scrub in TokenZero, FSZero, and GraphZero, one commit per repo, when the tree is quiet and the other sessions have committed.
2. Verify integrity the same way the hub was verified, and do not skip this: record count unchanged, id order unchanged, per-record key sets unchanged, and only source_repo_path, description, and comments differing. The hub check caught nothing wrong, but a silent field loss across 846 records would be very hard to notice later.
3. Copy or reference the two gates into each engine repo's CI, since a scrub with no gate will simply rot the moment the next br sync runs. The hub runs both check_no_host_paths.py and scrub_beads_export.py --check in a privacy job.
4. Add the scrub to each repo's documented br sync recipe, as was done in the hub AGENTS.md, so it is a required step rather than folklore.

Note the ordering constraint: the scrub must run AFTER br sync --flush-only and BEFORE git add, because br rewrites the export from SQLite on every sync and will reintroduce the absolute path each time. A one-time scrub without the recipe change and the CI gate accomplishes nothing durable.

Decide whether to vendor a copy of the script per repo or reference the hub copy. A copy per repo is more robust, since the engine repos should not require a hub checkout to pass their own CI, but then the four copies must be kept in sync.

Refs zerostack-sg3, zerostack-9g4.

title: artifact cleanup can delete the active CodeMode backend and take zero.token offline
description: Observed live 2026-07-25 while following the requirement to periodically clear stale build artifacts. Removing <home>/AI/TokenZero/target also removed target/release/tokenzero, which the active pi-zerostack CodeMode session was using as its zero.token backend. backend_status immediately reported tokenzero:null; subsequent zero.token ref expansion failed with env path missing. The separately installed ~/.tokenzero/bin/tokenzero remained healthy, so this is backend lifecycle coupling, not source corruption. Deliverables: (1) active backend binaries must live in a protected origin-main runtime directory, never a developer target dir eligible for cleanup; (2) cleanup tooling must detect and refuse active backend paths; (3) backend_status should report the configured path and remediation; (4) regression smoke removes a repo target tree and proves zero.token remains live; (5) document safe stale-artifact cleanup. Recovery today is push origin/main and await backend rebuild.
notes: Investigation refined root cause. The origin-main TokenZero binary is healthy and zero.token shell self-recovered, but backend_status still reports tokenzero:null because router/index.js reads the legacy shared/paths.js TOKENZERO developer-target constant instead of SUBSTRATES.token.binary(). Ref expansion also calls the legacy TOKENZERO constant in router/lib/refs.js, producing ref_not_found env errors after developer target cleanup even while the managed CodeMode child is healthy. Canonical source is currently only in unversioned <home>/Developer/pi-stack/packages/pi-zerostack and <home>/Developer/omp-extensions/omp-backend-router; no pi-zerostack git repo or origin exists, so a durable separate commit cannot be shipped from the four requested repos. Required fix: inject SUBSTRATES.token.binary into createRefHelpers and derive backend_status paths from SUBSTRATES. Reopened until canonical extension ownership is available.
close_reason: Root cause was binary-resolution precedence in the pi-zerostack extension: shared/paths.js ranked ~/AI/<repo>/target/release ahead of protected install prefixes, so the active CodeMode backend routinely resolved into a cleanup-eligible developer artifact tree. Pruning that tree deleted the running binary. Confirmed live before the fix: backend_status reported fszero=~/AI/FSZero/target/release/fszero and gzero=~/AI/graphzero/target/release/graphzero. Fixed in ~/Developer/pi-stack commit f81ba36: (1) backendBinaryCandidates() puts protected prefixes (~/.tokenzero/bin, ~/.fszero/bin, ~/.graphzero/bin, ~/.local/bin) first, developer targets remain a from-source fallback; (2) backend_status now reports artifact_cleanup_safety naming any backend still in target/ plus remediation, so pruning is a checked operation; (3) README documents the safe prune sequence. Verified: all four backends now resolve to protected paths (~/.tokenzero/bin/tokenzero, ~/.local/bin/fszero, ~/.local/bin/graphzero); new router/test/backend-paths.test.mjs reproduces the exact incident (create both binaries, rm -rf the target tree, assert the resolved backend is unchanged and still exists) and covers both branches of the safety report; mutation-testing both the candidate ordering and the safety filter turns the suite red; full pi-zerostack suite 169/169. pi-stack is a git repo so this is durably committed.

title: shell repo-inventory heuristic mangles compound commands, shredding file content into sample_paths
description:
Hit repeatedly while doing conformance work on 2026-07-25. Not a blocker, but it costs a wasted round trip almost every time and will do the same to every future agent.

zero.token.shell wraps some commands in a "structured (repo inventory command)" policy that reformats output into a repo_inventory block with files_seen/dirs_seen/sample_paths. That is useful for a bare ls. It is actively wrong when the command is a compound shell line whose real payload is on stdout.

Concrete case:
  zero.token.shell("ls /tmp/qs/probe-reports/ && cat /tmp/qs/probe-reports/$(ls ... | head -1)")
The heuristic saw a leading ls, classified the whole thing as repo inventory, and then rendered the JSON report I actually wanted as "sample_paths" entries, one array element per LINE of JSON:
  - gz-2026-07-25-050508.json
  - "contract_version": "1.0",
  - "invalid CodeMode ref \"gz://...\"",
  - "name": "ctx.step",
So the file content was shredded into a path list. Every line got treated as a filesystem path. I had to re-fetch via the combined_ref to read it.

Second case, same root cause: an ls of two paths where the second does not exist returns exit 1 and the stderr line
  ls: /path: No such file or directory
appears as a sample_paths ENTRY, alongside real -rwxr-xr-x lines. A consumer parsing sample_paths as paths gets an error message as a path.

Suggested fix, roughly in order of value:
1. Only apply the inventory policy when the command is a SINGLE listing command with no &&, ||, ;, or | and no command substitution. A compound line should fall through to plain capture.
2. Never route stderr into sample_paths. Inventory is a stdout concept.
3. When the policy is applied, still make the raw stdout trivially reachable; today combined_ref works but it is a second round trip that the caller did not know they needed until they saw mangled output.

Impact is mild but constant: it silently corrupts the shape of data you asked for, and it does so most often when an agent is reading evidence files, which is exactly when fidelity matters. Filed rather than worked around, per the standing instruction to report ZeroStack problems as beads.

Bare single listings are still classified as inventory as intended. Fixed in TokenZero 7bada5e.

title: Scale arbitrary aggregate plans at engine-work speed
description: P0 aggregate-throughput invariant: CodeMode must not impose a hardcoded operation count. One model-visible `zero_execute` may contain any bounded DAG of finds, reads, graph queries, token operations, multi-file snap edits, verification, loops, and reductions. It executes locally until the declared deadline/resource budget, keeping intermediate bytes out of model context. Runtime overhead should be nearly fixed plus actual engine/durability work, not N repeated model turns or N process/schema/render/fsync taxes. The former 1,000-operation case remains one regression point, not a product limit.
design: Add an aggregate action-tape/dataflow fast path beneath QuickJS. Queue and fuse independent connector promises; coalesce by surface/root/snapshot; vectorize through raw-worker v2; share catalog/root/store/index resolution; batch framing, schema validation, telemetry, ref publication, and durability only where semantics permit; preserve dependency barriers for dynamic outputs. Keep arbitrary JS loops/branches available. Use bounded streaming chunks and backpressure so plans scale past memory-sized batches without a static operation ceiling. Multi-file edits resolve snap targets together, validate every preimage, write one crash-recoverable aggregate journal transaction/certificate, commit deterministically, and verify all files; ambiguous/stale targets fail before mutation. Finalize once into compact aggregates/CAS refs, never N raw outputs. Instrument fixed runtime overhead, incremental overhead per logical op, engine/durability work, queue depth, fusion ratio, peak resources, and first saturation cause.
acceptance_criteria: No API/schema/runtime constant imposes a maximum logical-operation count; limits are explicit deadline, CPU, memory, output, concurrency, and authorization budgets with typed yield/ref or failure. Provenance-pinned scale curves run 1/10/100/1,000/10,000/100,000 operations, plus the largest safe point, across independent reads/finds, mixed FS/graph/token DAGs, sequential dependencies, reductions, and multi-file snap-edit/verify. Aggregate runtime overhead excluding measured engine/durability/network work targets fixed p95 <=2ms plus p95 <=10us per logical op; fusion reports honest logical ops and physical passes. The 1,000 bounded regression corpus remains hard <1,000ms, with vectorizable p50 <=100ms/p95 <=250ms and sequential p50 <=250ms/p95 <=500ms. A one-call 100-file edit fixture journals, commits, verifies, and returns one compact certificate/ref with no partial success after crash. Output stays <=2,000 visible tokens regardless of N. Cancellation/backpressure prevents heat or ballooning; repeated scale runs leave no resource tail. Injected per-op spawn/fsync/render, O(N^2) path, lost/reordered op, partial multi-file commit, output escape, and hidden model call fail gates.
notes: Parent zerostack-me51; pair with snap-edit zerostack-tj5c and finalization zerostack-24nv. Operation count is not a capability limit. The 1,000 case is only a concrete benchmark. Performance is expressed as fixed/incremental runtime overhead plus honest engine, durability, network, and requested-work cost.

title: Reduce warm FSZero child round trip to 1ms
description: Child of zerostack-me51. A warmed direct FSZero CodeMode child round trip is p50=12.04ms, p95=13.74ms, p99=16.22ms while the in-sandbox engine operation is p50=0ms/p95=1ms. The missing ~12ms is transport/finalization outside the operation. Identify exact costs in framing, stdio, JSON encode/decode, CAS/ref finalization, SQLite/journal work, and wake scheduling, then make the warmed child path 1ms-class.
design: Instrument both sides with monotonic nanosecond spans and a no-op/ping control. Preserve the planner-free worker contract. Evaluate binary framing, preallocated buffers, zero-copy payloads, persistent Unix-domain/shared-memory channels, batched or deferred noncritical finalization, and embedding the shared worker adapter where safe. Durability-critical publication remains crash-safe; derived diagnostic artifacts may not impose synchronous barriers. Reuse zerostack-tau2 shared adapter work rather than creating another protocol.
acceptance_criteria: Over 1,000 isolated warmed direct child reads, total child round trip is p50 <=1.0ms and p95 <=2.0ms; engine execution remains p95 <=1.0ms and measured transport/finalization stages close to the total within 0.25ms. Cold handshake is separate. Byte/ref/error outputs, worker protocol digest checks, cancellation, crash recovery, store isolation, and durable expansion remain identical; an injected +1ms transport delay fails the gate.

title: zero.token.shell response schema differs single-surface (text/stdout_ref) vs cross-surface (visible/result) - plans cannot read stdout portably
description:
zero.token.shell() returns two DIFFERENT, incompatible response schemas depending on whether the plan is routed single-surface (Rust sandbox) or cross-surface (QuickJS sidecar). Plan code cannot read stdout portably.

Verified at HEAD 355a7b7.

SHAPE A - single-surface (plan touches ONLY TokenZero):
  keys: combined_ref,exit_code,raw_tokens,status,stdout_ref,success,text,visible_tokens
  stdout is in  r.text ;  r.visible is undefined

SHAPE B - cross-surface (plan also touches FSZero/GraphZero):
  keys: accounting,content_type,mode,op,ref,refs,result,status,tool_response,visible
  stdout is in  r.visible / r.result ;  r.text is undefined
  ALSO: no stdout_ref / combined_ref at top level (only ref/refs), and some
  responses additionally carry a _zerostack provenance key while others do not.

REPRO (single plan, proves the switch):
  const a = await zero.token.shell('echo X', {cwd:'.'});          // Shape A
  await zero.fs.compound('list',{path:'crates'});                 // forces cross-surface
  const b = await zero.token.shell('echo CROSS', {cwd:'.'});      // Shape B
  return {aHasText:'text' in a, aHasVisible:'visible' in a,
          bHasText:'text' in b, bHasVisible:'visible' in b};
  => {aHasText:true, aHasVisible:false, bHasText:false, bHasVisible:true}

IMPACT: this is a live foot-gun, not theoretical. It broke my own plans twice during
this run with "cannot read property 'split' of undefined" when reading r.stdout_ref,
and forced defensive String(r.text||r.visible||r.result||'') everywhere. Any plan
written against one route silently returns empty strings on the other.

EXPECTATION: one stable documented shell response schema across both routes, or at
minimum a single guaranteed stdout accessor present in both.

Host boundary (crates/zero-codemode/src/host.rs STRICT_RESULT_WRAPPER) now normalizes every capability result onto canonical  (inline output; aliases text/visible/result/stdout) and  (ref-ed output; aliases ref/stdout_ref/combined_ref), so a plan reads shell output identically on either route. Connector-supplied fields are never overwritten; results with no output alias gain no fields (strict guard still throws). Alias tables exported as CANONICAL_RESULT_FIELDS / CANONICAL_TEXT_ALIASES / CANONICAL_REF_ALIASES. Documented in docs/codemode.md § Capability result shape. Tests: 5 new in crates/zero-codemode/tests/host_contract.rs (both_routes_expose_the_same_canonical_result_fields, canonical_fields_never_shadow_what_the_connector_returned, canonical_fields_pass_the_strict_guard_and_are_enumerable, a_result_without_any_output_alias_gains_no_canonical_fields, canonical_field_names_are_published). cargo test -p zero-codemode --features quickjs => 72 passed, 0 failed (host_contract 24/24). title: TokenZero shared store has no project namespacing: unrelated projects collide on one path
description:
This is the only divergence in the store-root triplicate that puts DIFFERENT objects at the SAME path, rather than the same object at different paths.

TokenZero/crates/tokenzero-engine/src/workspace.rs:106-124 always resolves to <store>/tokenzero/recovery-cache.json with no project key. N unrelated projects sharing one ZEROSTACK_STORE_ROOT all write that same file. workspace.rs:203-216 only emits a store_project_mismatch warning in the resolution report; nothing prevents the collision.

The other two namespace correctly when the store is outside the repo:
- GraphZero: <store>/projects/<project_key>/graphzero/ (zerostack_store.rs:114-123)
- FSZero: <store>/fszero/repos/<sid>/ (zerostack_store.rs:56-62)

Recommended canonical shape is GraphZeros: <root>/projects/<key>/<engine>, with the key being 16 lowercase hex chars of sha256 over the absolutized root path, no prefix. FSZeros sid- prefix belongs at the directory level, not in the key; keeping prefixes means no engine can predict another engines shard directory (FSZero sid-<16hex> = 20 chars vs GraphZero <16hex> = 16).

Also: key input bytes diverge. FSZero uses fs::canonicalize or the path as-given without absolutizing (zerostack_store.rs:100-105); GraphZero absolutizes against cwd when the path does not exist (store/path_safety.rs:35-45). For a nonexistent relative repo_root, FSZero hashes "rel/path" and GraphZero hashes "<cwd>/rel/path", producing different keys for the same repo.

Migration: TokenZero gains namespacing, <pin>/tokenzero/recovery-cache.json moves to <pin>/projects/<key>/tokenzero/recovery-cache.json. FSZero moves fszero/repos/<sid>/ to projects/<key>/fszero/. GraphZero unchanged.

Anti-collision gate: two distinct roots sharing one pin must resolve to different engine dirs. That test fails against TokenZero today.

Part of zerostack-sce part B.
notes: 2026-07-28 audit: blocked on parent zerostack-sce establishing the canonical shared store-root/project-key contract before cross-engine migration. Implementing TokenZero/FSZero paths first would entrench another divergent layout.

title: EPIC: Cut zero-store CAS cyclomatic density (put/list/atomic)
description:
## Goal
Lower cyclomatic density of zero-store CAS publish paths (`put_with_limit`, `list_objects`, `atomic_write_file`) under hard ceiling CC≤10 without changing CAS durability or race semantics; keep joint ΣCC non-increasing.

## Why (leverage)
Baseline 20260727-repo-sweep-r1: cluster hotspot ΣCC=43 (put 18 + list 12 + atomic 13). Highest product-path risk in the hub joint. Concurrent publish + fsync-before-replace + race converge are load-bearing.

## Risk class
high — Evidence tier: targeted `cargo test -p zero-store` only (never workspace). Human review: required on put/atomic transforms.

## Context (repo anchors)
- Books: `.cut-branches/runs/20260727-repo-sweep-r1/` (LATEST)
- Cards: `04-analysis-cards/{put_with_limit,list_objects,atomic_write_file}.md`
- Waves: `waves/wave1-zero-store-classifier.md`, `wave2-metric-gaming-posture.md`, `wave2-correctness-preflight.md`
- Files: `crates/zero-store/src/cas.rs`, `crates/zero-store/src/fs_replace.rs`
- Baseline: ΣCC joint=1071; analyzer lizard 1.23.0

## Current state (as-is)
`put_with_limit` packs size policy, dedup, fan-out dir ensure, temp write, atomic replace, race converge in one CC=18 body. `list_objects` filters walk paths (CC=12). `atomic_write_file` owns unique temp + write/sync/replace (CC=13).

## Desired state (to-be)
Parent functions ≤6–8 CC via named stage extracts; helpers ≤8; no public API change; race converge short-circuit `dest.is_file() && read_verified_at(...).is_ok()` preserved; fsync before replace preserved.

## Spec
### Behavior
1. Shall preserve exact CAS identity, size limits, PolicyDenied, Io error classes.
2. Shall not change concurrent-writer converge behavior.
3. Shall not scatter essential durability rules into untested micro-helpers (metric gaming ban).
### Interfaces
Public crate APIs stable unless separate auth.

## Constraints / bounds
- May edit: `crates/zero-store/src/cas.rs`, `crates/zero-store/src/fs_replace.rs`, `crates/zero-store/src/**` tests
- Must not: full workspace cargo test; engine private trees; drive-by renames
- Technique: extract method (staged); combine predicates on list_objects
- File lock: `ZeroStack/crates/zero-store/src/cas.rs` sequential; `fs_replace.rs` for atomic
- Stop if: >5 files or ΣCC rises without justified displacement

## Size / limits / deps
- Children: list_objects → atomic_write_file (add tests first) → put_with_limit
- Depends on: transform authorization + targeted crate test allowance
- Blocks: none outside cut-branches queue

## Adversarial / edge cases
1. Concurrent identical put: both writers converge, no double-body corruption
2. Non-NotFound stat errors surface as Io (not silent create)
3. Symlink substitution on fan-out dirs refused
4. atomic_write_file: crash between write and replace leaves no torn dest
5. list_objects: skip non-regular / filter predicates truth table stable

## Acceptance (`done_when`)
- [ ] Each of put_with_limit, list_objects, atomic_write_file re-measured CC≤10 OR blocked_with_reason on card residual
- [ ] Joint or crate-scope ΣCC not increased (re-run measure_complexity.py on crates/zero-store)
- [ ] `cargo test -p zero-store --lib` green (targeted only)
- [ ] Metric-gaming auditor clean on the edit pass (no single-use CC=1 wrapper spam)
- [ ] Analysis cards updated with after CC
- [ ] Fail if full cargo workspace suite was the only proof

## Verify
```bash
# from ZeroStack root — targeted only
python3 /Users/aditya/AI/JeffreySkills/_custom/cyclomatic-reduction/scripts/measure_complexity.py crates/zero-store --threshold 10 --output /tmp/zs-store-after.json
# compare total_cc to baseline part; use session scratch not shared /tmp in agent runs
cargo test -p zero-store --lib
```
Evidence: after JSON + test log + metric-gaming note.

## Out of scope
Engine CAS copies; GC sweep redesign; public ABI of engines.

## Handoff
Close children first; leave epic open until all three ≤ceiling or blocked. Point residual to NEXT_PASS. Campaign books under `.cut-branches/LATEST`.

title: Config discovery for embedded harnesses: env/XDG/well-known lookup instead of 7 hand-written absolute paths
description: config.yaml:134-141 hardcodes /Users/aditya/AI/{FSZero,GraphZero,TokenZero,ZeroStack}/target/release/... i.e. a developer worktree layout, in a user config that ships to any machine. Provide discovery order (env ZEROSTACK_HOME > XDG data dir > platform install dir > PATH) so a harness needs zero absolute paths, and a documented override for dev checkouts. Related: zerostack-no-hardcoded-environment-audit-4j6q.
notes:
Discovery contract landed in commit 0d6c1cff503b23d5fba20e7e076c1b0c73844985.

New crates/zero-codemode/src/discovery.rs resolves the aggregate host plus the fszero/graphzero/tokenzero delegates in order: ZEROSTACK_HOME/bin > ZEROSTACK_DEV_ROOT/<Repo>/target/release (documented dev-checkout override) > /zerostack/bin (default ~/.local/share) > platform install dirs > absolute PATH entries. A harness config now needs zero absolute paths. Blank/whitespace and relative roots are treated as unset; blank PATH entries (cwd) are skipped; only executable regular files are accepted so a same-named dir cannot shadow a later candidate; explicit XDG_DATA_HOME replaces rather than augments the default; each dir probed once. Entry points are pure (DiscoveryEnv + injected probe), no process-env mutation.

zerostack-codemode-host --locate prints a zerostack.binary_discovery.v1 JSON report: per binary either resolved path + source label, or every probed candidate, so failure is diagnosable instead of a bare ENOENT. Unresolved engines are reported, not fatal. Documented in docs/codemode.md.

Evidence: cargo test -p zero-codemode --test discovery_precedence => 14 passed, 0 failed (14 new tests). Full crate incl. quickjs feature => all suites pass, no warnings. Mutation-verified: reordering PATH ahead of ZEROSTACK_HOME failed exactly 4 precedence tests; reverted and re-confirmed green.
