title: EPIC: Converge shared CAS, GC, and store-root architecture in zero-store
description:
Unify the durability-critical CAS publish/verify/GC state machine and .zerostack store-root resolution in zero-store, then cut TokenZero, FSZero, and GraphZero over without byte, path, crash-consistency, or migration drift.

The epic owns extraction, engine adoption, namespacing, path safety, corruption prevention, and measured durability-preserving performance. Engine-specific wrappers may keep aliases, but canonical layout and algorithms live once.

Keep as store-root/canonical durable-object prerequisite; link to Z1b/Z6 and do not invent a new store layout.
acceptance_criteria:
All three engines consume zero-store for canonical CAS/GC/root resolution; no private behaviorally-equivalent copies remain; shared-store collisions and literal-tilde paths are impossible; crash/concurrency tests and digest/path equality gates pass; rollout and rollback are documented.
- Dependencies are machine-readable
- Receipts bind all frozen receipt fields
- Targeted RCH checks pass
- Native claims require native hosts; cross-compilation does not count

comments.author: aditya
comments.text:
Wave 1 part B landed, plus the publish side of part A.

Shipped in crates/zero-store:
- store_root.rs: one resolver for all three engines. Canonical rules, reconciling the three that had drifted: project-local .zerostack outranks the env pin; the pin requires shared-store opt-in; an exported-but-empty pin means unset; a pin outside the project is namespaced as <root>/projects/<key>/<engine>; the project key is 16 lowercase hex of sha256 over the absolutized root path with no prefix; the CAS is shared per store root and never project-namespaced. Engines pass only their own opt-in aliases, so precedence and truthiness live in one place. 21 tests, driven from the golden matrix, including the two gates the engines fail today: distinct projects never collide under one pin (TokenZero fails this, zerostack-ljx) and all three engines derive the same project key (FSZero fails this on its sid- prefix).
- gc_lock.rs: the single store coordination lock at <store_root>/gc/coordinator.lock. Publishers shared, sweeper exclusive. One lock means no lock order and no cycle, so deadlock freedom is structural. Acquisition is deadline-bounded so a wedged holder surfaces as a typed WouldBlock rather than a hang, and the kernel releases on process death so no stale reclaim is needed. The path is deliberately identical to TokenZeros existing GcCoordLock, and both fs4 and std map to flock on Unix, so a hub publisher and a not-yet-migrated TokenZero sweeper interoperate during the cutover.
- cas.rs: publish now runs under the shared guard, which is the publish half of the TOCTOU fix (zerostack-rhd). Added PutOutcome with a created flag, put_outcome, put_prehashed that re-derives and compares the digest so a wrong hash writes nothing, touch, list_objects, and remove_object plus quarantine_object which take a &StoreLock instead of acquiring one, so a sweeper cannot forget the guard. Dedup now refreshes mtime, since a dedup is a fresh reference and an age-based policy that never sees it collects a live object. The temp reaper recognizes all three historical engine shapes, closing the mutual blindness in zerostack-oh7. object_path no longer panics on short input.

Verification: zero-store 8 tests to 45. Workspace 60 to 100, all passing. zero-store is clippy-clean and fmt-clean. The publish/GC race has a deterministic regression test that parks a sweeper between its decision and its unlink using channel rendezvous, asserts a publish is excluded, then asserts the republished object is readable. No timing assumptions anywhere.

Empirically resolved an open question from the design analysis: on rustc 1.97.1 the std signatures are File::try_lock() -> Result<(), std::fs::TryLockError> and try_lock_shared() the same, not Result<bool>. Probed rather than assumed, so no new dependency was needed: fs4 is not required.

Remaining for this bead, the larger half of part A: port the zerostack.cas-gc.v1 state machine itself (records, mark, report, resumable sweep, epoch monotonicity, uncertainty policy) from TokenZero shared_cas.rs:296-1471 into a zero-store gc module, which needs serde promoted from dev-dependency to dependency. Until that lands the lock is in place but the sweeper still lives in TokenZero. Then the engine cutovers: TokenZero by PR, FSZero and GraphZero direct.

Also filed from the analysis of the three implementations: zerostack-rhd, pi1, ljx, oh7, 2x7 in the hub, tokenzero-8tdg, 4xvw, mivh, fszero-1woo, 44nj, p0cz, graphzero-m94u, f2jn.

title: Parallel worker spawns serialize on pi-rewind checkpoint lock (60s stall each at startup)
description: Observed 07-30: dispatching 3 worker-opus subagents simultaneously - each stalls up to 60s+ at startup on Timed out after 60000ms waiting for checkpoint lock at ~/.pi/agent/ayu/checkpoints/sessions/session/.pi-checkpoint-lock (pi-rewind extension). One worker sat >3min with zero tool calls until steered. Throttles wave dispatch throughput; per-session lock paths or disabling pi-rewind for subagent sessions would fix. Harness-side (pi extension), not ZeroStack core.
notes: compliance-audit 2026-07-30: empty prior notes. Parallel worker spawns serialize on pi-rewind checkpoint lock (~60s stall). Next: measure + fix lock scope in owning runtime. Do not close without commit SHA.

comments.author: aditya
comments.text: compliance-audit 2026-07-30: status in_progress consistent (pi-rewind checkpoint lock serialization). Notes empty. Likely pi-stack/runtime ownership. Needs assignee + measured stall reproduction. Do not close without commit-level evidence.

comments.author: aditya
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE (harness-side, pi-rewind 0.4.6 - NOT ZeroStack code):
@ayulab/pi-rewind bundle @ayulab__pi-checkpoint.js getRepoDir() keys the checkpoint repo dir on path.basename(sessionFile, ".jsonl"). Every subagent run writes its session as <run-dir>/session.jsonl, so ALL concurrent subagents resolve to the single dir ~/.pi/agent/ayu/checkpoints/sessions/session and serialise behind one .pi-checkpoint-lock (LOCK_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT_MS=6e4 -> the observed 60s stall/timeout).

Evidence of collision:
- 651 session files on disk all named session.jsonl.
- Literal dir sessions/session exists; its manifest.json points at a subagent run-0 path.
- Pre-patch probe on live bundle: getRepoDir("/x/y/abc123/run-0/session.jsonl") and getRepoDir("/a/b/deadbeef/run-1/session.jsonl") BOTH -> .../sessions/session. Top-level sessions (timestamp_uuid.jsonl) already got unique dirs.

FIX (applied to pi-stack's sanctioned patcher, not to ZeroStack):
scripts/patch-pi-rewind.mjs extended with PI_STACK_UNIQUE_CHECKPOINT_REPO_DIR: when basename === "session", suffix the dir with sha1(resolve(sessionFile)).slice(0,12). Exact-needle, unique-match, idempotent; refuses fuzzy patching. Also adds the createHash import. Top-level session dirs and existing checkpoint history untouched.

Post-patch probe on live bundle:
  /x/y/abc123/run-0/session.jsonl -> sessions/session-64889768c386
  /a/b/deadbeef/run-1/session.jsonl -> sessions/session-1dfff1752573
  /other/2026-07-30T00-00-00-000Z_019f.jsonl -> unchanged

TIMING (3 workers, faithful re-impl of pi-rewind lock.ts, 800ms repo-init under lock):
  before (shared sessions/session): time-to-first-tool-call = 802 / 1620 / 2436 ms (linear serialisation)
  after  (per-session dir):         time-to-first-tool-call = 801 / 801 / 801 ms (fully parallel)
Serialisation is linear in worker count, which is what produces 60s timeouts at real git-init cost and wave width.

Applied to local config: yes, non-destructive. Live bundle patched, node --check passes, backup at @ayulab__pi-checkpoint.js.before-scsz-20260730 (original sha256 1f322cd54483298398a5dc7d3bf215e183aa08240ab7d06a44c6e1078f2a914c). Re-running the patcher reports "already applied" and is a no-op.

Tests: npm run test:pi-rewind-patch -> 2/2 pass (idempotency + unique-repo-dir).

RESIDUAL: patch targets a node_modules bundle; install-packages.sh already re-runs the patcher after installing @ayulab/pi-rewind so reinstalls are covered, but a pi-rewind version bump can move the needle (patcher fails loudly rather than fuzzy-patching). Not yet confirmed against a real 3-way live subagent wave - timing above is synthetic but a faithful reproduction of the extension's own lock algorithm. Keeping in_progress until the next real parallel dispatch confirms no 60s startup stall.

description:
br (beads_rust) writes "source_repo_path":"<home>/AI/ZeroStack" into every issue record in .beads/issues.jsonl, which is tracked in this public hub repo. This is systemic, not a one-off: every issue carries it. The same applies to the TokenZero, FSZero, and GraphZero repos.

This is a different problem from the benchmark harness leak (zerostack-9g4): the writer is br itself, not a Python harness, so the fix is either:
  a. Configure br to omit or relativize source_repo_path (check br config/help for an option), or
  b. Add a pre-commit or pre-sync scrub that rewrites source_repo_path to the repo name or to "." in .beads/issues.jsonl before it is staged.

Either way, new exports must stop carrying the absolute path. The already-committed content is accepted as-is (no history rewrite, per user decision in zerostack-9g4).

If br cannot be configured, the scrub script should be shared across all four repos since they all use br. Consider putting it in the hub scripts/ and referencing it from each repos pre-sync step.

Do not untrack .beads/issues.jsonl: it is the cross-session bead handoff mechanism.

Refs zerostack-9g4.

title: lossy elision is only flagged in a trailing footer, never inline at the cut point
description:
Two smaller ZeroStack surface issues found during conformance work on 2026-07-25, filed together since both are about output fidelity.

1. LOSSY COMPRESSION CAN DROP THE PAYLOAD WITH ONLY A FOOTER AS WARNING
Reading a conformance report through zero.token.shell returned a result tagged
  [mode=lossy lossy_policy_id=tokenzero.visible-compression.v1
   lossy_spans=[{description=omitted-bytes reason=visible-budget
   recovery_may_be_needed=true}]]
The visible text was truncated mid-value. The footer is honest, but it is at the END of a long block, so an agent that reads top-down and stops early will act on a partial JSON payload believing it is complete. When the omitted span falls inside a JSON document the remaining text is not even parseable, yet nothing marks the truncation point inline.
Suggested: mark the elision INLINE at the point it happens, e.g. a clear sentinel where bytes were dropped, so truncation is visible exactly where it matters rather than only in a trailing annotation. Bonus: when the payload is detected as JSON, prefer eliding whole values over cutting mid-token.

2. grep -A/-B THROUGH shell RETURNS A REF, NOT THE MATCH
  zero.token.shell("grep -n 'fn extract_json_payload' -A 30 file.rs")
returned only
  preview: 884:fn extract_json_payload(
i.e. the first matched line, with the -A 30 context available solely behind a second expand of the blob ref. Same for -B. The whole point of -A/-B is the surrounding context, so the one flag that makes grep useful is the one whose output does not survive. This turns a routine one-call code read into two calls, every time.
Suggested: when the command carries -A/-B/-C, treat the context lines as the payload and show them, since the caller has explicitly declared how much context they want.

Neither is a correctness bug in the engines; both are ZeroStack surface ergonomics that cost an extra round trip and, in case 1, risk silent misreads. Filed per the standing instruction to report ZeroStack problems as beads.

Before, the -A context was discarded and only the match line survived:
  grep -n "fn extract_json_payload" -A 30 conformance/src/lib.rs
  -> preview: 884:fn extract_json_payload(
  The 30 lines of requested context were reachable only through a second expand of the blob ref.

After, the context comes back inline in one call:
  grep -n "fn substrate_label" -A 12 conformance/src/lib.rs
  -> 498:fn substrate_label(config: &RunConfig) -> String {
     499-    let name = |p: &PathBuf| {

  Full requested window, no second round trip.

Fix: search_shell_view capped sample_matches at 20 unconditionally. It now scales the cap with the largest -A/-B/-C value (handling both -A30 and -A 30) and stays at 20 when no context was requested, so ordinary greps are unaffected. TokenZero 7bada5e.

Part 1 (lossy elision only flagged in a trailing footer) is NOT fixed here. It turns out to have a matching RED test on the TokenZero side, tokens::tokenizer_tests::visible_budget_prefix_retains_every_fitting_line, which fails with a visible output consisting of nothing but the lossy footer: the compressor spent the whole budget on its own annotation and kept none of the payload, violating invariant P01-001. That is the same defect seen from the inside. Tracking it there as tokenzero-rnv2, since the fix belongs in the token budget accounting rather than in render/domain.rs.

Leaving this bead open for part 1, now narrowed to: mark elision INLINE at the point bytes are dropped, and prefer eliding whole JSON values over cutting mid-token.

comments.author: AzureOrchid
comments.text:
Part 1 is BLOCKED on a dirty TokenZero tree, not on design. Recording findings so it is not lost.

BLOCKER
The fix belongs in enforce_token_budget_with_ref in crates/tokenzero-core/src/tokens.rs, and that file is uncommitted work belonging to another live session: 81 files dirty on branch harness-no-host-paths, with tokens.rs and lib.rs both modified. Editing underneath that risks destroying their work, which already happened to me once today in this repo (zerostack-wth). Mailed QuietSummit and CobaltAnchor with an ack request; will take this as soon as the tree is committed or stashed.

SEPARATE REGRESSION FOUND WHILE INVESTIGATING, reported by mail
crates/tokenzero-core/src/tokens.rs:37 in that uncommitted work reintroduces
  const LOSSY_VISIBLE_BUDGET_MARKER: &str = "[mode=lossy ...]";
a byte-identical, zero-caller duplicate of VISIBLE_BUDGET_LOSSY_DECLARATION on line 35. cargo build warns "constant LOSSY_VISIBLE_BUDGET_MARKER is never used", and TokenZero CI runs clippy with -D warnings, so it is a build failure once committed.

It is specifically a regression of tokenzero-rnv2, which was closed for collapsing three duplicate copies of this exact string into one pub const. Verified origin/main is clean: only the declaration at line 35 and its use at line 51, no second constant. The duplicate is local-only. If it lands, rnv2 reopens, since a divergent copy of this string is precisely what made the visible-budget test fail P01-001 (test modelled a 14-token marker, real marker costs 33).

CURRENT BEHAVIOUR, read from the code
enforce_token_budget_with_ref keeps a prefix of whole lines, then appends the marker as a trailing line:
  out = prefix + "\n" + marker
It already does the thing rnv2 added: marker_tokens is subtracted from the budget before deciding what fits, and if the marker alone exceeds the budget, or nothing fits, the marker is returned alone as a correctness floor. So the accounting is sound. The defect in this bead is purely POSITIONAL: the annotation is always appended at the end, never placed where bytes were actually dropped.

Note the marker has two forms. With a recovery_ref it is a readable "... omitted by visible budget; expand REF ..." line; without one it is the machine-readable lossy declaration. Both are appended trailing, so both have this problem.

DESIGN INTENDED, stated for objection before I start
1. Emit the omission marker INLINE at the cut point rather than only as a trailing footer, so truncation is visible exactly where it happens to a top-down reader.
2. When the payload is detected as JSON, elide whole values instead of cutting mid-token, since a mid-token cut leaves text that will not parse.
3. Keep VISIBLE_BUDGET_LOSSY_DECLARATION as the single source of truth and preserve the marker-cost accounting rnv2 established, so P01-001 stays green.
Since truncation here is always a suffix cut, "inline at the cut point" and "trailing" coincide for the plain case; the real win is item 2 plus not losing the marker when a caller reads only the head of a long block.ZEOF

title: origin/main status file goes stale after manual checkout advance: reports old rev and built:false while serving the new binary
description:
Found live 2026-07-26 while completing the dogfooding loop.

SEQUENCE:
1. Pushed 6 FSZero perf commits (d24102d -> 3e420b0).
2. Advanced the protected checkout: git fetch + reset --hard origin/main. HEAD = 3e420b0.
3. Rebuilt with the exact documented command:
     cargo build --release -p fszero-codemode --bin fszero-codemode -j 1
   Finished in 25.46s; binary mtime 22:55.
4. Ran a plan through zero_execute. It works and is fast (search 18ms).

BUT ~/.pi/agent/zerostack-origin-main/fszero.status.json still reports:
  rev:         d24102de...   (the SUPERSEDED commit)
  refreshedAt: 2026-07-26T02:49:18Z  (before the rebuild)
  built:       false          (a release binary demonstrably exists)

So the status file describes a checkout state that no longer exists. The
binary being served is correct; the metadata about it is wrong.

WHY IT MATTERS: this status file is the ONLY way a session can answer 'is my
pushed work actually live?' -- the exact question the dogfooding loop depends
on. substrates.js:396 already documents a previous incident in this same
mechanism where 'refreshedAt froze, and pushes to origin/main silently never
went live while status cheerfully reported config-override'. This is the same
failure mode surviving in a different path: the refresh is lazy and only
scheduleOriginMainRefresh writes the stamp, so a manual advance+build never
updates it.

Same family as zerostack-4aa: the mechanism works, but its self-report is
untrustworthy, so a session cannot tell a live improvement from a stale one.

ACCEPTANCE
1. Status reflects reality regardless of who advanced the checkout -- derive
   rev from the checkout (git rev-parse HEAD) and built from binary existence
   plus mtime vs rev, rather than trusting a cached stamp.
2. built:false while a current release binary exists is itself a detectable
   inconsistency; surface it rather than reporting it flatly.
3. Regression test: advance the checkout out-of-band, rebuild, and assert the
   status snapshot reports the new rev and built:true.
4. Document the supported way to force a refresh after a manual push+build.

title: EPIC: Structural convergence across the three engines
description:
The owner's observation, measured 2026-07-25: the three engines are not three
instances of one design. They are three different designs, and that difference
is why the same bug must be fixed three times.

MEASURED LAYOUT DIVERGENCE

  engine     top-level src/   crates/   root Cargo.toml
  FSZero     YES, 103 files       3      is itself a package (lib)
  TokenZero  none                 9      pure virtual workspace
  GraphZero  none                12      pure virtual workspace

FSZero is a monolith with 103 files at src/ that grew 3 satellite crates.
TokenZero and GraphZero are proper workspaces. Consequences already observed:

- A naive audit grepping <repo>/src returns ZERO for TokenZero and GraphZero
  and gives a false 'no duplication' reading. This happened during the audit
  that produced this bead -- the first pass concluded blake3/rusqlite/CAS were
  FSZero-only, which is wrong. Tooling that assumes one layout silently
  mis-measures two of three engines.
- 'Where does X live?' has three different answers, so cross-engine work costs
  a discovery step every time.

WHAT IS ALREADY CONSISTENT (do not churn these)
  edition 2024 + nightly toolchain: all three agree.
  zero-abi + zero-ref: adopted by all three.
So convergence is achievable; it has already happened twice.

WHAT IS INCONSISTENT (the actual backlog)
1. Layout: monolithic src/ vs workspace-of-crates (above).
2. zero-store adoption: GraphZero only. FSZero and TokenZero keep private CAS
   copies -- see ee2, which now carries the measured symbol-level evidence.
3. Store-root resolution: divergent enough that two engines wrote real store
   data into a literal '~' directory (zerostack-tilde-store-root-2r6), one of
   them doubly nested.
4. Gates: TokenZero enforces fmt AND clippy; FSZero enforces neither. So the
   same code is acceptable in one repo and rejected in another.
5. Test organization: three independent implementations of packaging_lifecycle
   (7 tests each), packaging_e2e, readme_claims, racc_durability_matrix,
   readme_command_audit -- see the zero-testkit EPIC.
6. Hashing/storage deps chosen independently: all three depend on sha2, two on
   rusqlite, with no shared wrapper.

THE ARGUMENT FOR FIXING IT
Every inconsistency above converts a one-line fix into a three-repo port with
three chances to diverge. The clearest case is measured: ovn found 6
F_FULLFSYNC per plan (~24ms of 38ms, ~63% of latency) inside CAS code that
exists in three copies. Consolidating first means that fix is written once.

This bead is the TRACKER for structural convergence, not a single change.
Its job is to keep the list above honest and sequenced. Concrete work lands in
sce (store-root + CAS core), ee2 (adoption), yoe (shared codemode runtime),
the zero-testkit EPIC (tests), and hxl (distribution).

DELIVERABLES
1. Decide the canonical layout. Likely: every engine is a virtual workspace and
   FSZero's 103-file src/ becomes a crate. That is a large mechanical change --
   scope and sequence it, do not start it mid-Phase-1.
2. Write the layout down as a contract in the hub so new crates cannot diverge.
3. Converge the gates: one fmt/clippy policy across all engines, enforced in CI.
4. Track items 1-6 to closure, each via its owning bead.
5. Add a hub check that fails when an engine drifts from the contract
   (layout, gates, shared-crate adoption). Coordinate with the conformance
   suite (30a) rather than building a second mechanism.

CONSTRAINT
Do not begin large layout moves during Phase 1 (unblock) or while Phase 2.5
CAS consolidation is in flight -- a repo reshuffle mid-cutover makes every
conflict harder to read. Sequence after ee2 lands.

title: Cross-surface result shape is inconsistent: zero.token.shell returns .text, zero.fs.compound('read') returns .payload.ref
description:
Found live while dogfooding 2026-07-25.

zero.token.shell(cmd)               -> result.text          (string, directly usable)
zero.fs.compound('read', {...})     -> result.payload.ref   (no .text at all)
zero.graph.*                        -> unaudited, likely a third shape

An agent writing a plan cannot predict how to get at a result without trial
and error, and guessing wrong FAILS SILENTLY: reading .text on an fs result
yields undefined -> '' with no error. That cost multiple turns this session
and produced two verification steps that falsely reported 0 bytes.

This is the hub's contract to own: zero-abi already exists for exactly this
kind of cross-engine agreement.

Deliverables:
1. Audit the result shape of every zero.* verb across all three engines and
   document the canonical shape in the hub.
2. Converge on one accessor for inline content and one for ref-ed content.
   Ref-ing out large results is correct; disagreeing about HOW is not.
3. Make the failure loud: accessing a field that does not exist on a result
   should be diagnosable, not silently undefined.
4. Conformance test in the shared suite asserting all three engines expose
   results identically. Coordinate with zerostack-conformance-refresh-ci-30a
   and the zero-testkit EPIC.

Related: fszero-fs-read-content-broken-b4yg (the P0 instance of this in FSZero).

title: migrate pack manifest to zero-abi canonical JSON (digest+signature invalidating)
description:
Follow-up to zerostack-graphzero-canonical-json-drift-881, which PROVED the divergence (GraphZero 41170ab, 4 passing differential tests) but deliberately did not migrate.

GraphZero PackManifest::unsigned_canonical_json emits struct declaration order; zero_abi::canonical_json emits sorted keys. Different bytes, different SHA-256.

Migrating is not a cleanup because unsigned_canonical_json is BOTH the digest input (digest_sha256) and the exact ed25519-signed payload (graphzero-pack/src/sign.rs:9 sign, :16 verify). Switching encoders changes every pack manifest digest and invalidates every existing signature.

Required:
1. Bump MANIFEST_SCHEMA_VERSION so old and new manifests are distinguishable rather than silently incompatible.
2. Decide verification policy for already-signed v1 manifests: accept via the legacy encoder, or hard-fail and re-sign. Do not silently accept both, that reintroduces the ambiguity.
3. Delete unsigned_canonical_json, call zero_abi::canonical_json, promote zero-abi from dev-dependency to a real dependency of graphzero-pack.
4. Flip the two intentionally-inverted assertions in canonical_json_drift.rs (they are written to fail once the encoders converge, with messages saying so).
5. Record which manifests were hashed with the divergent encoder (deliverable 3 of the parent bead).

Do NOT start this until deliverable 4 of the parent (hub-side guard) lands, or a third implementation can appear during the migration.

Amend as formal/model evidence input and bind model version, commands, fixtures, mutants, assumptions.
acceptance_criteria:
- Dependencies are machine-readable

- Targeted RCH checks pass

title: Epic: centralize shared tests and cap each engine at 50
description: Parent: zerostack-structural-convergence-93e. Consolidate all cross-engine and shared product verification into one canonical library under top-level `ZeroStack/tests/`, then reduce each engine repository to a hard maximum of 50 locally owned, independently registered tests. Current source-annotation scan on 2026-07-30 found TokenZero 1,160, FSZero 811, and GraphZero 1,068 Rust test attributes; obtain authoritative RCH `cargo test --workspace --all-targets -- --list` baselines before editing. Every survivor must guard a named user-visible promise or engine-specific invariant not better tested centrally. Shared packaging, lifecycle, durability, README/CLI, raw-worker, adapter, RACC, ref/store, installation, and cross-engine scenarios belong in the hub suite, not copied engine suites.
design: The numerical limit is fixed, not derived. Each engine must prove a complete workspace build with `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --no-run` through RCH, enumerate no more than 50 default local tests, run all of them green, then pass the centralized black-box suite against its built binaries. No collapsing unrelated cases into one opaque mega-test to game the count. Parameterized shared matrices belong under `ZeroStack/tests/`; local survivors remain independently reportable. Default doctests/integration/unit tests count. Fuzz/benchmark harnesses must be separately inventoried and cannot hide default correctness tests. Deletions remain exact-path approval-gated.
acceptance_criteria: Top-level `ZeroStack/tests/` is the sole canonical shared suite library and includes its runner, fixtures, contract catalog, engine adapters, counting gate, and documentation; no active shared suite remains duplicated under `crates/zero-testkit`, `conformance/tests`, or engine repositories except thin registration/adapters explicitly justified. TokenZero, FSZero, and GraphZero each enumerate <=50 default local tests across the whole workspace/all targets, compile every target, run every local test green, and pass the centralized suite. Every local survivor maps to one named unique promise; every removed/moved test is classified and exact-path approved; the gate fails at 51 and has a mutation/self-test; before/after counts and runtime are committed.

title: Literal '~' directories in tokenzero/ and graphzero/ hold misplaced store data; store-root resolution leaves tilde unexpanded (graphzero doubly nested)
description:
Found 2026-07-25 during a cross-engine structural audit.

TokenZero and GraphZero each contain a literal directory named '~' at repo
root, holding real ZeroStack store data written to the wrong place:

  tokenzero/~/AI/TokenZero/.zerostack/graphzero/...            413 files
  graphzero/~/AI/GraphZero/~/AI/GraphZero/.zerostack/fszero/...  13 files

Note the GraphZero path is DOUBLY NESTED: ~/AI/GraphZero/~/AI/GraphZero/.
A tilde-prefixed path was resolved against a root that already had the same
unexpanded prefix, so this is not a one-off typo -- it recurred, compounding
each time. FSZero is clean, so this is a two-engine defect, not universal.

ROOT CAUSE (to confirm): a store root of the form '~/AI/<Engine>' is used
without shell expansion -- passed to a Rust fs API or a quoted shell var, where
'~' is an ordinary character. Something then created './~/AI/...' relative to
the repo. Contents include store.sqlite3, WAL files, locks, shard bins, and
session-memory, so a real engine session was reading and writing there.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS
1. Data went somewhere nobody would look. A store that silently lands in the
   wrong directory is the same class as zerostack-e3g (store corruption) --
   the engine believed it was persisting correctly.
2. It crosses engines: tokenzero/~ contains a GRAPHZERO store, graphzero/~
   contains an FSZERO store. So the bad root is being propagated between
   engines through the shared store-root resolution path.
3. That path is exactly what zerostack-sce moves into zero-store. Fix the
   resolution there, once, or all three engines keep their own version of it.
   This is a concrete argument for the ee2/sce consolidation.

DELIVERABLES
1. Find the writer. Grep for '~' in store-root construction across both
   engines; check ZEROSTACK_/FSZERO_ROOT/GZ_REPO_ROOT/TOKENZERO_ROOT env
   handling and any script passing a quoted '~/...'.
2. Fix in the shared store-root resolver (coordinate with sce): either expand
   '~' explicitly, or REJECT a leading '~' with a clear error. Never create a
   literal '~' directory.
3. Regression test: resolving '~/foo' as a store root either yields $HOME/foo
   or errors -- and never produces a directory named '~'.
4. Clean up: confirm the 426 files are recoverable/duplicated elsewhere, then
   delete both trees. Do not delete before confirming nothing unique lives
   there.
5. Add a repo-hygiene check that fails if a path component equal to '~' appears
   anywhere in the working tree.
close_reason: Hub zero-store refuses literal '~' roots (tests green). Engine directory cleanup filed as follow-up child under sce.

title: Make snap-to-file edits begin in one sub-second call
description: P0 product invariant: when a model decides to edit a local file, it must not spend another model turn locating, unpacking, or re-deriving the target. From harness `zero_execute` entry, normal supported edits must begin their journaled mutation in under one second, with a 1ms-class warmed target. FSZero discovery already emits canonical `HIT path#Lstart-Lend` records. One existing black-box plan proved search -> mutate -> verify in one model-visible call and 34ms transcript wall time, but it required parsing/re-deriving the path and three FS actions. Passing the returned target ref verbatim to mutate still fails `bad path: not found`, and the existing target-ref proof bypasses FSZero journaling with direct std::fs writes. This bead owns the fused, safe, timed implementation.
design: Make ordinary `zero.fs.compound('mutate', ...)` accept two canonical target variants: a discovery `path#Lstart-Lend` ref passed verbatim, and a fused snap specification containing query/scope/uniqueness/preimage/replacement. The fused variant performs indexed discovery, uniqueness decision, precondition check, journal begin, atomic replacement, certificate publication, and verification inside one FS action/physical pass where contract-safe. Instrument monotonic timestamps at aggregate execute entry, FS dispatch, snap resolve, journal begin, first write, atomic commit, verify, and settled result. Root-confine targets; constrain line/byte window exactly; require old-content or digest; fail typed and mutation-free on stale, ambiguous, multi-hit, out-of-window, symlink escape, concurrent change, or unavailable index. Never silently strip target fragments, broaden to the whole file, shell out, use direct std::fs outside the journal path, or require the model to inspect a discovery result before editing.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh-model black-box task `find the uniquely identified symbol/string and replace it` succeeds through one `zero_execute`, one FS dispatch, one journaled mutation, and zero intermediate model-visible discovery/ref-expansion calls. The exact target ref from every FSZero discovery route mutates verbatim. Timed gates, excluding provider/model thinking but including the full harness after tool execute entry: warmed execute-entry -> journal-begin p50 <=1ms, p95 <=2ms, p99 <=10ms; warmed execute-entry -> verified settled p50 <=5ms, p95 <=10ms; cold fallback p95 <=250ms; every normal supported edit begins and settles in <1,000ms. Run at least 1,000 warmed and 100 cold isolated edits with stage sums within 0.25ms. The same gates pass via standalone `zsx`, session sidecar, pi-zerostack, and generated Claude/Codex/ZCode/Kimi/Grok adapters. History/undo/certificates match ordinary mutate. Stale/ambiguous/escape/concurrent cases fail typed in <1,000ms without file or journal mutation. Injected +1ms hot-path and +1,000ms delay mutants fail the appropriate gates.
notes:
Delivery evidence (2026-07-31):

Safe FSZero engine implementation committed as 2dd7217 (`feat: add journaled snap-to-file edits`). Canonical `path#Lstart-Lend` mutation uses target_ref::parse_target_ref, exact line windows, fused `{query,scope,uniqueness,preimage,replacement}`, journaled dispatcher path, kernel-owned exact postimage verification, certificates/history/undo, UTF-8/CRLF/missing-final-newline fidelity, metadata-exact rollback, transaction rollback, conservative uniqueness, and typed stale/ambiguous/root/traversal/symlink failures. Independent RCH evidence: connector 20/20; transaction 4/4; target/ref/proof 6/6; AST certificate 3/3; diff-check clean. Independent review found no actionable defects.

Persistent latency gate committed as 150dec2 (`test: add persistent snap-edit latency gate`). Normal persistent temp filesystem, 1,000 fused journaled edits, dispatch_count=1000: p50 104.986ms, p95 138.862ms, p99 148.693ms, max 166.184ms, duration 97.69s. Shipping max<1,000ms passes. Aspirational p50<=5ms/p95<=10ms remains red and owned by zerostack-me51. A rejected 14-file optimization measured about p50 5.0-5.2ms but was reverted because file publication and SQLite evidence were not crash-atomic and /dev/shm was not an honest FULL-durability benchmark.

Fresh Sol model proof emitted exactly one zero_execute and one fused action. First attempt exposed pi lowering `mutate requires path`, filed as zerostack-zajl. After lowering, second attempt reached FSZero but exposed global 16-hit cap before scope, filed as zerostack-wpi6; tool transcript proves one zero_execute start/end and details.actions=1, outer failed envelope 4,655ms, mutation-free. Scope-first discovery fix committed as FSZero 8d20a98 (`fix: scope fused snap discovery before hit cap`): canonical/root-confined file or directory scope filters indexed keys before cap; one physical scan; canonical workspace-relative windows; 20 out-of-scope decoys succeed; 20 in-scope hits fail typed; traversal/symlink escape mutation-free. Final RCH evidence: connector 25 pass/1 ignored; search payload 7; prefilter 8; AST grep parity 1; target/ref 6; crash/reopen 3; production release build passed. Independent final review found no blocker.

pi-stack lowering fix remains under review in packages/pi-zerostack/router/lib/lowering.js and router/test/read-contract.test.mjs. It must add strict fused dispatch without regressing legacy spec/edit arrays/aliases/compound('edit')/direct path mutation, and must prevent directFsPlan regex misclassification when fused string values contain `path:`, `find:`, or `replace:`. Successful fresh-model proof against FSZero 8d20a98 is still required before closure.

title: TokenZero pays 6 F_FULLFSYNC per CodeMode plan in SharedCas::publish (~24ms of 38ms)
description:
TokenZero pays 6 F_FULLFSYNC barriers per CodeMode plan via SharedCas::publish.

MEASURED (tokenzero-codemode over stdio, warm child, empty plan "return 0;"):

  stage                          p50
  total (empty plan)          38.19ms
  finalize_codemode_result    37.41ms
    deferred_json/text x5     24.27ms   <-- 63% of the plan
    store.commit()            11.19ms
      persist (rewrite)        7.46ms
      persist fsync            4.39ms
  bootstrap_plan_executor      0.43ms
  containment                  0.67ms
  transport (ping)             0.02ms

Stages sum to ~36 of 38.19ms, so the accounting closes.

ROOT CAUSE
SharedCas::publish (crates/tokenzero-recovery/src/shared_cas.rs:78) does
tmp.sync_all() then a parent-dir sync_all() on every miss. On macOS both are
F_FULLFSYNC, measured at ~4ms each on this disk (plain fsync is 0.035ms).

Instrumented dedup counter: 3 misses per plan, 6 barriers total, 24.22ms.
The content-hash fast path at line 86 (`if path.exists()`) works -- it hits 3
of 6 times -- but the other 3 blobs are the execution's own telemetry, steps
and execution-record JSON, which embed a fresh execution_id and timestamps
and therefore hash differently on EVERY plan. A content-addressed dedup can
never help content that is unique by construction.

WHY THIS IS NOT THE FSZERO FIX
FSZero's 5u7 barriers were removable because the rows were execution-scoped
scratch with no durability guarantee (expand refuses them outright). These
CAS objects are different: a torn blob is content-address-corrupt, and the
sync_all before rename is what prevents publishing a locator to short bytes.
The barrier is doing real work here, so it cannot simply be relaxed.

CANDIDATE DIRECTIONS (not yet evaluated)
1. Batch the per-plan publishes: one fsync for all N blobs of an execution
   instead of N, since they commit together anyway.
2. Treat the execution audit trail (telemetry/steps/record) as its own class
   and let it take a cheaper path, the way FSZero now does -- these are
   derived artifacts of a plan, not user content.
3. Skip the parent-dir sync_all per object; one dir sync per batch is enough
   to make all the renames durable.

ACCEPTANCE
- Median empty tz_execute_code plan under 10ms, measured the same way.
- zero.token.shell('true') overhead under 15ms over native fork (currently
  52.83ms vs 2.08ms native = 50.75ms overhead), which is 5u7 acceptance 3.
- A crash test proving a published CAS object is never readable at short
  bytes after the change, mutation-verified.

CONTEXT
Found while closing zerostack-5u7 for FSZero, where the identical symptom
(fixed cost per round-trip, does not scale with work) turned out to be 3
F_FULLFSYNC per plan. FSZero is now 6.07ms/read through the router. TokenZero
is the same disease in a different engine, but needs a different cure.

title: Generate ZeroStack adapters for five coding clients
description: Child of zerostack-harness-agnostic-distribution-59ra. Package the non-MCP `zsx` path for Claude Code CLI/app, Codex CLI/app, ZCode/GLM app/CLI, Kimi Code CLI/web app, and Grok Build TUI/dashboard/agent. Current private skills/hooks prove reachability but are inconsistent, per-engine, path-pinned, and often deny a native call so the model spends a second turn retrying through `zs`. Generate every adapter from one public manifest and installer.
design: Add `zerostack integrate <target|all>` driven by one versioned adapter manifest/template set. Every adapter establishes a session identity and owner process, starts/prewarms `zerostack-session` invisibly on supported SessionStart, points `zsx`/optional edge at its private socket, and requests graceful teardown on SessionEnd; OS parent-death binding is authoritative when hooks are skipped. Claude: plugin skill plus lifecycle hooks. Codex: `.codex-plugin` skill/hooks shared by CLI/app. ZCode: `.zcode-plugin` skill/command/hooks for app/bundled CLI. Kimi: skill plus supported lifecycle/profile hooks for CLI/web. Grok: public plugin/hooks for TUI/dashboard/headless agent. Each teaches one aggregate `zsx` grammar; no per-engine selector, private Pi path, duplicated AGENTS body, global daemon, or deny-and-retry loop. Installer patches config structurally with backup/dry-run/uninstall and never touches auth/secrets.
acceptance_criteria: On clean isolated homes, install, upgrade, doctor, and uninstall pass for all five targets without hardcoded paths/config corruption. Each fresh CLI/app session discovers a <=500-token on-demand skill, silently starts exactly one aggregate session sidecar, and performs the canonical `find this unique symbol/string and edit it` task through one model-visible tool/terminal call, one FS dispatch, and zero visible discovery/ref turns. Every adapter records execute-entry -> journal-begin and -> verified-settle and meets zerostack-tj5c's warm/cold/<1,000ms gates. Live smokes cover Claude Code 2.1.220, Codex 0.145.0 CLI/app, ZCode 3.6.4 app/bundled loader, Kimi 0.29.2 CLI/web, and Grok 0.2.117 TUI/headless; also record provider calls/tokens/cost, output refs, peak/idle CPU/RSS, and teardown. Hooks never cause denied-call retry waste; unavailable startup fails once with remediation. Generated adapters expose the full aggregate surface, pass one golden suite, contain no Pi dependency, and leave no process when no vendor session exists.

title: FSZero worker thread panics on transient SQLite busy, then reports the dead worker as retryable backpressure forever
description:
Proven with a stack trace on 2026-07-25. Two failures compound; both are in the path of zerostack-5u7 and very likely cause zerostack-4aa.

REPRODUCTION
Spawn two fszero-codemode children on the SAME root, initialize both, then fire one fz_execute_code at each concurrently (a trivial read plan). Both children emit:

  thread '<unnamed>' panicked at src/core/session.rs:196:25:
  fszero: durable store required (fsqlite durable open failed for <root>/.fszero/store.sqlite3: database is busy); set FSZERO_ALLOW_EPHEMERAL=1 to opt into in-memory recovery
  stack backtrace:
     2: <fs_zero::core::session::FSZeroSession>::with_repo_store::<&std::path::PathBuf>

and from then on EVERY request to either child returns:
  {code:-32002, message:'stdio MCP session worker unavailable', data:{kind:'backpressure', retryable:true, capacity:32}}

Two children on SEPARATE roots: no contention at all, both steady at ~30ms. So the trigger is same-root concurrency, which is the normal case for two Pi sessions in one repo, or for any tool that spawns its own child alongside the router's.

DEFECT 1 - panic on a transient condition
src/core/session.rs:184-196 with_repo_store treats every try_with_repo_store error as fatal and panics unless FSZERO_ALLOW_EPHEMERAL=1. 'database is busy' is transient by definition, unlike corruption or EACCES, and SQLite's own contract is that the caller retries. Fail-closed is right for an integrity violation and wrong here. Needs a bounded busy retry/backoff before any panic, and busy specifically must be distinguished from genuinely fatal open errors.

DEFECT 2 - a dead worker is advertised as retryable
with_repo_store is called INSIDE the session worker thread (src/mcp_protocol/stdio.rs:86 spawn_session_worker). The panic unwinds that thread, rx is dropped, and every later dispatch takes the TrySendError::Disconnected arm at stdio.rs:184, which calls write_busy_response -> {kind:backpressure, retryable:true, capacity:32}.

That is false in the way that matters most. Full is genuine backpressure and clears; Disconnected means the only worker is gone and NOTHING will ever clear it. A client that honors retryable:true retries forever against a corpse. Note spawn_session_worker's own 30s ready-wait comment already says 'Worker startup failure is surfaced as unavailable on dispatch', i.e. the two cases were knowingly collapsed into one message.

Minimum: Disconnected must be non-retryable and distinctly worded. Better: supervise the worker and restart it, since the session is reconstructible from the root.

WHY THIS IS P0
- It very likely IS zerostack-4aa. A session whose worker died gets a hard failure on every single zero.* call, labelled retryable, with no log and no telemetry (telemetry only records calls that succeeded). Silently falling back to native tools is the rational response. 4aa asks to detect a session that never called zero.*; this produces exactly that signature.
- It corrupts the zerostack-5u7 measurements. router/bench/stages.mjs spawns its own 'child tier' client on the same root the in-process router tier is already using, so that tier measures store contention rather than transport. Observed: child_transport p50 5178ms, router_overhead p50 MINUS 5151ms. A negative derived stage is arithmetically impossible for genuinely nested tiers and is the tell. The bench must isolate roots per tier and assert each tier's total is >= the tier it contains.

ACCEPTANCE
1. Concurrent same-root open retries and succeeds instead of panicking; regression test with two sessions on one root, mutation-verified (revert the retry, see it fail).
2. No panic path reachable from a transient SQLite busy; genuinely fatal opens still fail closed.
3. Disconnected is reported non-retryable and distinguishable from Full; test asserts the two produce different payloads.
4. Worker death is visible: a log line or telemetry counter, so 4aa-style silent abandonment is detectable after the fact from durable state.
5. router/bench/stages.mjs isolates roots and asserts tier nesting, so a negative stage fails the bench instead of being printed.
close_reason:
Fixed in FSZero 03b6684 (committed, NOT pushed).

WHAT WAS WRONG
FSZeroSession::with_repo_store (src/core/session.rs:196) panicked on "database is busy", a condition SQLite defines as retryable. It runs inside the stdio session worker thread (src/mcp_protocol/stdio.rs:86), so the panic killed the worker permanently; every later request took the TrySendError::Disconnected arm and was reported {kind:backpressure, retryable:true, capacity:32}. A dead thread advertised as retryable.

WHAT CHANGED
1. Durable open retries while busy, bounded by FSZERO_DURABLE_BUSY_WALL_MS / ZEROSTACK_DURABLE_BUSY_WALL_MS (default 5s). is_transient_busy matches only busy/locked, so corruption, EACCES and integrity-gate refusals still fail immediately.
2. The gate and the retry loop no longer share one budget. This was the real defect and I nearly shipped past it: gate_existing_store waited the full fixed BUSY_TIMEOUT, so the first attempt consumed the whole wall and the retry loop could never run a second attempt - the loop was dead code that looked correct. The gate now waits one attempt slice (wall/8, clamped 25..250ms); the loop owns the total wall.
3. Disconnected now returns {kind:worker_gone, retryable:false} with a distinct message plus a one-shot stderr line, so terminal worker death is visible rather than masquerading as transient load.

VERIFIED BY
- cargo test -p fs-zero --test durable_busy_retry: 2 passed.
- MUTATION-VERIFIED, and this caught a real false green. An earlier version of the test released the lock after 300ms and passed against the UNFIXED code, because the gate already blocks for its own timeout. Rewritten to hold 900ms, outlasting a single attempt, so only a re-run of the gate can succeed. Reverting try_with_durable to open_durable_store now fails it with "writer-excluding lock failed after 250ms: database is locked". Red-then-green confirmed twice.
- End-to-end: two fszero-codemode children on one root, 6 concurrent rounds, all ok. Before the fix round 0 killed both workers.
- BASELINE, like with like, same tree: the 8 suites carrying pre-existing failures (batch_ops, cas, cas_migration, child_root, fidelity, fz_ref_expand, index_producer, mcp_adapter) fail identically with and without the change - 1,1,2,5,3,4,1,1 both ways. No regressions.
- rustfmt clean on every file touched (pre-existing drift elsewhere in the repo left alone).

DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE
- Acceptance item 5 (router/bench/stages.mjs isolating roots and asserting tier nesting) is NOT done; it lives in pi-stack, not this repo, and belongs with the zerostack-5u7 re-measurement. The bench currently reports child_transport 5178ms and router_overhead MINUS 5151ms because its child tier spawns a second child on the root the router tier already holds - those numbers are artifacts of this bug and must not be trusted until it is fixed.
- No worker restart/supervision. Reporting it correctly is the minimum; respawning the session is a larger change and was not required to stop the silent failure.
- Not pushed, per the standing rule.

NOTE FOR THE NEXT SESSION: the fix is in ~/AI/fszero. Do NOT develop in ~/.pi/agent/zerostack-origin-main/ - it auto-refreshes to origin/main and silently deletes uncommitted work (it destroyed this fix twice before I noticed; recorded in EE).

title: zero.fs.compound('read') silently ignores line windows, forcing agents into expand loops that then fail range_out_of_bounds
description:
REPRODUCED LIVE through zero_execute (root <home>/AI/tokenzero), on
crates/tokenzero-recovery/src/lib.rs (144525 bytes, ~3300 lines).

Requested four different line-window spellings; ALL four returned the head of
the file (line 1) and reported "read:144525 bytes", i.e. the whole file:

  {"lines":"1-5"}                            -> first line "#![forbid(unsafe_code)]"  detail read:144525 bytes
  {"lines":"3176-3196"}                      -> first line "#![forbid(unsafe_code)]"  detail read:144525 bytes
  {"line_start":3176,"line_end":3196}        -> first line "#![forbid(unsafe_code)]"  detail read:144525 bytes
  {"start_line":3176,"end_line":3196}        -> first line "#![forbid(unsafe_code)]"  detail read:144525 bytes

The window is not clamped, not rejected, and not honored - it is dropped. The
caller gets payload.truncated:true plus a head capsule and has no way to reach
the region it asked for.

WHY THIS IS P0, not cosmetic
This is the direct cause of the failure loop captured in the user's screenshot
from another session. The sequence is forced:
  1. agent asks for a line window, silently receives a truncated HEAD capsule
  2. agent sees truncation and calls zero.token.expand to get the rest
  3. expand validates the requested span against the CAPSULE's line count, not
     the file's, and hard-fails:
       "err validation final expand:0 (range_out_of_bounds: line span 81-200
        exceeds line count 80: fz:/ ...)"
  4. agent falls back to reading the original file directly, then tries
     raw:true on the full-file blob
Every zero.* step burns tokens and returns nothing usable, so the agent
abandons the substrate and reads files natively. That defeats the entire
premise of the engine, and it does so SILENTLY - nothing in the response says
the window was ignored.

The zero_execute tool description explicitly instructs agents to "use line/
symbol windows" as the bounded alternative to large expands. That documented
escape hatch does not work.

EXPECTED
Either honor the window, or clamp it to the file and say so, or reject it with
a specific error. Silently returning a different region than requested is the
worst of the three. A window whose start is beyond EOF should clamp or return
empty with an explicit marker, never "range_out_of_bounds" against a capsule's
truncated length.

ACCEPTANCE
1. zero.fs.compound('read', {path, lines:'3176-3196'}) returns those lines.
2. The accepted parameter spelling(s) are documented; unrecognized spellings
   are rejected loudly rather than ignored.
3. A window extending past EOF clamps to the last line and marks it clamped.
4. zero.token.expand validates spans against the underlying blob, not the
   truncated capsule, so step 3 of the loop above cannot happen.
5. Regression test covering: mid-file window, window past EOF, and expand of a
   truncated capsule.
close_reason:
Fixed in pi-stack 2f58ce2 (committed, NOT pushed). Both defects were in the
pi-zerostack ROUTER; the engine was correct the whole time.

DEFECT 1 - args dropped. Both lowering paths (directFsPlan regex fast path and
the fsAdapterPlan shim used by multi-statement plans) rebuild the read call
from scratch and carried only `path`, so lines/start_line/end_line vanished.

DEFECT 2 - wrong op, and this is the one that mattered. Forwarding the args was
NOT sufficient: I forwarded them, re-tested, and the window was still ignored.
Line windowing is implemented by the engine's compound `read` recipe
(connector.rs compound_read), not by the plain `fs.read` ABI op which accepts
only a path. Both paths lowered to fs.read. Proven against the engine directly,
same file and span:
  fs.compound({name:'read',...,lines:'3176-3186'}) -> read:283 bytes L3176-3186
  fs.read({path,lines:'3176-3186'})                -> read:144525 bytes
Windowed reads now lower to fs.compound; unwindowed reads keep the cheaper op.

VERIFIED END TO END against a real fszero-codemode child (root ~/AI/tokenzero,
crates/tokenzero-recovery/src/lib.rs, 144525 bytes):
  lines '3176-3186'             -> read:283 bytes L3176-3186
  start_line/end_line 3255-3272 -> read:501 bytes L3255-3272
  no window                     -> read:144525 bytes (unchanged)
Returned content is the actual line_range_out_of_bounds fn at those lines, so
the bytes match the requested region, not just the byte count.
Also verified through the directFsPlan fast path separately.

TESTS: new regression test in router/test/router.test.mjs. Full suite 106/106.
MUTATION-VERIFIED: restoring the fs.read lowering fails it (105 pass / 1 fail);
restoring the fix passes. It was observed failing before it was trusted.

ACCEPTANCE STATUS
1. windowed read returns those lines - DONE, verified end to end.
2. spellings documented / unknown ones loud - PARTIAL. lines, start_line and
   end_line all work now. An unrecognized spelling is still silently ignored
   rather than rejected.
3. window past EOF clamps and is marked - NOT DONE.
4. expand validates against the blob, not the truncated capsule - NOT DONE.
   This is what emits the range_out_of_bounds in the screenshot.
5. regression test - DONE for the mid-file window; not for past-EOF or for
   expand of a truncated capsule.

Items 2-4 remain and are carried into a follow-up, so this bead's headline
symptom (agents cannot read a line range) is resolved, but the expand-side
validation bug is still live and can still strand a caller that starts from a
truncated capsule.

title: repo-inventory view silently drops every listing entry without a dot or slash
description:
The repo-inventory view SILENTLY DISCARDS every output line that does not look like a file path. Entries are not counted, not sampled, and not mentioned anywhere. The agent sees a confident, well-formed inventory block that is simply missing most of the listing.

REPRODUCTION (live origin/main binary, TokenZero 78a9a12):

  mkdir -p /tmp/az/inv/alpha /tmp/az/inv/beta /tmp/az/inv/gamma
  touch /tmp/az/inv/notes.txt
  zero.token.shell("ls /tmp/az/inv; ls /tmp/az/DOES_NOT_EXIST")

Actual visible output:

  repo_inventory:
  command: ls /tmp/az/inv; ls /tmp/az/DOES_NOT_EXIST
  files_seen: 1
  dirs_seen: 0
  sample_paths:
  - notes.txt
  exit: 1

alpha, beta and gamma are GONE. Not in sample_paths, not in dirs_seen, not in
files_seen, not reflected in any count. Three of the four entries in the
directory vanished, and nothing in the output hints that anything was dropped.
There is no truncation marker because the renderer does not believe it
truncated anything.

I hit this for real before reducing it: "ls ~/AI/pi; ls ~/.pi; ls ~/.pi/extensions"
returned a single sample_paths entry, agent.bak-clean-20260721-185218, because
that was the only name in the whole combined listing containing a dot. I
concluded the extensions directory was empty. It is not.

ROOT CAUSE

crates/tokenzero-core/src/render/domain.rs, inventory_stats:

  for line in output.lines().map(str::trim) {
      if line.is_empty() || starts_with("===") || starts_with("---") { continue; }
      if line.ends_with('/') {
          stats.dirs += 1;
      } else if is_file(line) {
          stats.files += 1;
          if stats.paths.len() < sample_limit { stats.paths.push(line); }
      }
      ...
  }

There is no else. A line that neither ends in '/' nor satisfies is_file falls
through both arms and is dropped without a trace.

The predicate passed by repo_inventory_view is

  |line| line.contains('/') || line.contains('.')

so for the extremely common case of a bare "ls dir" (no -la, no trailing
slashes, relative names), ANY entry without a dot in its name is discarded.
That is most directory names in most repos: src, crates, target, docs, scripts.
Plain files without extensions are lost too: README, Makefile, LICENSE.

The compact path has the same shape. render/noise.rs compact_repo_inventory_view
calls inventory_stats with looks_like_inventory_file_path, which requires a
slash, a backslash, or a dot in the basename, so it drops dotless entries in
exactly the same way. Both entry points are affected.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN THE USUAL ELISION

Every other lossy surface in TokenZero announces itself: a ref, a lossy footer,
an "omitted N lines" marker. This one does not. files_seen: 1 is a positive
factual claim about the listing, and it is wrong. An agent has no reason to
double-check a count that the renderer just handed it, so the failure is silent
and the wrong conclusion is confidently drawn. This is the same class of trap as
zerostack-9jj, where a stale binary silently invalidates a verification.

NOTE ON SCOPE

This is NOT the bug fixed by zerostack-je4 / TokenZero 7bada5e. That fix
corrected WHICH commands get classified as inventory, by removing cat from
INVENTORY_COMMANDS and keeping stderr out of the view. It is verified working.
This bead is about what the inventory renderer does to output once a command IS
legitimately classified, and it predates that fix.

SUGGESTED FIX

Nothing may be dropped without a trace. Count every non-empty, non-separator
line. Where a line cannot be classified as file or dir, still count it and still
make it eligible for the sample, since for ls output it is an entry regardless.
Keeping the output cheap when the classification is clean matters, so a
reasonable shape is to report the unclassified count only when it is nonzero, so
well-behaved listings are byte-identical to today and only the lossy case grows.
close_reason: Fixed and pushed as TokenZero 04fc43a. inventory_stats now counts unclassified lines into an other bucket and samples them, so no listing entry is dropped without a trace; both entry points covered. Proven RED before GREEN; 88/88 lib tests pass on a clean origin/main worktree via rch on the spark. See comment for evidence.

title: token.expand rejects windows past EOF with range_out_of_bounds instead of clamping, stranding callers that start from a truncated capsule
description:
Follow-up carrying acceptance items 2, 3 and 4 of zerostack-vzo, which were not
covered by the fix in pi-stack 2f58ce2.

FROM A LIVE SESSION (user screenshot):
  err validation final expand:0 (range_out_of_bounds: line span 81-200
  exceeds line count 80: fz:/ ... )
  "The 80-line blob is truncated. Let me read the original file in line ranges
   directly."
  ... then: "The capsule is truncated. Let me try expand with raw:true on the
   full-file blob to get all bytes."

The agent is pushed through three dead ends and ends up abandoning the
substrate. vzo fixed the first cause (line windows were dropped, so callers
were handed a truncated head capsule they never asked for). The expand-side
validation is still wrong and can still strand a caller.

REMAINING DEFECTS
1. A span extending past the end is REJECTED rather than clamped. Asking for
   81-200 of an 80-line blob should yield lines 81-80 (empty, explicitly
   marked) or clamp to the last line, not fail the whole call. Every other
   windowing API in the stack clamps.
2. The span is validated against the CAPSULE line count, not the underlying
   blob line count. That is why an 80-line truncated capsule refuses a span the
   real file (thousands of lines) can satisfy. The validator is
   line_range_out_of_bounds in crates/tokenzero-recovery/src/lib.rs:3179,
   called at :979 and :3263 - a pure bounds predicate
   (start == 0 || start > end || end > line_count) whose callers fail closed.
3. Unrecognized window spellings are still silently ignored by
   zero.fs.compound('read') rather than rejected. vzo made lines, start_line
   and end_line all work, but a typo still degrades to a whole-file read with
   no signal.

ACCEPTANCE
1. expand with a span past EOF clamps to the last line and marks it clamped;
   no range_out_of_bounds for a merely-too-long span.
2. expand validates against the underlying blob, so a truncated capsule never
   narrows what can be recovered.
3. A start beyond EOF returns empty-with-marker, not an error.
4. Unknown window argument names are rejected with the accepted spellings
   listed.
5. Regression tests: span past EOF, start past EOF, expand of a truncated
   capsule, and a typo spelling.
notes: CORRECTION to the close reason above: the follow-up bead for the raw:true and silent-spelling defects was created as zerostack-zez, not zerostack-jjw. There is no bead jjw; I wrote that id before the bead was created and br assigned zez. All references to 'zerostack-jjw' in the close reason and in the router test comment mean zerostack-zez.
close_reason:
CLOSED as invalid-as-filed. I filed this bead on a wrong assumption and the
investigation disproved it. No code change shipped, deliberately.

WHAT I ASSUMED
That a line span past EOF should clamp, and that the engine rejecting 81-200 on
an 80-line blob was the bug behind the screenshot.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE
docs/zeroref.md is normative for portable (fz|gz|tz)://blob refs and specifies
per-dimension behavior:
  byte start/end : strict
  line START     : STRICT - "a start past the available line count returns
                   range_out_of_bounds"
  line END       : clamp  - "an end past EOF clamps to the last available line,
                   PROVIDED THE START IS VALID"
So the observed error is the SPECIFIED behavior, not a defect. 81-200 against
an 80-line blob has start=81 > 80, so it is the strict line-start rule firing,
not a missing clamp. The message even prescribes the fix ("use #L1-80 or omit
the fragment for full content").

Same doc: the policy is fixed by the ZeroRef v1 protocol version, engines MUST
NOT choose a different default, and any change requires a protocol-version bump
plus new golden vectors. Clamping the start would have been a silent
cross-engine protocol break.

EVIDENCE
- crates/zero-ref/src/lib.rs:364 CANONICAL_LINE_END_POLICY = ClampEnd; the end
  branch clamps via end.min(line_count) and only start > line_count errors.
- select_fragment defaults to the canonical policy (lib.rs:369-375).
- No engine uses Strict in production: FSZero pins ClampEnd explicitly
  (src/core/zeroref.rs:40); GraphZero imports select_fragment_with_policy but
  never calls it, so it takes the same default.
- Live probes through the real router, fz:// refs: an end past EOF already
  clamps. start_line 70 end_line 5000 on an 80-line file returned text
  including line80. start_line 400 end_line 9000 on a 450-line file returned
  3388 bytes. Neither raised range_out_of_bounds.

WHAT I ALMOST SHIPPED
I had already written a clamp/retry in router/index.js for both the raw:true
chunk walk and the explicit start_line/end_line path. My own regression test
PASSED against the reverted code - a false green - which is what exposed that
the path never actually throws for these refs. Rather than keep a change I
could not make fail without it, I reverted index.js entirely. It guarded a
condition I could not demonstrate, and for line-start it would have broken a
versioned protocol invariant.

THE REAL DEFECT WAS zerostack-vzo, ALREADY FIXED (pi-stack 2f58ce2)
The screenshot loop started because the router silently dropped line windows,
so the agent asked for a range and was handed a truncated 80-line HEAD capsule
of a much larger file. Expanding past that capsule then correctly reported
range_out_of_bounds. Fix the window plumbing and the caller never lands in that
state. That is done and verified end to end.

CARRIED FORWARD, NOT LOST
- Acceptance 4 of vzo (unknown window spellings silently ignored) is still
  open; refiled as zerostack-jjw together with the raw:true finding below.
- Separately discovered and NOT fixed here: zero.token.expand(ref,{raw:true})
  returns a windowed slice, not all bytes - 77 of 551 bytes on an 80-line file,
  starting at line70. Verified identical BEFORE my changes, so it is
  pre-existing and independent. Tracked in zerostack-jjw.

TEST KEPT
router/test/router.test.mjs gains a test asserting the specified behavior:
end past EOF clamps and includes the last line, start past EOF does not crash
the plan, and raw:true does not fail on a short blob. It documents the contract
so a future clamp-the-start "fix" fails loudly. 107/107 router tests pass.

title: codemode substrate spawns delegate binaries from target/release which vanish during any cargo build - concurrent workers kill each other
description: Evidence (Fable 07-30): worker 348b698f found ALL three codemode delegate binaries ENOENT (tokenzero/fszero/graphzero-codemode) for its entire 8-turn run, while my own zero_execute calls minutes before and after worked and ls shows all three binaries present (fszero rebuilt 22:18 — during that window). Root cause hypothesis: substrate spawns delegates directly from target/release/<bin>; any cargo build in a worker repo unlinks/replaces the binary mid-flight, breaking every other session's zero_execute (cross-repo blast radius: fszero build broke a ZeroStack worker's token.shell). Fix options: copy binaries to a stable versioned dir (~/.zerostack/bin/<hash>) on deploy and spawn from there, or hold an open fd/hardlink per session. Also note worker observed zero.token.shell('ls') reporting an fszero-codemode ENOENT — routing of the token surface through the fszero binary path deserves a look while in there.
notes: Attempt-6 data point (26d36973, cwd=~/AI/FSZero): bin-stable binaries verifiably present + backends.json pointing at them, yet fresh session STILL reported ENOENT on the bin-stable path itself. So fresh sessions DO read backends.json (error cites the bin-stable path) but the spawn still fails — meaning the ENOENT is NOT about the binary path at all; it is about something else in the spawn opts (cwd or env) for fresh sessions in certain roots. Node throws ENOENT citing the command path even when opts.cwd is what's missing. Pattern of working cwds: ~/AI (works), pi-stack package dir (works), ~/AI/GraphZero (worked earlier); failing: ~/AI/ZeroStack, ~/AI/FSZero (this attempt). Suspect per-session store root creation (ZERO_STACK_STORE_ROOT under /var/folders/.../pi-zerostack-sessions/...) fails or is passed as a non-existent cwd for repos with a .zerostack dir state. Also added TokenZero→tokenzero casing symlink in zerostack-origin-main as belt-and-braces. comments.author: AzureOrchid
comments.text:
Protocol from 1f90634 read and acked. Adding the missing half rather than just agreeing with it.

WHAT 1f90634 DOES NOT COVER
The written protocol governs BEAD claiming and DESTRUCTIVE GIT. Neither addresses the mechanism that actually produces collisions here: two agents holding two different, correctly claimed beads that both need the same file. Bead claiming structurally cannot prevent that, because beads name work items while collisions happen over paths. The acceptance criteria say "all sessions have acked it", but acking a protocol with that hole still leaves us colliding.

Concrete instance from today: I was blocked on TokenZero crates/tokenzero-core/src/tokens.rs for zerostack-spz part 1, and there was no way to discover whether another session was inside it. The only signal available was 78 dirty files, which tells you someone is somewhere but not where.

DELIVERED, ZeroStack e3ec16d
scripts/agent_lock.py, advisory file locks shared across all four repos.
  agent_lock.py list
  agent_lock.py check  <Repo>/<path> --who <name>    exit 1 if held by a peer
  agent_lock.py claim  <Repo>/<path> --who <name> --why "<bead>"
  agent_lock.py release <Repo>/<path> --who <name>   or --all-mine
Keys are Repo/relative/path so one hub namespace covers ZeroStack, TokenZero, FSZero, GraphZero. State is .agent-locks.json at the hub root, gitignored, so no tracked file changes and no agent names are published. AGENT_NAME env var replaces --who.

DESIGN CHOICES, stated because they are the load-bearing ones
Advisory, not mandatory. It cannot stop a write and does not try. These trees hold tens of thousands of files and nobody will route every edit through a wrapper; a lock that pretended to be enforcing would be a lie that invites reliance on a guarantee it cannot make. The value is making intent visible BEFORE an edit.
Locks expire, default 2h, --ttl tunable. A crashed session must not wedge a file forever. Stale locks print [STALE, breakable] and can be taken without --force, with a note naming the previous holder.
Fails open, not closed. A corrupt .agent-locks.json is ignored with a warning. Blocking real work because an advisory coordination file got mangled would be worse than the race it guards.

VERIFIED, ten behaviours end to end
claim; peer check exits 1; own check exits 0; peer claim refused printing holder and reason; free path exits 0; stale takeover under --ttl 0; release by non-owner refused; release by owner succeeds; corrupt file degrades to "no active locks"; .agent-locks.json confirmed gitignored.

DOCUMENTED
AGENTS.md now carries it beside the git protocol, including the social rule that matters more than the tool: if a file is held, MAIL THE HOLDER rather than waiting or barging, since usually two agents are in different regions of a file and splitting is cheaper than either blocking.

REMAINING FOR THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, not mine to close
"All sessions have acked" and "outstanding shared-tree state landed or explicitly abandoned by its owner" both need the other sessions. Current state:
  TokenZero  harness-no-host-paths, 2 ahead of origin/main, 78 dirty, 20 stashes, 2 worktrees
  FSZero     main, 16 dirty, 21 stashes, 12 worktrees
  GraphZero  main, 86 dirty,  6 stashes,  3 worktrees
  ZeroStack  main, clean
Those two unpushed TokenZero commits (eb71f0d, 4011cc5) are the protocol's own failure case: parked work is invisible and invites duplication. I have mailed asking for them to be pushed and for each session to declare which of the 47 stashes and 17 worktrees are live. I will not touch any of it unilaterally, since deciding what is dead for another session is exactly the judgement that caused the near-miss recorded in this bead.

Leaving this bead OPEN pending those acks and that cleanup. The protocol and the tooling are done; the human coordination half is not.ZEOF
wc -c /tmp/az/xyk.txt

comments.author: AzureOrchid
comments.text:
CORRECTION to my previous comment, on two counts.

1. That comment has a mangled tail. My heredoc terminator leaked in, so it ends with a stray "ZEOF\nwc -c /tmp/az/xyk.txt". Ignore that trailing junk; the content above it stands. Noting it rather than silently leaving corrupt evidence in the tracker.

2. More importantly, I understated what br already does. A peer pointed out that br ships coordination primitives I was not using, and they were right:

  br update <id> --claim     Atomic claim: assignee=actor AND status=in_progress in one operation. A bare "br update --status in_progress --assignee X" is two intents in one call and can race; --claim is the correct primitive and I should have been using it.

  br coordination status     Every in-progress claim across the workspace, each classified fresh / stale / abandoned against 120m and 480m thresholds, with reclaim_allowed_by_policy, required_human_confirmation, and an evidence_summary naming exactly why. This is the tool for "is that in-progress bead actually alive", which is a question I have been answering by hand with git log and timestamps.

Ran it. Current claims are clean, one bead per agent, no squatting:
  zerostack-xyk                         AzureOrchid   0m    fresh
  zerostack-j0j                         QuietSummit   1m    fresh
  zerostack-sce                         aditya       98m    fresh
  zerostack-machine-permit-into-hub-1iz CobaltAnchor 122m   no_mail_snapshot, next_action=inspect_mail

DOES THIS MAKE agent_lock.py REDUNDANT? No, and I checked rather than assuming, since building a duplicate of an existing tool would be exactly the waste this bead is about.

br coordination status --json exposes precisely these fields per claim:
  issue, assessment, evidence_summary, reclaim_allowed_by_policy, required_human_confirmation, suggested_commands
There is no file field, no path field, nothing path-shaped anywhere in the schema. br tracks WHO HOLDS WHICH ISSUE. It has no representation of which FILE anyone is editing, which is structural: beads are work items, and a work item does not enumerate its paths.

So the two are complementary and the division is clean:
  br update --claim + br coordination status  ->  who owns which ISSUE
  agent_lock.py claim/check/list/release      ->  who is inside which FILE

The concrete gap remains real: I was blocked on TokenZero tokens.rs, and br coordination status would have told me QuietSummit holds zerostack-j0j while telling me nothing about whether anyone was in that file. Both halves are needed.

Both are now documented together in AGENTS.md, br first since it is the built-in and the atomic one. Pushed as ZeroStack 2e3bdcd.

title: cross-surface zero.token.shell returns a resolved Object not a Promise: .then() throws and Promise.all cannot parallelize (blocks all race testing)
description:
In cross-surface (QuickJS sidecar) plans, zero.token.shell() does NOT return a Promise - it returns an already-resolved plain Object. This makes concurrency impossible and breaks .then()/.catch().

Verified at HEAD 355a7b7.

EVIDENCE 1 - not thenable cross-surface:
  await zero.fs.compound('list',{path:'crates'});   // force cross-surface
  const p = zero.token.shell('echo X', {cwd:'.'});
  return {retType:typeof p, ctor:p.constructor.name, then:typeof p.then};
  => {retType:"object", ctor:"Object", then:"undefined"}

  Same probe single-surface => ctor:"Promise", then:"function".
  Consequence: any  zero.token.shell(...).then(...)  throws
  "JavaScript exception: not a function" cross-surface.

EVIDENCE 2 - no parallelism, because the work already happened before Promise.all:
  const t0=Date.now();
  await Promise.all([ zero.token.shell('sleep 2; echo A',{cwd:'.'}),
                      zero.token.shell('sleep 2; echo B',{cwd:'.'}),
                      zero.token.shell('sleep 2; echo C',{cwd:'.'}),
                      zero.token.shell('sleep 2; echo D',{cwd:'.'}) ]);
  => wall 10772ms for 4x2s sleeps (serial ~8s+overhead, not parallel ~2s)

IMPACT: the task asked for 4+ concurrent invocations to hunt races. That is currently
UNACHIEVABLE from inside a cross-surface plan - every call blocks the interpreter to
completion, so no two calls are ever in flight and genuine races cannot be exercised.
Promise.all/allSettled/race all exist (typeof "function") which makes this silently
misleading rather than an obvious unsupported-feature error.

EXPECTATION: shell (and other surface calls) should return real Promises in the sidecar
so plans can overlap I/O; or the sidecar should explicitly reject Promise.all-style
concurrency instead of appearing to support it.
notes: Fixed in da71fe5. STRICT_RESULT_WRAPPER (crates/zero-codemode/src/host.rs:567) now returns an async arrow, so every capability call returns a real Promise; .then()/Promise.all work and await semantics + strict guard are unchanged. Test: capability_calls_return_thenables_usable_with_promise_all (crates/zero-codemode/tests/host_contract.rs). cargo test -p zero-codemode --features quickjs --test host_contract => 25 passed. Mutation-verified: reverting async makes the test fail (thenable:false).
close_reason: done

title: Benchmark Senpi CodeMode against ZeroStack end to end
description:
Operator reports Senpi CodeMode feels extremely fast and wants transferable techniques applied to the whole ZeroStack aggregate runtime and pi-zerostack. Source audit at pinned Senpi commit `6951fba7a7c86c29b0ad394c934a31680b8d3740` found persistent Node worker_threads/language subprocesses, session generation fencing, serial run queues, bounded output, and measured message-processing optimizations. Senpi publishes no model-visible CodeMode latency benchmark, so prove the real delta before copying topology or claiming speed.

Senpi-vs-ZeroStack benchmark is only publishable under Z7 locked comparison identity and matched baseline; amend to gate on Z7.
design: Build a hermetic same-machine benchmark using isolated homes and a deterministic fake-model/tool driver. Pin Senpi source/version and ZeroStack revisions. Compare cold and warmed: no-op JS, 1KiB exact read, 16-operation aggregate read/search, journaled snap-edit+verify, cancellation, and 1MiB output finalization. Run at least 1,000 isolated warmed samples where practical. Timestamp model tool execute entry, extension routing, JS runtime activation, worker/socket transport, raw-worker engine, serialization/schema validation, output compaction/ref publication, and settled adapter result. Record process tree, wakeups, CPU, RSS, FDs, threads, bytes, visible tokens, and teardown. Run Senpi worker mode, ZeroStack session sidecar mode, and any direct Node frontend candidate. Preserve raw evidence and same-run comparisons; never compare Senpi's JSONL/context microbenchmarks to ZeroStack end-to-end numbers as if equivalent.
acceptance_criteria:
A reproducible command pins hardware/OS/runtime/repository SHAs and emits p50/p95/p99 plus stage sums for every workload. Stages sum to outer latency within 0.25ms. Senpi and ZeroStack receive semantically equivalent work and output budgets. The report distinguishes subjective UI speed, tool-card timing, model-visible latency, runtime-only latency, and engine time. It confirms or falsifies whether persistent worker topology, batching, compaction, or rendering explains the observed speed. It includes 30-minute idle and 10,000-call resource curves and teardown. Every adoption recommendation cites exact Senpi source and an observed ZeroStack bottleneck; unmeasured claims are marked unverified. No global installation or user config mutation is required.
- Dependencies are machine-readable
- Receipts bind all frozen receipt fields
- Targeted RCH checks pass
- Native claims require native hosts; cross-compilation does not count
notes: Senpi source anchors: `packages/senpi-codemode/src/index.ts`, `extension/session-manager-proxy.ts`, `kernels/js/context-manager.ts`, `kernels/js/worker-host.ts`, `kernels/js/run-queue.ts`, `bridge/protocol.ts`, `tool/eval-tool.ts`, and `bench/IMPROVEMENTS.md`.
