title: expand raw:true returns a windowed slice instead of all bytes; unknown line-window spellings silently ignored
description:
Two independent defects found while working zerostack-vzo and zerostack-x40.
Both are PRE-EXISTING and were verified against unmodified code.

DEFECT 1 - zero.token.expand(ref, {raw: true}) does not return all bytes.

raw:true is documented as the escape hatch for "exact byte recovery", and the
zero_execute tool description tells agents to use {raw:true} when they need
exact bytes. It returns a windowed slice instead.

Measured through the real router on an 80-line, 551-byte file:
  zero.fs.compound('read', {path:'short.txt'})   -> ref
  zero.token.expand(ref, {raw:true})             -> 77 bytes, starting at line70

77 of 551 bytes, and it does not even start at line 1. The read emits a ref
that already carries a line window, and the raw path honors that window rather
than expanding to the whole object.

Verified pre-existing: identical result (77 bytes, line70) with the working
tree reverted, so this is not fallout from the vzo fix.

Impact: an agent that correctly follows the documented advice to use raw:true
for exact bytes silently receives a fraction of the file with no truncation
marker. Silent partial data is worse than an error, because nothing downstream
can tell that bytes are missing.

DEFECT 2 - unrecognized line-window spellings are silently ignored.
(This is acceptance item 4 of zerostack-vzo, which was not covered by the fix
in pi-stack 2f58ce2.)

vzo made lines, start_line and end_line all work. A typo or any other spelling
still degrades to a full-file read with no signal, which is the same class of
failure vzo was filed for: the caller believes it asked for a window and is
handed something else. The router rebuilds the read args explicitly, so any key
it does not recognize is dropped on the floor.

ACCEPTANCE
1. expand(ref, {raw:true}) returns the complete object bytes regardless of any
   window carried by the ref, or fails loudly if it cannot.
2. A regression test asserts raw:true byte-exactness against a file larger than
   one 200-line chunk AND one smaller than a chunk (the 80-line case above).
3. Unknown window argument names on zero.fs.compound('read') are rejected with
   the accepted spellings listed, rather than silently widening to a full read.
4. A regression test asserts the rejection.
close_reason:
PARTIALLY FIXED BY ME; acceptance 1 was ALREADY FIXED before this session.
Recording the split honestly rather than claiming both.

DEFECT 2 (unknown line-window spellings silently ignored) -- FIXED by me in
pi-stack 0587fb0. The router's fast paths rebuild the read call from scratch, so
any key they did not recognize was dropped on the floor and the read silently
widened to the whole file. Window-shaped arguments are now REJECTED with the
accepted spellings named (lines, start_line, end_line, line_start, line_end).
A rejection the caller cannot act on would only trade a silent failure for a
dead end, so the error names what to use instead.
  Same commit also fixed line_start/line_end being accepted and then ignored
  (that is b4yg bug 2 -- the two beads were indeed the same root cause in the
  same code, as this bead predicted).

DEFECT 1 (expand raw:true returns a windowed slice) -- NOT fixed by me; it no
longer reproduces. Evidence for that claim, not assertion:
  - Ran the bead's EXACT fixture (80 lines spelled line1..line80 = 551 bytes,
    the file the bead measured at 77 bytes starting at line70) through the real
    router. Result: 551 bytes starting at line1, ending line80. Correct.
  - Re-ran the same check against the PRE-CHANGE router (HEAD~1) with the same
    engine: raw:true still returned all 551 bytes from line1. So it passed
    before my change too.
  - Confirmed by diff: my commit does not touch the raw:true path at all
    (git diff HEAD~1 -- router/ shows no change to refs.js, where
    ["expand","--raw",ref] is built). I cannot take credit for it.
  Most likely already resolved by the earlier pi-stack line-window work
  (2f58ce2 / 3190f6d) cited in this bead's own text.

ACCEPTANCE, verified through the real router against the patched engine:
1. raw:true returns complete object bytes -- PASS (551/551 from line1 on the
   bead's own fixture. Not my fix; verified not-regressed.
2. Regression test asserting raw:true byte-exactness on a file LARGER than one
   200-line chunk AND one smaller -- PASS both: 80-line/2471B and
   900-line/60192B files, byte-exact, plus the bead's 551B case. 9/9 acceptance
   checks green.
3. (from the defect-2 half) unknown spelling rejected -- PASS, mutation-verified:
   removing the rejection reds that check and only that check; restoring returns
   9/9.

Permanent guards: router/test/read-contract.test.mjs, 11 tests, each
mutation-verified red-then-green. npm test 182/182, 0 failures (baseline 171).

LEFT ALONE: not pushed (goal doc says do not push without explicit request).
EOF
)
